                                                                                                                        §100 Contract

 1

 2   §100                                                                                                                 CONTRACT

 3   1.     Term of Contract

 4          This contract is made and entered into by and between the Cincinnati Board of Education (“Board”) and the Cincinnati
 5          Federation of Teachers Local 1520 AFT, OFT, AFL–CIO (“Federation”) and shall be binding and effective from
 6          January 1, 2007 through December 31, 2009.

 7   2.     Contract Implementation

 8          The Board and Federation shall jointly plan and implement training in regard to contract implementation.

 9          Training shall cover the entire contract with emphasis on all new or amended provisions, grievance and other appeal
10          procedures, and discipline provisions. Such training shall begin with the 2007-2008 school year and continue during the
11          term of the contract. Participants shall include, at a minimum, Federation Building Representatives, Executive Council,
12          and staff; principals and appropriate central office administrators and any personnel involved in grievance administration.

13          The parties shall also conduct a briefing for community leaders on new provisions of the contract and any other
14          provisions in which there is interest.
15   §110                                                                                                             RECOGNITION

16   1.     Sole and Exclusive Bargaining Agent

17          The Board recognizes the Federation as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for the purpose of bargaining wages,
18          hours, benefits and all other terms and conditions of employment for all teachers in the bargaining unit, including
19          classroom teachers, certificated night-school teachers and summer school teachers who are also day-school classroom
20          teachers on an annual rate, librarians, school social workers, coordinating teachers, nurses, counselors, psychologists,
21          occupational therapists, physical therapists, audiologists, speech and language pathologists, and pre-school teachers, and
22          daily-rate substitutes; but excluding, other daily and hourly-rate teachers, lunchroom managers, administrative assistants,
23          directors, associate directors, associates, assistant principals, principals, personnel director, assistant superintendents,
24          deputy superintendents, and superintendents.

25          The Board recognizes the Federation as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for the purpose of bargaining wages,
26          hours, benefits and all other terms and conditions of employment for all teachers in the bargaining unit, including
27          classroom teachers, certificated night-school teachers and summer school teachers who are also day-school classroom
28          teachers on an annual rate, librarians, visiting teachers, coordinating teachers, nurses, counselors, psychologists, and pre-
29          school teachers, and daily-rate substitutes; but excluding, other daily and hourly-rate teachers, psychiatric social workers,
30          lunchroom managers, administrative assistants, directors, associate directors, associates, supervisors, associate
31          supervisors, assistant supervisors, assistant principals, principals, personnel director, assistant superintendents, deputy
32          superintendents, vice presidents, and superintendents.

33   2.     Rules Governing Recognition Election

34          Any effort by any other employee organization or members of the bargaining unit to replace or remove the Cincinnati
35          Federation of Teachers as the sole and exclusive bargaining agent for the bargaining unit described above in Paragraph 1
36          shall be governed solely by the provisions of O.R.C. §4117 and the rules concerning recognition elections adopted by the
37          State Employment Relations Board (SERB). In any election conducted by SERB, the election ground rules available
38          separately as an appendix shall apply where not in conflict with O.R.C. §4117 or SERB rules.

39   3.     No Recognition of Rival Organizations

40          The Board shall not recognize any other organization, which seeks the right to represent the employees in the bargaining
41          unit represented by the Federation during the term of this contract, nor shall the Board contribute to the growth or creation
42          of rival organizations.

43   4.     Information Available about Conditions of Employment

44          Information, statistics, and records relating to wages, hours, benefits, and all other terms and conditions of employment
45          reasonably necessary for the proper enforcement of the terms of this contract shall be made available to the Federation
46          upon request and upon payment by the Federation of any costs related thereto.
     1
     §120 Fair Practices                                                                                                          page
 1   5.     Receipt of Information Given to the Public

 2          The Federation shall receive the information which is to be given to the public on the Friday before the Board of
 3          Education meeting or as soon thereafter as it is available.

 4   6.     Availability of Public Information

 5          Public information referred to in the minutes but not distributed shall be made available to the Federation upon request at
 6          cost.
 7   §120                                                                                                         FAIR PRACTICES

 8   1.     By Board

 9          The Board agrees that no person(s), group(s), department(s) or division(s) responsible to the Board shall discriminate
10          against any employee on the basis of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, or membership in, lawful participation or
11          association with the lawful activities of the Federation.

12   2.     By Federation

13          The Federation agrees to represent all persons in the bargaining unit equally and fairly.
14   §130                                                                                                   FEDERATION RIGHTS

15   1.     Exclusive Organizational

16          a.     Orientation

17                 The Federation shall have the exclusive right to participate in the New Teacher Orientation, or similar summer
18                 inservice program, which may replace the New Teacher Orientation and shall have the opportunity to meet
19                 separately with new teachers. The Board shall consult with the Federation in planning the summer orientation
20                 program for new teachers.

21          b.     Federation Meetings

22                 The facilities requested by the Federation under §130 Paragraph (2a) shall not be denied, except where there is a
23                 previously announced and conflicting school activity.

24                 Upon notification of a chapter meeting, the principal shall not subsequently schedule any meeting or event to
25                 conflict with a Federation Chapter meeting.

26          c.     Office Bulletin Board

27                 The Federation shall have the exclusive right to use one-third (1/3) of the bulletin board located in the school
28                 office in nearest proximity to the teachers' mailboxes.

29          d.     Dues Deductions

30                 The Board shall deduct the uniform and periodic Federation dues from the paychecks of any teacher who
31                 voluntarily authorizes in writing that such deductions be made. Dues shall be deducted at one of two rates,
32                 representing either the full annual Federation dues or partial annual dues divided by the number of paychecks. The
33                 Board shall transmit dues deducted from the paychecks of employees to the Federation promptly following the
34                 delivery of paychecks to employees. The Board shall make every effort to transmit dues within five (5) days of
35                 paycheck delivery.

36                 Dues for substitutes shall be deducted at a daily rate. When a substitute changes from a daily rate to long-term
37                 substitute or long-term substitute to daily rate substitute, the appropriate adjustment shall be made by the Board in
38                 the rate of dues deduction.

39                 Teachers who desire to cancel Federation dues deduction shall obtain from the Federation a “cancellation of dues
40                 deduction” form, complete it and return it to the Federation. The Federation shall transmit the original of such
41                 cancellations promptly to the Board. Under no circumstances shall the Federation deny the right of any teacher to
42                 revoke an authorization of payroll deduction of union dues.
                                                                                                                                      2
                                                                                                            §130 Federation Rights
 1             The Board shall not be liable to the Federation for the remittance of payment of any sum other than that
 2             constituting actual deductions made from the wages of teachers. The Federation shall indemnify and hold the
 3             Board harmless against any and all claims, demands, suits or other forms of liability including, by way of example
 4             and not limitation, the cost of any judgment against the Board and the reasonable value of any attorney fees
 5             incurred, that may arise out of or by reason of action taken by the Board or not taken by the Board for the purpose
 6             of complying with any provision of this Section.

 7             The Board shall provide CFT, at no cost, promptly following the end of each payroll period, an alphabetical list of
 8             all employees who have authorized CFT dues deduction for the pay period and an alphabetical list of all
 9             employees from whose paychecks the Board has deducted fair share fees pursuant to Paragraph (e) below.
10             Following the end of each payroll period, the Board shall provide the Federation promptly a list of teachers added
11             to or deleted from dues deduction or fair share fee during that pay period. The Board shall make every effort to
12             transmit this information within five working days following the end of each payroll period.

13       e.    Fair Share Fee

14       (1)   As allowed by O.R.C. §4117.09 (C), all employees covered by this Agreement who are not members of the CFT
15             shall pay to the CFT, through deductions from each paycheck, their fair share of the costs of the collective
16             bargaining services rendered by the CFT that are properly chargeable to non-members under state and federal law,
17             as determined through the method described below (referred to hereafter as “fair share”). The obligation of non-
18             members to pay such fair share commences with the first paycheck due in September, or with the first paycheck
19             due sixty (60) days after initial employment in the bargaining unit, whichever occurs later.

20       (2)   Such fair share payment by non-members shall be deducted by the Board from the earnings of the non-member
21             employees and daily rate substitute teachers and remitted to the CFT, provided, however, that the CFT shall
22             submit to the Board at least 14 days prior to the first paycheck to teachers at the beginning of each school year an
23             affidavit which specifies the amount constituting said fair share not exceeding the dues uniformly required of
24             members of the CFT, and which describes the rationale and method by which the fair share was determined,
25             including a list of the expenditures which were excluded in determining the fair share. The CFT shall also certify
26             to the Board that a notice concerning the calculation of fair share payments by non-members has been published
27             for at least 14 days prior to the first paycheck to teachers at the beginning of each school year, pursuant to the CFT
28             “Non-member Fair Share Payments Implementation and Appeal Procedure”, a copy of which is attached to this
29             contract as Appendix B.

30             The Federation represents to the Board that it will establish a reduced fee for contract teachers and long-term
31             substitutes who work less than sixty percent of full time, consistent with the Federation’s per capita obligations to
32             its affiliates.

33       (3)   The CFT shall prepare a form of notice to employees by which non-member employees shall be informed of the
34             percentage and method of calculation of the fair share fee which shall include the report of an independent auditor
35             disclosing and verifying the major categories of expenses upon which the fee calculation shall be based. The
36             notice shall inform employees of their right to object to the calculation of the fair share fee and to submit an
37             objection to the fee to arbitration. Such right to object shall require the objector to send a letter to the CFT
38             President by regular U. S. mail or by delivery to the CFT office at any time after the notice, but within thirty (30)
39             days after the first salary payment of the school year from which his or her fair share fee has been deducted. The
40             notice to non-members shall set forth the address and telephone number of the CFT and the manner in which such
41             employee may obtain a copy of the CFT's internal appeal procedure.

42       (4)   Prior to the delivery of the first paycheck due to employees in September of each school year, the CFT shall
43             distribute the notice and appeal procedure described above by (1) posting them on the CFT bulletin board in each
44             building; (2) summarizing the notice and the internal appeal procedure in a CFT newspaper distributed to all
45             bargaining unit members in the first month of the school year; (3) providing Federation Building Representatives
46             with copies of the notice for distribution to employees identified as non-member employees of the Board pursuant
47             to Paragraph (a) above.

48       (5)   Upon the CFT's timely receipt of an objection under CFT's internal appeal procedure, the CFT shall deposit in an
49             escrow account separate from all other CFT funds, the amount of fee payments received on behalf of any
50             objector(s) that is fairly placed at issue by his or her objection, but not less than ten percent (10%) of the fair share
51             fee as verified by an independent auditor. Until such time as the report of the independent auditor is received by
52             the Board, if any objector files an objection with the Board as to the amount placed in escrow, the Board will
53             deposit the entire fair-share fee in the interest-bearing account referred to in this Article. The CFT shall furnish the
54             objectors and the Board with verification of the terms of the escrow arrangement, and, upon request, the status of
55             the fund as reported by the Bank.


     3
                                                                                                       §130 Federation Rights
 1          The escrow account will be established and maintained with a federally insured commercial bank with offices in
 2          Cincinnati, Ohio, and the Agreement therefore shall provide that the escrow accounts be interest bearing at the
 3          highest possible rate; that the escrowed funds be outside of the CFT's control until the final disposition as
 4          provided for herein; and that the escrowed funds will terminate and the funds therein be distributed only by the
 5          terms of an ultimate award, determination or judgment, including any appeals, or by the terms of a mutually
 6          agreed settlement between the CFT and any objector(s), or if the objector(s) abandons the objection.

 7   (6)    If an ultimate decision in any proceeding hereunder directs that the amount of the fair share fee should be lower
 8          than the amount fixed by the CFT, the CFT shall promptly adopt such determination and notify the Board to
 9          reduce deductions from the earnings of non-members to said prescribed amount. Such adjustment shall not entitle
10          any non-member who had not made a timely objection to a refund or rebate for past fair share fee payments.

11   (7)    As an express condition to the Board's agreement to grant a fair share fee arrangement to the CFT, the CFT shall
12          indemnify and hold harmless the Board, its members, officers, agents, and employees from and against any and all
13          claims, demands, actions, complaints, suits, refunds, rebates, or other forms of liability including attorney fees and
14          expenses paid or payable by the Board that shall arise by reason of action taken by the Board for the purpose of
15          complying with the provisions of this Article with respect to fair share fees, or in reliance on any list, notice,
16          certification, affidavit, or assignment furnished under any of such provisions by the CFT.

17                 The Federation's counsel shall be the lead counsel during any litigation concerning the fair share fee.

18   (8)    Nothing in this Article shall inhibit or interfere with the rights of any employees objecting to the payment of CFT
19          dues or fair share fees based on religious grounds. The rights of such members shall be resolved under the
20          provisions of Section 4117.09 (C) of the Ohio Revised Code, allowing for the contribution of an equivalent
21          amount to a charitable organization.

22   (9)    In order to continue to enjoy fair share fee, the Federation shall maintain a membership equal to 70% or more of
23          the bargaining unit as of the expiration of this contract.

24   (10)   The CFT represents to the Board and to the employees it represents that its “non-member fair share payments
25          implementation and appeal procedure” and its other practices and conduct in the course of implementing the fair
26          share fee arrangement conform to state and federal law.

27   f.     Other Voluntary Deductions

28          CFT COPE and other voluntary deductions listed in §700.3.n which have been voluntarily authorized in writing
29          by a teacher, shall be made upon receipt of the written authorization. The Board shall not establish for teachers,
30          deductions for other political funds or insurance coverage not currently in effect without the written agreement of
31          the Federation. This provision does not restrict the Board's right to change insurance carriers.

32          Regarding COPE deductions, the Board shall deduct from the amount transmitted to the Federation, $.04 per
33          deduction and $10.00 per transmittal.

34          Employees who desire to cancel CFT COPE deductions shall notify the Federation in writing. The Federation
35          shall transmit any such cancellations promptly to the Board. Under no circumstances shall the Federation deny the
36          right of employees to revoke the authorization of payroll deduction of CFT COPE contributions

37          The Board shall not be liable to the Federation for the remittance of payment of any sum other than that
38          constituting actual deductions made from the wages of teachers. The Federation shall indemnify and hold the
39          Board harmless against any and all claims, demands, suits or other forms of liability including, by way of example
40          and not limitation, the cost of any judgment against the Board and the reasonable value of any attorney fees
41          incurred, that may arise out of or by reason of action taken by the Board or not taken by the Board for the purpose
42          of complying with any provision

43   g.     Federation Leave

44          Upon written request of the Federation, the Federation President and up to three (3) others shall be assigned to the
45          Federation to conduct Federation business. Any employee so assigned shall be paid the full salary to which the
46          employee is entitled according to Appendix A, Schedule C, and shall include any extended time or supplemental
47          pay requested by the Federation, up to limits established by STRS and enjoy all increments, benefits and leaves as
48          other bargaining unit members, and shall continue to accrue seniority. The Federation shall reimburse the Board
49          for salary, medical, dental and term life benefits provided to such employees, retirement contributions paid on
50          their behalf, and any other expenses related to salary and fringe benefit costs. In addition, upon written request by
51          the Federation, this shall also be granted to any CFT member elected or hired for a full-time position with the
                                                                                                                                4
                                                                                                             §130 Federation Rights
 1               Federation’s state or national affiliates, and to part-time CFT employees who are compensated for work beyond
 2               the school day. Such employees shall be paid the full salary to which the employee is entitled according to
 3               Appendix A, Schedule C, shall enjoy all increments, benefits and leaves as other bargaining unit members, and
 4               shall continue to accrue seniority. The Federation shall reimburse the Board for salary, medical, dental and term
 5               life benefits provided to such employees, retirement contributions paid on their behalf, and any other expenses
 6               related to salary and fringe benefit costs. For an elected position, the request shall be honored indefinitely, if the
 7               Federation so desires. For a member hired for a position, the request shall be honored for up to four years, if the
 8               Federation so desires.

 9               If the Human Resources Office is notified by April 1 of a given school year that an employee assigned to the
10               Federation wishes to return to regular service the ensuing school year, such employees shall return to regular
11               service on the same basis as a teacher returning from a leave of absence longer than one school year.

12        h.     Printing of Contract

13               Upon ratification of this contract, the Federation and the Board’s designee shall meet to jointly approve the
14               wording of the final agreement and thereafter shall jointly submit the contract for printing. The Federation shall
15               have 7,000 copies of this contract printed, 2,000 of which shall be delivered to the Board. The Board and the
16               Federation shall agree on the format. The Board shall pay one-half (1/2) the cost of having the contract printed in
17               the union shop within the school district submitting the lowest of three bids obtained by the Federation. The
18               Federation shall distribute one (1) copy to each member of the bargaining unit. The Board shall provide new
19               employees with a copy upon employment.

20               The Board shall print at least 5,000 copies of the tentative agreement. The CFT shall pay one-half the cost of
21               printing the Tentative Agreement.

22        i.     Federation Pony Delivery

23               The building in which the Federation office is located shall be included as a regular stop on the school mail
24               delivery route.

25   2.   Non-Exclusive Organizational Rights

26        a.     Federation Chapter

27               The Federation chapter in each building shall have the right to transact Federation business on school property
28               before and after the teachers' regular school day.

29        b.     Board Meetings

30               The Federation President or designee shall have a seat and the right to speak at all public meetings of the Board of
31               Education and its subcommittees.

32        c.     Employee Relations/Federation President Meetings

33               The Superintendent’s designee for labor relations and the Federation President, or his/her designee, shall meet at
34               least monthly during the year to discuss current school problems and procedures of this contract. Additional
35               meetings shall be held upon request of either party.

36        d.     School Visitation

37        The Federation President, or his/her employee designee, shall have the right to visit the schools to investigate working
38        conditions, teacher complaints or problems, or for a purpose relating to the terms and conditions of employment, provided
39        there is no interruption of the school program and that the Federation representative announces his/her destination and
40        person(s) to be visited to the principal or to the person in charge if the principal is not immediately available. If possible,
41        visits should be announced by telephone before the visit. Representatives of rival organizations visiting a school or work
42        location shall be afforded only such privileges as are granted to any member of the public.

43        e.     Building Representation and Privileges

44               Every school or unit in the system shall have a Federation Building Representative from that building/unit who
45               shall be elected by the Federation.


     5
                                                                                                            §130 Federation Rights
 1          f.     Distribution of Materials

 2                 The Federation shall have the right to distribute bulletins and other pertinent materials through the inter-school
 3                 mail delivery system. The Board shall not accept for distribution through the inter-school mail system bulk
 4                 mailings, which are clearly identified as produced by a rival organization.

 5          g.     Posting Notices

 6                 Federation representatives shall have the responsibility for posting and removing Federation notices and no other
 7                 person shall do so.

 8          h.     Use of Mailboxes

 9                 The Federation shall have the right to distribute bulletins and other pertinent materials by placing them in the
10                 mailboxes of teachers and other professional employees.

11          i.     Use of Faculty Bulletin Boards

12                 The Federation shall have the right to use a portion of other existing faculty bulletin boards in addition to the
13                 bulletin board in the main office.

14          j.     Directory Information

15                 Board will annually, within 20 days of the first paycheck delivered to teachers in September, provide to CFT a list
16                 of bargaining unit members, including their work location, position classification, and home address. Teachers
17                 assigned to more than one school shall be listed at their “home school” (paycheck site).

18                 In addition, the Board shall provide the following information for each bargaining unit member as soon as such
19                 information is entered in Board computers: phone numbers (unless employee objects), seniority date, areas of
20                 certification, grade(s) and/or subject(s) taught, whether the teacher holds a supplemental contract under Appendix
21                 A, Schedule E. Any part of such information that has been entered in Board computers will be provided even if all
22                 of the information listed above is not available.

23          k.     New Employee Information

24                 The Board shall promptly provide the Federation with the names and addresses of new employees.

25          l.     Electronic Network

26                 The Federation shall be treated as a school site regarding technology networking. The Board shall provide the
27                 network connections to the Federation’s network server. In addition, data which is public information or required
28                 as part of this agreement, if available electronically, shall be made available to the Federation electronically.
29                 Board expenditures to provide such information shall be limited to the cost of maintaining the network connection
30                 to the CFT office using the same standards as for school offices.
31   §140                                                                                                      PERSONNEL FILES

32   1.     Access to Personnel Files

33          The official personnel file of each teacher shall be maintained by the Human Resources Office. The Board and CFT
34          recognize that certain Ohio laws govern access to records maintained by or on behalf of the Board. However, insofar as
35          they are acting in their capacity as employees or representatives of the Board, only the following may have access to
36          teacher personnel files: members of the Board of Education; attorneys of the Board needing access to personnel files; the
37          Superintendent and his/her designees who serve in an administrative or supervisory capacity in relation to the teacher, and
38          other Board employees conducting an evaluation or assessment of the teacher or considering the teacher for a position,
39          with the approval of the Director of Human Resources, or his/her designee; the teacher; and such other persons as the
40          teacher may authorize in writing.

41




                                                                                                                                     6
                                                                                                                §140 Personnel Files

 1   2.     Examining One's Own Personnel File
 2


 3          A teacher may examine his/her personnel file upon request. With respect to the official personnel file, the teacher shall
 4          schedule an appointment at least one (1) working day in advance with a representative of the Human Resources Office in
 5          whose presence the file shall be examined. Copies of any material in the personnel file shall be made available upon
 6          request and upon payment of the cost of copying. After 7 years, upon teacher request, all disciplinary infractions that
 7          have not re-occurred and do not create a legal exposure or liability for the Board shall be expunged by mutual agreement.

 8   3.     Notice of Material Placed in a File

 9          Upon receipt of any written communication (including a notation) involving accusations or derogatory statements against
10          a teacher, the Human Resources Office shall, before placing such material in the official personnel file, notify the teacher
11          of his/her right to dispute the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, or completeness of the communication (or notation).
12          Notification shall not be required when documents are addressed or copied to the teacher. The teacher's written response
13          must remain attached to the derogatory statements as long as the item is on file.

14   4.     Maintenance of Other Personnel Files

15          No other official personnel file concerning a teacher shall be maintained. However, letters, memoranda, copies of
16          documents which are in the official personnel file and other material concerning a teacher may be maintained in a
17          personnel file by the building/unit administrator.

18   5.     Notice of Material in Other Files

19          When a principal or other administrator finds it necessary to insert any written communication (including a notation) in a
20          teacher's personnel file maintained at the building/unit level which reflects adversely upon the teacher's conduct, service,
21          character, or personality, s/he shall afford the teacher an opportunity to read such communication. The teacher shall also
22          have the right to answer such communication and his/her answer shall be attached to the file copy.

23   6.     Use of Material in Personnel Files

24          Any written material withheld from the official personnel file and the personnel file maintained at the building/unit level,
25          and not otherwise known to the teacher, shall not be used as evidence in any action against the teacher. Should a teacher
26          dispute the contents of a written communication or notation in either personnel file referred to above, the Board shall
27          delete any information that it cannot verify or that it finds to be inaccurate.

28   7.     Notice of Citizen Examination of a Personnel File

29          Upon receipt of a citizen request for access to a teacher's personnel file under O.R.C. §149.43, the Human Resources
30          Office shall notify the teacher in writing, including the date of the request and the name of the person making the request.
31   §145                                                                           PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COMMUNITIES
32   CFT and the Board are both committed to improve student achievement by establishing Professional Learning Communities in
33   which all stakeholders take collective responsibility to ensure student learning by creating structures to promote a collaborative
34   educational culture focused on continuously improving results. The dominant model for PLCs is the team-based schools.
35


36   1.     Selection of Schools as Team-Based Schools
37            Team leaders will facilitate meetings and professional discourse that focus on the analysis of current school data. The
38            team leader will design and deliver professional development activities based on the data analysis.
39
40            Schools may continue to apply to be team-based through the EIP application process. The application process will
41            include a 2/3 secret ballot vote of the faculty and LSDMC approval. Existing Team-Based schools need not reapply.
42            EIP shall recommend schools to the Superintendent for conversion.
43


44          The School Redesign Team may convert schools in the Intervention or Redesign categories as team-based schools
45          pursuant to the School Accountability Plan.
46




     7
                                                                                                        §145 Team-Based Schools
 1        a.     LSDMC Composition

 2               The District shall ensure that, before a school applies or is selected to become team based, its LSDMC is
 3               constituted according to Board policy.

 4        b.     Evaluation

 5               The district will engage an outside, nationally known consultant after consultation with the EIP to conduct an
 6               annual evaluation of team-based schools.

 7   2.   Definition of Teams

 8        a.     Team Composition

 9               A team shall consist of three to five teachers sharing a common group of students. Four teachers on a team is the
10               preferred structure.

11               Primary and Intermediate Teams: Four teachers (three and five member teams are the exceptions)

12               Middle Team: For grades 7-8, a team must include teachers with middle grades or secondary certification in math
13               and science or 20 semester hours in those disciplines that would count towards secondary certification. Teams of
14               four or more shall also include teachers with middle grades or secondary certification in social studies and English
15               or 20 semester hours in those disciplines that would count towards secondary certification.

16               Grades 9-10: The team must include teachers certified in the core academic areas, i.e. math, science, English and
17               social studies and may include foreign language.

18               Grades 11-12: Teachers will generally not be assigned to teams.

19        b.     Team Leaders

20               Each teaching team (i.e. four or more teachers with a common group of students) shall have a paid team leader.
21               These positions shall first be offered to credentialed lead teachers through the lead teacher selection process. If no
22               lead teacher is selected, the team shall select a team leader for a two-year term with the approval of the principal.
23               The team leader shall be required to apply for lead teacher credentials during the next application period, if
24               eligible. At the end of the two-year term, the position shall again be posted as a lead teacher position and the
25               selection process above shall be repeated. A team leader who is not a lead teacher shall receive a $3000 annual
26               stipend.

27               Each non-team based school shall be allocated from the District budget sufficient stipends to pay for level leader
28               lead-teacher services at the primary, intermediate and middle school levels where there are four or more FTE
29               teachers at such levels, up to a maximum of three positions for any school with those levels.

30               Any teacher, including specialist teachers, should be eligible to be a team leader with team leader compensation—
31               as long as this provision does not inadvertently produce more teams and provided that the teacher meets job
32               qualifications that include knowledge of the standards.

33               The team leader’s duties include, but are not limited to, the following: serves as instructional leader of the team;
34               represents the team on the ILT; conducts team meetings; mentors and coaches team members; submits team
35               meeting minute and quarterly reports to the principal; coordinates the analysis of student achievement data;
36               facilitates the implementation of the Standards in Practice process; and facilitates team communication with
37               parents.

38   3.   Forming Teams

39        The ILT will oversee formation of teams. The ILT will annually determine how many teacher teams will be formed
40        within budget parameters. Teachers shall form vertical teams by level (i.e. K-3, 4-6, 7-8, 9-10): but team assignments are
41        subject to adjustment or approval by the ILT annually. Those teachers unable to agree on team composition will be
42        assigned to teams by the ILT by May 15. Teams will be formed under the following parameters:

43               (a) experience, racial and gender representation on each team must be considered;

44               (b) a teacher must commit to serving on a team as provided for in §250.1.m.
                                                                                                                                     8
                                                                                                         §145 Team-Based Schools
 1        After existing staff has been assigned to teams, the transfer and staff selection procedures in §250 will be used to fill
 2        remaining team vacancies and to fill vacancies in positions that serve the school as a whole.

 3   4.   Role of Teams

 4        a.     Team rights and responsibilities

 5               A team shall be responsible for educating its students to help them meet or exceed CPS promotion standards for
 6               that level (or high school credit granting standards in core courses for grades 9-10). The team shall determine
 7               instructional methods, consistent with the school's adopted program focus, if any, and shall determine how to
 8               group and schedule students for instruction in the subjects covered by the team. The team shall determine
 9               disciplinary procedures consistent with the district’s Code of Conduct and the Local School Behavior Plan.
10               Continuity in student-teacher relationships shall be a primary consideration.

11        b.     Assigning Students to Teams

12               Teachers shall assign students to teams. Students assigned to each team shall be representative of the school's
13               overall student population in regard to gender, race, and academic achievement. Handicapped students may be
14               assigned to teams or to special education units as determined by their IEP's and the school's Service Delivery
15               Option (SDO), if any.

16   5.   Teachers Not Assigned to Teams

17        The ILT will determine the number and type of other (non-team) teaching positions needed at the school, consistent with
18        statutory, contractual and program requirements.

19   6.   Training

20        The parties shall provide assistance to a school in transition to team based organization at the request of its ILT, to assist
21        with the formation of teams, organization of classes by teams and/or the decision making process.

22        In the first two years of being team-based, schools will be provided a total of six (6) early release days (approximately 1/2
23        day) annually for training.

24        Additionally, in the spring of the academic year before a school initially converts to the team-based system, two
25        additional early release days will be provided.

26        Schools converting to team-based in subsequent years shall receive paid summer training in the amount determined by the
27        Superintendent after consultation with the EIP.

28        Teachers newly assigned to team-based schools after the school’s conversion shall receive paid summer training in the
29        amount determined by the Superintendent after consultation with the EIP. This training will be provided in the summer
30        prior to assignment, or if the appointment is made after the beginning of the school year, the training will be provided
31        during the following summer.

32   7.   Budget Allocations for Schools and Teams

33        In team-based schools, the ILT has the discretion to determine what specialists, if any, are to be deployed in these schools.

34        School budget allocations shall be made according to the per-pupil budgeting process or the adopted budgeting process.
35        No allocations will be made for specific positions. The ILT, with the approval of the LSDMC, shall use the school’s funds
36        to support the school’s academic mission. The ILT, with the approval of the LSDMC, will allocate a percentage of the
37        school’s budget for teams’ use in the instruction of their students.

38        Teams may agree to combine resources in order to purchase goods or services or requisition personnel.

39        Teacher, teams and schools shall be entitled to choose among vendors selected by the board for purchase of supplies,
40        instructional materials and transportation for field trips, or arranging their own purchases.

41        If a team agrees to provide coverage for a teacher’s absence for personal/family illness, personal leave, or for approved
42        absences for training or professional meetings where grant money or the Professional Development Funds would pay for
43        the substitute, the funds that the substitute would have cost the District shall be transferred to that team’s budget.

     9
                                                                                                            §145 Team-Based Schools
 1


 2   8.     TAP (Teacher Advancement Program)
 3
 4               Currently we have schools participating in the Teacher Advancement Program (TAP). The application process will
 5               include approval by 2/3 secret ballot vote of the faculty. TAP schools will incorporate these four elements: 1) multiple
 6               career paths: enables teachers to pursue a variety of positions throughout their career in or out of the classroom
 7               connected to the Career in Teaching Program, 2) ongoing applied professional growth: to increase student achievement
 8               by providing ongoing job embedded professional growth: to increase student achievement by providing ongoing job
 9               embedded professional where teachers have time to meet, learn, plan, mentor, and share with other teachers to imrove
10               the quality of their instruction, 3) instructionally focused accountability: teachers are held accountable for applicable
11               teaching standards as well as the academic growth of their students, and 4) based on availability of funds, incentives up
12               to $2,000 per teacher, tied to student achievement value-added gains according to a formula designed by the Redesign
13               Committee: incentives are tied to student achievement value-added gains as defined by the State of Ohio.
14
15   9.          Incentive Route
16
17               Based on the availability of funds, the Redesign Committee will be empowered to design a formula for incentives up to
18               $2000 per teacher, tied to student achievement value-added gains. Any school will be eligible for this incentive.
19               Incentives will be offered annually.
20
21               a.   Professional Discourse
22                    The PLC leader will be trained to lead this professional discourse.
23               b.   Professional Development
24                    Professional Development hours scheduled during the teacher workday may be applied toward Individual
25                    Professional Development Plans (IPDPs).

28   §150                                                                                                     SCHOOL LEADERSHIP

29   1.     Instructional Leadership Teams (ILT)

30          An Instructional Leadership Team shall be formed at each school.

31          a.        Role of the ILT

32                    Instructional Leadership Teams (ILT’s) shall be established so that the principal, teachers, and other members
33                    may share leadership and make decisions in the following areas:

34                    •    to develop, review, and evaluate the instructional program;
35                    •    to monitor and improve school operations and procedures that impact on instruction.
36                    •    to plan and monitor training of staff;
37                    •    to develop and monitor school budget;
38                    •    to create and maintain a safe and orderly school environment;
39                    •    to oversee the formation of teams, in team based schools, within given parameters;
40                    •    to perform all other responsibilities assigned by this contract to the ILT;
41                    •    meet to review budget and implementation of ILT decisions quarterly.
42


43                    The principal and all teachers shall implement decisions of the ILT when it acts within the scope of its authority
44                    and in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements and Board policies. Discipline of
45                    teachers or other staff and other personnel matters shall not be handled by the ILT, except as provided in this
46                    agreement.

47          b.        ILT Composition

48                    The Instructional Leadership Team shall include:
49                    •   the principal,
50                    •   up to two assistant principals,
51                    •   two parent representatives selected by the parent members of the LSDMC,

                                                                                                                                       10
                                                                                                         §150 School Leadership
 1             •      two non-teaching staff members elected by the non-teaching staff of the school,
 2             •      teacher members, as follows:

 3             The Federation Building Representative,

 4             Any lead teacher serving as program facilitator at the school or in another school-wide lead teacher position;

 5             The lead teacher for special education or, if no lead teacher has been selected, an elected representative of special
 6             education teachers provided at least 5% of the students at the school have an IEP.

 7             Each team, department (of four or more), or level shall be represented by its lead teacher, or, if no lead teacher has
 8             been selected, by its elected team leader or elected representative.

 9             One elected representative on the ILT for each 5 FTE specialist teachers in a school. One elected representative
10             for each 5 FTE educational support personnel/intervention specialists in a school. For example: 1 to 5 FTE = 1
11             representative; 6-10- FTE = 2 representatives; 11-15 FTE = 3 representatives. For this purpose, Educational
12             Support Personnel shall include District employed nurses, speech pathologists, psychologists, school social
13             workers, occupational therapists, physical therapists and counselors.

14             However, at high schools, the math, science, communications arts, and social studies departments shall have a
15             representative on the ILT. The ILT shall combine other departments (including foreign language, career
16             paths/business, health) that have less than 4 members each for the purpose of representation.

17             At team-based schools, additional teachers shall be elected at large to bring teacher membership to 60% on the
18             ILT. At non-team-based schools, additional teachers shall be elected by team, level, and/or department, as
19             necessary, to bring teacher membership to 60% on the ILT.

20             Specialists include art, music, physical education, health, drama, dance, and building substitutes.

21        c.   Operation of ILT

22             i.       ILT Voting Procedures

23                      The ILT will determine how it will make decisions. Decisions of the ILT shall be made when a quorum of
24                      ILT members are present. A quorum shall be 51% of the members of the ILT and shall include the
25                      principal. All meetings of the ILT shall be open and shall be held outside of the student day, except under
26                      urgent or emergency circumstances.

27             ii.      Faculty Approval of ILT Decisions

28                      Faculty approval of the ILT's recommendations, by majority vote unless otherwise indicated, shall be
29                      required for the following decisions. These areas are:
30                      •    lesson plan format under §220.13,
31                      •    approval of the school’s budget for submission to the LSDMC
32                      •    distribution of instructional supply funds under §180.4,
33                      •    extra-curricular activities plan under Appendix A, Schedule E, Note H,
34                      •    adoption of a new program focus or other major change in the school's program (2/3 vote),
35                      •    approval of ESEA Title I School Wide Project (2/3 vote),
36                      •    application for Professional Practice School status (2/3 vote),
37                      •    approval of the school’s One Plan (2/3 vote)
38                      •    Local School Behavior Plan (2/3 vote).

39                      Teachers shall elect faculty liaisons to parent organizations and teacher representatives to the LSDMC.

40             iii.     ILT Subcommittees

41                      The ILT may appoint subcommittees to assist in carrying out its responsibilities, including developing
42                      policies and procedures listed above. However, the ILT shall act on the reports and/or recommendations of
43                      any subcommittees. Such subcommittees may include non-ILT members.

44             iv.      ILT Agendas and Minutes


     11
                                                                                                             §150 School Leadership
 1                          The Principal and a teacher co chair, selected by the teacher members of the ILT, shall jointly prepare an
 2                          agenda for ILT meetings. The agenda shall be distributed to all teachers and staff 24 hours prior to each
 3                          regular ILT meeting; and minutes shall be taken and distributed to all teachers, LSDMC members, and
 4                          staff within three days. The minutes shall include all decisions made by the ILT.

 5                          If a school has an externally funded Ohio Department of Education coach, the coach will report
 6                          periodically to the ILT on progress in improving student achievement.

 7          d.     ILT Training
 8
 9                 The Board and CFT encourage ILT training at Mayerson Academy with school-release time for all non-team-
10                 based schools and any interested ILTs.

11                 The Board and the Federation shall provide training to all schools adopting an ILT, after consultation with the
12                 schools regarding their needs.

13                 Further, the parties shall provide assistance and mediation if the members of an ILT so request or if the parties
14                 agree that an ILT is having difficulty working together or making decisions.

15          e.     Policies and Practices

16                 Policies and practices, which are implemented at the building level, shall not be inconsistent with the terms of this
17                 contract.

18          f.     Parallel Structures

19                 No other structure shall be established by the administration or the teachers to supersede or parallel the ILT.

20          g      Role of LSDMC

21                 Nothing in this section shall detract from the role or the authority currently granted to the LSDMC by Board
22                 Policy.

23                 If a school has an externally funded Ohio Department of Education coach, the coach will report periodically to the
24                 LSDMC on progress in improving student achievement.
