26   §160                                                                                                                   GENERAL

27   1.     Long Range Planning

28          The Board and the Federation agree that long range planning shall be essential for an efficient and effective education
29          program in the Cincinnati Public Schools. Any committee established by the Board for such purpose shall include
30          representation from the Federation, appointed by the Federation.

31   2.     Academic Freedom

32          Academic Freedom shall be guaranteed to teachers, and no arbitrary limitations shall be placed on study, investigation,
33          presentation and interpretation of facts and ideas concerning man, human society, the physical and biological world, and
34          other branches of learning, subject only to accepted standards of professional responsibility and to the Board's
35          responsibility to govern the public schools.

36   3.     Personal Life

37          A teacher's personal life shall not adversely affect his/her employment status unless his/her teaching effectiveness is
38          clearly impaired thereby. Within the framework of this section, teachers shall not be intimidated in their work by non-staff
39          groups or individuals.

40   4.     Residency

41          Teachers shall live where they choose. The Board and Federation encourage teachers to live in the school district and
42          enroll their children in district schools.

                                                                                                                                     12
                                                                                                              §150 School Leadership
 1   5.     Temporary Contract Alteration

 2          A specific provision of this contract may be temporarily suspended or altered only upon the written consent of both
 3          parties.
 4   §170                                                                                        PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

 5   1.     Career in Teaching Program

 6          The CFT and the Board are both committed to improving the profession of teaching. A profession offers opportunities for
 7          professional growth, involvement in decision-making, communication and collaboration, and increased responsibilities
 8          and accountability. By implementing change in the organization of schools, teachers will have the opportunity to take on
 9          greater responsibilities which will bring with it greater status, higher salary, opportunities to collaborate, as well as
10          leadership roles to improve instruction and student achievement. The parties also view a career ladder as a way to give
11          incentives to attract and keep quality teachers in the profession. To this end, the parties have established the Career in
12          Teaching Program.

13          a.     Levels and Advancement

14          (1)    The Career in Teaching Program shall include five career development levels:

15                 Level I        Apprentice: A teacher remains an apprentice until s/he meets the standard for placement at the novice
16                                level. A teacher must successfully complete apprenticeship in two years. An apprentice is subject to
17                                non-renewal after one year and shall be non-renewed if the two-year apprenticeship is not
18                                successfully completed.

19                 Level II       Novice: A teacher who has successfully completed apprenticeship or is exempted by the program
20                                guidelines of the TES and has not met the criteria outlined for the career level or higher teacher.

21                 Level III      Career: A teacher who meets the standards for the career level as defined in the TES.

22                 Level IV       Advanced: A teacher who meets the standards for the advanced level as defined in the TES.

23                 Level V        Accomplished: A teacher who meets the standards for the accomplished level as defined in the TES.

24          (2)    Lead teachers are selected from the advanced and accomplished levels and have met additional criteria established
25                 by the plan. Lead teachers shall accept assignments, including teaching assignments, meeting the district's
26                 instructional needs. Advancement to the level of Lead Teacher shall not be automatic. The number of Lead
27                 Teacher positions available shall be determined annually by the needs of the district, but shall be at least 10% of
28                 the bargaining unit, subject, however, to agreement of the parties on the availability of funds, on the program
29                 budget, and on the distribution of lead teacher positions for each year. Lead teachers' duties may include the
30                 following: consulting teachers, curriculum specialists, staff development specialists, demonstration teachers,
31                 subject leaders, team leaders, and program facilitators.

32                 Lead teachers shall have the right to return to the same schools and to the same or similar assignments without
33                 loss of seniority provided they exercise the right no later than the expiration of their first term. If the lead teacher
34                 position is eliminated during the lead teacher’s first term in the assignment, the teacher has no rights to a position
35                 in that school. If this occurs during the first term away from the sending school, the teacher returns to the original
36                 sending school. If this occurs in subsequent terms away from the sending school, no specific assignment will be
37                 guaranteed.

38                 Lead teachers shall receive stipends above the salary to which they would otherwise be entitled. Such pay, in
39                 recognition of the additional time worked and additional responsibilities, shall be negotiated by the parties,
40                 pursuant to the Career in Teaching Program Agreement.

41                 A teacher shall be considered for designation as a lead teacher and for any lead teacher role, notwithstanding the
42                 current staff racial balance at the school of his/her current assignment.
43
44                           Retirement shall not automatically terminate lead teacher status if the teacher is re-employed within
45                           his/her credentialed period.

46          (3)    The Career in Teaching Program shall be extended to other position classifications such as counselors,
47                 psychologists, visiting teachers, librarian and teacher librarian.

     13
                                                                                                §170 Professional Development
 1        (4)    The Career in Teaching program is committed to having the credentialed lead teachers reflect the diversity in the
 2               district’s teaching staff. Efforts shall continue to recruit all eligible candidates to apply for credentialing.

 3        b.     Career in Teaching Agreement

 4               The Career in Teaching Program shall be governed by the Career in Teaching Program Agreement, also referred
 5               to herein as the “plan,” which is reprinted as Appendix D.

 6        c.     Lead Teacher Panel

 7               A six member Lead Teacher Panel shall be appointed by CFT and the Board. The term of each member shall be
 8               no longer than 3 years. There shall be co-conveners, one appointed by the Federation and one appointed by the
 9               Superintendent. The Federation shall appoint lead teachers to serve as members of the Lead Teacher Panel. The
10               Panel will administer applications, credential the lead teachers and recommend additional roles and
11               responsibilities for lead teachers, but will not assign lead teachers to positions. The panel has the authority to
12               make procedural decisions necessary to implement the plan; to interpret and apply provisions of the plan; but not
13               to amend the plan.

14        d.     Funding

15               The Board will allocate $1.1 million each school year or an amount annually agreed to by the parties pursuant to
16               the Career in Teaching Program Agreement exclusive of career teacher increments. The CFT and Board agree to
17               mutually seek funding to supplement the planning and implementation of the plan, including the funding of
18               additional Lead Teacher positions.

19   2.   Cincinnati Teachers Professional Development Fund

20        The Board and Federation seek to encourage ongoing professional development through participation in professional
21        organizations, conferences, continuing education, sabbaticals, and other professional growth activities. Therefore, the
22        parties have created the Cincinnati Teachers’ Professional Development Fund (CTPDF).

23        a.     Joint Committee

24               The Cincinnati Teachers Professional Development Fund shall be governed by a joint panel comprised of an equal
25               number of teachers appointed by the Federation and administrators appointed by the Superintendent.

26               The committee will determine guidelines, criteria, and application procedures for professional development
27               activities referred to in paragraphs b, and c below.

28               In any procedures, which involve rating or evaluating proposals, teachers shall be in the majority.
29               Communications regarding the Cincinnati Teachers’ Professional Development Fund shall be sent on a letterhead,
30               bearing its name and indicating that the fund is a cooperative undertaking of the Board and the Federation.

31        b.     Conference/Convention Fund

32               The Board shall establish a professional conference/convention fund and deposit annually $175,000. These funds
33               may be used for travel, lodging, registration fees, substitute coverage, and food.

34        c.     Summer Professional Development Opportunities

35               $150,000 shall be set aside to provide summer professional development opportunities, beginning with Summer,
36               1995. Guidelines and application procedures shall be established by the Professional Development Panel.

37               The Professional Development Fund Committee may require recipients to provide a report or service to the
38               district as a result of their participation. At the end of each quarter, the Committee shall report, using district
39               records, the recipients, the activities funded, and the cost of each activity.

40               The Panel shall seek to provide equitable opportunities for use of the funds to teachers in various teaching fields
41               and levels. In its guidelines, the committee may reserve funds annually for program priorities.




                                                                                                                                 14
                                                                                                   §170 Professional Development
 1   3.   Educational Initiatives Panel

 2        The Board and Federation recognize their responsibility to promote positive change and reform in the Cincinnati Public
 3        Schools in order to improve educational results. The parties agree that partnership between teachers and administration is
 4        vital to the development and implementation of sound educational policies and programs. Therefore, the Educational
 5        Initiatives Panel (EIP) shall serve as a strategic planning team responsible for educational reform in the district. The Panel
 6        will be composed of an equal number of administrators appointed by the Superintendent and teachers appointed by the
 7        Federation. The Superintendent and the Federation President shall Co-Chair the Panel.

 8         The EIP will monitor the progress of current initiatives, plan new programs, support and encourage local school
 9        improvement and restructuring efforts. Board of Education approval may be required for some programs or initiatives.

10        The Superintendent and the Federation President shall annually evaluate the previous year’s work and then establish
11        priorities for the work of the EIP. These priorities shall be on the agenda for the first meeting of the school year, no later
12        than October 1. The Panel shall establish any necessary internal operating guidelines. The EIP shall be responsible to
13        communicate regularly with its constituents.

14        a.     Joint Committees

15               Committees, which relate to instructional policies and practices, or those whose work will impact on terms and
16               conditions of employment, shall be established as joint committees by the EIP. The EIP shall review annually the
17               existence of joint committees. Each joint committee shall have Co-Chairs, one designated by the administration
18               and one designated by the Federation. Committees shall have at least as many teachers as administrators. Teacher
19               representatives shall be appointed by the Federation. The parties recognize the importance of parent and
20               community participation in developing programs and the EIP will seek representatives from parents, community,
21               and other employee groups, as appropriate.

22               The EIP will monitor joint committees which currently exist and take action on their reports, with the following
23               exceptions: Peer Review Panel, Career in Teaching Panel and Appeals Panel, Teacher Allocation Committee,
24               Employee Benefits Committee, Professional Practice School Panel, Cincinnati Teachers Professional
25               Development Panel, and the Health & Safety Committee.

26               When a committee has been charged with making recommendations to the Superintendent, the Superintendent
27               shall respond to the committee stating his/her intentions regarding the report.

28               The Board and the Federation are committed to race and gender balance and will seek appropriate balance on joint
29               committees as well as representation by teaching fields, grade levels and/or professional roles.

30        b.     State and Federal Funds

31               The EIP shall review programs supported by state and federal grants and approve plans regarding the best
32               educational use of these funds. Funds shall include ESEA Title I and Title VI programs, Impact Aid, and
33               Educational Mobility Funds, as well as other state and federal grants, which may become available to the district.
34               The EIP may establish committees in regard to specific programs referred to above. These committees shall be
35               established in conformity with the state and/or federal requirements for stakeholder participation in program
36               design.

37   4.   Curriculum Councils

38        Curriculum Councils are elected bodies established by the Federation to represent teachers in the various subject areas as
39        well as support service professionals. Curriculum Councils will work cooperatively with the Superintendent’s Designee
40        and other appropriate administrative units to develop and maintain high quality curriculum, assessment instruments and
41        practices, and select and/or create high quality teaching materials. Curriculum Councils will provide teachers, through the
42        Federation, for textbook selection committees and for development or revision of curriculum and assessment instruments.

43        Councils also provide a vehicle for teachers to communicate among themselves about effective teaching practices,
44        research and other new developments in their disciplines, communicate with professional organizations in their
45        disciplines and with external agencies which impact on teachers or can assist teachers in their work. Councils are
46        encouraged to plan professional development activities for their constituents.

47        Each Curriculum Council shall have a chairperson, which shall be a lead teacher position. The Chairperson shall be
48        selected by the Council's Steering Committee and approved by the Superintendent’s Designee).


     15
                                                                                                     §170 Professional Development
 1          The Board will provide routine clerical services and supplies through the Academics and Accountability Department to
 2          support the work of the Councils. Further, a pool of one hundred (100) days of released time for professional development
 3          activities, conferences, or other legitimate activities of the Councils will be made available to them. Procedures for use of
 4          such professional days shall be established by the Federation President and the Superintendent’s Designee.

 5          In addition, each Council shall have the opportunity to send one elementary delegate and one secondary delegate, one of
 6          who shall be the Chairperson or designee, to the national convention of the professional organization for that discipline,
 7          funded by the Professional Development Fund. The Fund’s expense and reporting guidelines shall apply.

 8          The Curriculum Council Chairpersons shall together constitute the Interdisciplinary Council; the Superintendent’s
 9          Designee shall meet quarterly, at least, with the Interdisciplinary Council to discuss the district’s instructional programs
10          and act, as needed, to improve quality. Further, the district shall designate a liaison to each of the Curriculum Councils for
11          on-going communication. Resolutions of Curriculum Councils may be presented to the EIP after having been reviewed by
12          the Interdisciplinary Curriculum Council. The EIP shall respond to the resolution within 45 days.
13   §180                                                                                                         SCHOOL BUDGETS

14   1.     Commitment of Parties to a Balanced Budget

15          The Board and Federation acknowledge their commitments to educate the children of the District within a balanced
16          budget and to work cooperatively to achieve these goals.

17   2.     Budget Commission

18          The Superintendent and the Federation President shall appoint a CPS Budget Commission to:

19          a.     Ascertain what percent of the budget is spent on instruction and other direct services to students vs.
20                 administrative, logistical and support services.

21          b.     Recommend what those percentages should be in future years.

22          c.     Recommend a budget annually to the Superintendent.

23          d.     Monitor district and school spending compared to budget.

24          e.     Monitor CPS revenue and pursue additional revenue at local, state, and federal levels and ensure that CPS pursues
25                 available grants that support its priorities and programs.

26   3.     District Funding of Schools

27          School budgets shall be charged the average salary and benefits per FTE for each job classification in its budget.

28          The school district shall send the annual budget packet and quarterly budget reports to the ILT teacher co-chair.

29   4.     Money for Instructional Supplies

30          Funds allocated by the Board for consumable classroom materials and supplies shall be spent for that purpose. The
31          amount allocated to each school for this purpose shall be reported to the principal and to the Federation building
32          representative annually. Schools’ expenditures for this purpose shall be reported separately under accounting procedure
33          adopted by the Board. Funds allocated for classroom materials and supplies shall be distributed according to a plan jointly
34          developed by the ILT, which shall be completed by the end of each school year for the following year. Funds budgeted by
35          the Board for instructional supplies and materials shall include an allocation for speech pathologists based on twenty-five
36          elementary students per pathologist.

37          Schools shall be directed to set aside instructional supply money using the current per pupil allocation for new staff
38          members and for classrooms newly opened.

39          The dollar apportionment for supplies made available to the school or unit shall be made on an equitable basis system-
40          wide.




                                                                                                                                       16
                                                                                                                §180 School Budgets
 1   5.     Adequacy of Supplies

 2          Supplies, equipment and instructional material necessary for the implementation of all programs and course work shall be
 3          provided to teachers for each school year. The Board shall ensure that teachers have reasonable access to copy machines
 4          at each school for the reproduction of teaching materials. The ILT may allocate funds from their instructional supply
 5          money for consumable supplies for the copy machine. In team-based schools, ILT’s shall be responsible for ensuring the
 6          adequacy of supplies to each teacher.
 7   §200                                                                        TEACHER CERTIFICATES AND CONTRACTS

 8          Believing that higher standards are needed for schools, teachers and administrators in order to provide an outstanding
 9          education for all students, the Board and Federation affirm their commitment to the legal guidelines for licensure in Ohio.
10          Teachers currently under contract are encouraged to convert current certification to a five-year Professional License in a
11          timely manner.

12   1.     New Teachers

13          New teachers shall hold a Provisional License, successfully complete the Entry-Year Program and performance
14          assessment within two years, and obtain a five year Professional License.

15   2.     Teaching Outside Area of Certification

16          No teacher shall be required as a condition of employment to teach outside his/her area of certification/licensure.

17   3.     Renewal of Certificate/License

18          Teachers who have a certificate on file in the Human Resources Office, which needs to be renewed, shall be informed by
19          the administration of the necessity to renew in January of the year of renewal.

20   4.     Re-Employment of Limited Contract Teachers

21          Limited contract teachers who are re-employed shall be offered contracts before the close of the school term.

22   5.     Contract Renewal

23          A contract shall be considered automatically renewed unless notification is given by April 30, except that supplementary
24          contracts shall terminate upon completion of the assigned duties and payment therefore and are not subject to notification
25          to the employee of non-renewal.

26   6.     Continuing Contracts

27          Each teacher who has attained the career level in the TES of the Cincinnati Public Schools upon re-employment shall be
28          offered a continuing contract, provided that teacher holds a valid eight-year Professional Ohio Teaching Certificate or five
29          year professional license. A teacher who has previously held a continuing contract in Ohio shall become eligible for a
30          continuing contract after serving a two-year period in the Cincinnati Public Schools, provided the teacher’s
31          comprehensive evaluation has affirmed his/her place at career level or higher, and the teacher holds a valid eight-year
32          Professional Ohio Teaching Certificate or five year professional license.

33          A teacher may waive his/her right to be considered for a continuing contract by stating in writing to the Personnel
34          Director that he/she does not wish to be considered for a continuing contract. Such a declaration shall preclude a teacher
35          being considered for a continuing contract for the following school year. The teacher shall be considered for a continuing
36          contract for a subsequent school year only after he/she submits another declaration to the Human Resources Director
37          requesting a review of his/her eligibility by November 1.

38          Full-time personnel with multiple job contracts shall be permitted to apply for a continuing contract in the field of choice,
39          provided they work at least one-half time in that field.

40          A teacher’s continuing contract shall not be withheld due to delay in receiving transcripts from a college or university
41          provided the teacher supplies official documentation that the necessary courses have been successfully completed and is
42          in good standing with the college or university.




     17
     §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1   7.     Year of Service

 2          A year of service for regular, full-time contract teachers shall be a minimum of 120 days of full-time employment within
 3          a given school year. A day of service for regular, full-time contract teachers shall be a minimum of seven hours.

 4   8.     Continuing Contracts for Non-Classroom Teachers

 5          Employees serving in the position classifications of counselor, librarian, psychologist, teacher-librarian, school nurse, and
 6          visiting teacher, upon meeting the above criteria as they apply to the aforementioned positions, shall be offered a
 7          continuing contract, upon re-employment in their current positions. No employee, however, shall hold a continuing
 8          contract for more than one position concurrently.

 9          In the event an employee holds a continuing contract for one position classification and is offered a continuing contract
10          for a second position classification, the employee shall have a one-time option to select which continuing contract is to be
11          in effect.

12          If an employee previously held a continuing contract as a classroom teacher during the current period of employment in
13          the Cincinnati Public Schools and is reduced-in-force from a second position classification for which s/he holds a current
14          continuing contract, the employee shall have the option of waiving the current continuing contract and reverting to the
15          former continuing contract status as a classroom teacher. In the event the employee is reinstated to the position
16          classification from which s/he was reduced-in-force, the employee shall have the option of selecting which continuing
17          contract is to be in effect.

18   9.     Notice of Separation

19          Consistent with state statutes, teachers should notify the Board of their separation from service, for any reason, no later
20          than July 10. Teachers providing notice between July 11 and September 15 shall have 3 days sick leave deducted from
21          their accumulated sick leave. Teachers contemplating separation from the district will be exempt from this provision
22          providing they have notified the Human Resources of the possibility of their separation in writing prior to July 10, and
23          have notified the Board by August 15 of their separation.

24          Retirees may be considered for re-employment without public hearings, notwithstanding ORC. 3309.345.820
25   §210                                                                                                 TEACHER EVALUATION

26          The Board and Federation have developed teacher evaluation standards and procedures, which will be implemented
27          district-wide effective with the 2000-2001 school year. The standards and procedures are described in the Teacher
28          Evaluation System (TES) Manual.

29          The EIP will establish a joint TES committee to review and possibly revise the evaluation system for those teachers
30          evaluated in every fifth year of service. The recommendation of the TES committee must be approved by the EIP prior to
31          implementation.

32          The TES committee and the EIP shall consider these items along with any others the committees deem relevant:
33          •   How to provide for and integrate professional development with the standards in the evaluation system
34          •   How to reduce the time required from the teachers being evaluated and improve teaching and student achievement
35          •   How to develop and maintain exemplars to illustrate to teachers what behaviors and activities are expected
36          •   Whether the number of standards can be reduced
37          •   How to include more formative activity, including coaching, mentoring and other support and assistance for teachers
38              being evaluated

39   1.     Evaluation

40          a.     Orientation

41                 Before teachers are evaluated they shall receive an orientation to the Evaluation standards and procedures. The
42                 evaluators shall, prior to conducting an initial observation, introduce himself/herself to the teacher and explain
43                 his/her purpose for being there.

44          b.     Ratings

45                 Teachers shall be evaluated distinguished (4), proficient (3), basic (2), or unsatisfactory (1), in each of four
46                 domains.

                                                                                                                                      18
                                                                                                       §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1        c.   Standard Evaluation Form

 2             There shall be one (1) standard Comprehensive Evaluation Summary Form and one (1) standard Annual
 3             Assessment Report Form used for evaluation of classroom teachers, which shall be provided to teachers in the
 4             orientation.

 5        d.   Who Administers the Evaluation

 6             The principal or assistant principal or teacher evaluator/consulting teacher shall be responsible for administering
 7             the evaluation process. The individual who performs or assists in the evaluation of a teacher shall be competent to
 8             do so. Teachers assigned to non-public schools and teachers assigned to three or more schools may be evaluated
 9             by a program administrator, if any, or by a consulting teacher, as agreed by the parties. A certification process has
10             been developed and implemented for all evaluators (TE’s, CT’s, principals, AP’s).

11        e.   Demonstration of Teaching Techniques

12             The Consulting Teacher shall demonstrate or have demonstrated teaching techniques in the teacher's class or in a
13             classroom situation with comparable instructional needs upon the request of the teacher.

14        f.   Observation Reports

15             The evaluator shall, as a part of the evaluation process, list the date, time, place, and subject of observations made
16             with the classroom teacher, which are used, as the basis of the evaluation. It is recognized that the observation
17             reports for non-classroom teachers may not be specific as to date, time, and place because the report may include
18             observations of activities occurring over a period of time. However, such reports shall specify the type of activity
19             observed.

20        g.   Evaluator’s Responsibilities

21             Before a teacher may be given a rating in a comprehensive evaluation that results in the teacher being non-
22             renewed, terminated, placed in intervention, denied an increment or placed at a lower salary level, the evaluator(s)
23             must:

24             (1)    have made at least five (5) observations (either individually or cumulatively) of the teacher's performance,
25                    sufficient in length to justify the conclusions; new hires and teachers on intervention must have at least six
26                    (6) observations;

27             (2)    have consulted with the teacher being evaluated;

28             (3)    have provided the teacher with written suggestions for improvement which are reasonable; and

29             (4)    provide written reasons for such decision after a final consultation with the teacher.

30        h.   When Teachers May Be Evaluated and the Comprehensive Evaluation Process (clean up language)
31


32             1.     Teachers who may be scheduled for a comprehensive evaluation will be:

33                    (a) new hires

34                    (b) novice 3 (teachers at step 5 or 6)

35                    (c) teachers on intervention

36                    (d) teachers who ask to be considered for a continuing contract

37                    (e) teachers applying for lead teacher credentials

38                    (f)   volunteers if capacity to serve them exists
39




     19
                                                                                                    §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1        2.      Other teachers will not be required to participate in a comprehensive evaluation until they have
 2                professional development opportunity accompanying the annual assessments during the 2001-2005 school
 3                years.
 4


 5        3.      Except for new hires and teachers on intervention, the comprehensive evaluation will consist of five
 6                classroom observations, two done by the principal and three by the teacher evaluator. Effective in 2005-
 7                06, three of the five will focus on the standards-based unit (district standards where they exist or state or
 8                national association standards in the absence of district standards). That standards-based unit of two to
 9                three weeks will be developed by the teacher. The quarters in which the standards-based unit will be
10                observed will be mutually agreed to by the teacher and evaluators. The other two observations will be
11                done without prior notification to the teacher.
12


13        4.      Between 2001-02 and 2005-06, three of the five observations (one by the principal and two by the teacher
14                evaluator) will be announced in advance so that the teacher will know the week in which the observations
15                will occur. New hires in the district and teachers on intervention will have six observations by the
16                appropriate evaluator(s).
17


18        5.      To achieve the advanced level, a teacher must receive a score of at least two 3’s and two 4’s on the four
19                domains with a 4 in Domain 3. However, during the 4-year phase-in process (and for teachers on
20                Comprehensive Evaluation 2000-01), a teacher may also achieve advanced level with a 3 in Domain 3 and
21                4’s in each of the other three domains.
22


23   i.   Effective 2005-2006, teachers may be scheduled for a Comprehensive Evaluation:

24        (1)     during the teacher's first year of service

25        (2)     during the teacher's third year as a novice

26        (3)     every fifth year of service through step 26 (effective 2007-2008)

27        (4)     the year preceding issuance of a continuing contract

28        (5)     when the teacher has been assigned to a different subject area. For this purpose a change in subject area
29                shall be defined as one or more of the following:

30              (a) at the secondary level, change to a different subject area under a different certificate
31              (b) change between special education and regular education
32              (c) change between Career Paths and regular education

33        (6) when the teacher has been assigned to a different position classification

34        (7) when the teacher has not met the performance standard expected for his/her current level as defined in TES.
35              If a teacher currently at career level or higher receives a 1 or 2 in any domain, such comprehensive
36              evaluation will be conducted through the Intervention component of the Peer Assistance and Evaluation
37              Program.

38   j.   Annual Assessment

39        (1) A teacher shall undergo the annual assessment every year s/he is not scheduled for comprehensive evaluation
40            or peer review. Annual assessment, defined in the TES shall include at least 1 classroom observation
41            sufficient in length to justify the conclusions reached.

42        (2) Teachers at steps 16, 21, and 26 shall successfully complete two annual observations to receive the
43            increments at the next steps.

44        (3) Teachers scheduled for a Comprehensive Evaluation on steps 16, 21, and 26 will defer the Comprehensive
45            Evaluation to the following year.



                                                                                                                            20
                                                                                                      §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1        k.   Referral to Intervention

 2             (1) When the teacher’s principal has concerns about the teacher’s performance, the principal shall inform the
 3                 teacher in writing of his/her concerns for the evaluation. The principal shall refer the teacher to the Peer
 4                 Review Panel to be considered for Intervention.

 5             (2) Twenty working days after the PRP receipt of a request for investigation, the principal and teacher shall
 6                 receive written notification of the intervention decision, unless the PRP extends due to extenuating
 7                 circumstances. Consulting teacher caseloads shall not be considered extenuating circumstances. If the PRP
 8                 does not place the teacher on intervention or the PRP is late the principal can choose administrative appraisal
 9                 within the context of the Teacher Evaluation System.

10        l.   Teacher Request for a Comprehensive Evaluation

11             Teachers, who ask to be considered for a continuing contract, teachers applying for initial lead teacher credentials,
12             and volunteers, if capacity to serve them exists, may submit written request for comprehensive evaluation.

13        m.   Use of Evaluation

14             The observation and evaluation process shall be carried out with the full knowledge of the teacher and shall not be
15             used in a manner inconsistent with the purpose of evaluation.

16        n.   Special Assistance for Newly Assigned Teachers

17             Special assistance shall be given to newly assigned teachers using such resources as can be provided by the
18             principal, the consulting teacher, and other personnel.

19        o.   Teacher's Copies of Reports
20
21             Each teacher shall be given a copy of all report forms and supportive documents forthwith, following each
22             observation. Assessments, including classroom observation summaries, must remain confidential and must be
23             delivered in a sealed envelope.

24        p.   Deadlines for Final Written Evaluations

25             The Comprehensive Evaluation Summary shall be completed and submitted to the Human Resources Office no
26             later than the 2nd Friday in March if the rating could result in the teacher being non-renewed, terminated, placed
27             in intervention, denied an increment or placed at a lower salary level. In the case of a recommendation of non-
28             renewal arising out of the evaluation process only, the evaluator's recommendation of non-renewal of a limited
29             contract shall be given to the teacher not later than the 2nd Friday in March. All other evaluation reports shall be
30             completed and submitted by May 15. Failure to meet these deadlines may be a basis for appeal. Copies of all
31             evaluation materials shall be furnished to the teacher evaluated prior to placement in the teacher's personnel file.
32             The teacher shall have the right to attach a written comment to the report. In the event the teacher is to be
33             terminated, the Board shall advise the teacher in compliance with the Ohio Revised Code.

34             (See exception regarding mid-year dismissal, §210.2.g)

35        q.   Appeal Process

36             Teachers may appeal the scores on Domains 1, 2, 3, and 4 by sending a written Request for Review to Human
37             Resources within 10 working days of receiving the final scores on the comprehensive evaluation. The TES
38             Appeals Panel shall review the documentation and determine if the evidence supports the scores given by the
39             evaluators. If not, the TES Appeals Panel will review the evidence and provide new scores. If the TES Appeals
40             Panel overrides the appeal, it shall delineate the specific rationale in writing to the teacher.

41        r.   Appeal with Respect to Non-Renewal

42             Teachers who receive notice of a recommendation for non-renewal as a result of an evaluation shall have the
43             following appeal rights:

44             1.   Teachers evaluated through the PAEP shall have the appeal rights specified in the Peer Review Guidelines;
45                  and


     21
                                                                                                          §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1               2.   Teachers not evaluated, as part of the PAEP shall have those appeal rights from an administrative
 2                    recommendation for non-renewal specified in Appendix C.

 3               A limited contract teacher with less than five consecutive years of satisfactory or better service shall be entitled to
 4               a written notice of the Superintendent's recommendations not to re-employ the teacher and such notice shall be
 5               given to the teacher no later than the first Monday in April and shall include a statement of the reasons for the
 6               Superintendent's decision.

 7               In addition, any teacher who receives a written notice of the intention to terminate or not re-employ the teacher
 8               shall have the rights specified in §300.3.d, e, or f.

 9        s.     Professional Development Aligned with TES

10               The professional development will be delivered using a variety of resources and activities and will focus and align
11               the TES standards. Videotapes of teachers performing at the 2, 3, and 4 levels in different types of schools, at
12               different grade levels, and in different content areas will be available. Exemplars of portfolio pieces will be
13               developed. Mayerson classes will support the TES domains.

14        t.     Joint Decision-Making

15               The EIP will meet regularly to accomplish the following:

16               •    Revision of TES booklet.

17               •    Analyze data and monitor the progress of the Teacher Evaluation System for equity and fairness.

18   2.   Peer Assistance and Evaluation Program

19        The Board and the Federation have established a Peer Assistance and Evaluation Program to improve the quality of
20        teaching in the Cincinnati Public Schools. PAEP has two components: (a) Induction designed to assist and evaluate
21        teachers during their first year of service in the district; and (b) Intervention, intended to assist experienced teachers who
22        exhibit serious teaching deficiencies. Intervention shall be reserved for teachers who have completed three or more years
23        of service in the district.

24        a.     Peer Review Panel

25               The Peer Review Panel (PRP) shall serve as the governing body of the program, shall select consulting teachers
26               and shall determine program guidelines consistent with terms of the Collective Bargaining Contract and Board
27               policy. The panel shall be responsible for administering the budget of the Peer Assistance and Evaluation
28               Program. It shall consist of an equal number of teachers appointed by the Federation and administrators appointed
29               by the Superintendent.

30               The PRP shall review the program guidelines every two years.

31        b.     Scope of Program

32               The Peer Assistance and Evaluation Program shall be available in all teaching fields and ESP categories. Up to 20
33               consulting teachers (FTE's) shall be assigned by the Peer Review Panel depending on caseloads arising each
34               school year. Additional consulting teachers, if needed, may be funded through the Career in Teaching Program
35               budget. Part time consulting teachers shall be utilized to serve certain teaching fields where there is not a
36               sufficient caseload for a full time position. Consulting teachers may also be assigned to conduct classroom
37               observations of teachers participating in comprehensive evaluations as defined in the TES.

38        c.     Caseload for Consulting Teachers

39               Caseload of full-time consulting teachers shall be limited to 14. Each second year apprentice and intervention
40               teacher will count as 1.5 in their caseload. Other teachers participating in the comprehensive evaluation will count
41               as 0.16.

42        d.     Term for Consulting Teachers/Teacher Evaluator

43               Consulting teachers/Teacher Evaluator shall serve in the position for a maximum of 3 years.

                                                                                                                                     22
                                                                                                            §210 Teacher Evaluation
 1          e.     Applicants for Consulting Teachers/ Teacher Evaluator

 2                 Applicants for consulting teacher/Teacher Evaluator positions may not be on the administrative leadership
 3                 eligibility list. However, a teacher may remove his/her name from the leadership eligibility list in order to apply.
 4                 A consulting teacher may not be appointed to an administrative position while serving as a consulting teacher and
 5                 for one full school year after serving as a consulting teacher.

 6          f.     Stipend

 7                 Consulting teachers/Teacher Evaluator are lead teachers. The PRP shall consider any lead teacher applicant(s)
 8                 who is properly certificated for an available consulting teacher/Teacher Evaluator position. However, if no lead
 9                 teacher applies, the PRP may select an otherwise qualified applicant who is not a lead teacher.

10                 Consulting teachers/Teacher Evaluator shall receive lead teacher stipends consistent with the CTP agreement.
11                 However, a consulting teacher/Teacher Evaluator who is not a lead teacher shall receive an annual stipend of
12                 $3000. This stipend is intended to compensate consulting teachers/Teacher Evaluator for conferences, inservice
13                 activities, practicum, and other professional duties related to the position, including 5 additional days before or
14                 after the school year.

15          g.     Mid-Year Dismissal

16                 If a teacher remains an apprentice during the second year of service and if, in a December interim report, the
17                 teacher is rated unsatisfactory, s/he may be dismissed. In the PAEP, such recommendations for dismissal prior to
18                 the end of the school year must be approved by the PRP. In such cases, the teacher shall have the rights afforded
19                 to a limited contract teacher facing non-renewal for performance reasons under the Collective Bargaining
20                 Contract. Dismissal under this provision shall not afford the teacher the due process rights under O.R.C. §3319.16.
21   §215                                                                                            DISCIPLINE AND DISMISSAL

22   1.     Right to a Conference

23          Before a teacher has a written reprimand placed in his/her official personnel file or personnel file maintained at the
24          building level or before a teacher receives an administrative transfer, suspension without pay for a period not to exceed
25          three (3) days, or a written notice of dismissal, the teacher, upon request, shall have a conference during which the
26          circumstances shall be explored. In cases of an administrative transfer, suspension without pay for a period not to exceed
27          three (3) days, or notice of dismissal, the administrator shall notify the teacher of his/her right to have such a conference.
28          The teacher shall be entitled to be accompanied by a Federation representative or another employee of the teacher's
29          choice. If the conference results in discipline, the reasons for the discipline shall be reduced to writing and given to the
30          teacher following the conference.

31   2.     Notice and Site of the Conference

32          Disciplinary conferences may be held either at the Education Center or at the school. The teacher shall receive at least
33          three (3) days notice of the conference.

34   3.     Conference Timing

35          The conference shall precede the discipline as stated in paragraph above except in extreme circumstances where removal
36          from duties may need to precede such conference.

37   4.     Rights under State Law

38          If the conference results in an administrative recommendation of dismissal, the affected teacher shall have the rights
39          afforded him/her under state law, except where the parties have established specific rights and procedures which are
40          provided in lieu of statutory proceedings.

41   5.     Suspension Without Pay

42          As a form of disciplinary action, the Board may suspend a teacher without pay for a period not to exceed three (3) days.
43          However, a teacher may file a grievance challenging the suspension.




     23
                                                                                                      §220 Teaching Assignments

 1   §220                                                                                            TEACHING ASSIGNMENTS

 2   1.     Change in Assignments Defined

 3          A change in assignments shall be defined as a change in a teacher's team assignment or, for teachers not assigned to
 4          teams, as a change in a teacher's level and/or subject area within a building or unit.

 5   2.     Certification/Licensure

 6          A teacher shall be assigned classes according to his/her certification/licensure.

 7   3.     Vacancies in Buildings

 8          Vacancies are subject to assignment within the building using the procedure below before any vacancies are posted
 9          district wide. After teaching assignments within the building are determined, remaining vacancies, if any, shall be posted
10          district wide.

11   4.     Assignment to Teams

12          In team-based schools, including middle schools with interdisciplinary academic teams, the ILT will annually determine
13          the number of teams at each level. A teacher who wishes to change teams must submit his/her request in writing to the
14          team leader prior to February 25. A teacher at the school who is not currently assigned to a team may also submit a
15          written request to the team leader to fill a vacancy on the team by February 25. Teams shall submit their
16          recommendations to the ILT by March 1 regarding filling of vacancies. The ILT shall either approve the team’s
17          recommendations or reject the recommendations in whole or in part, and inform the team of its objections and/or
18          concerns. If its recommendations are not approved, the team shall reconvene, consider the ILT's objections and/or
19          concerns and submit final recommendations by March 10. The ILT will determine team assignments and so notify
20          teachers by March 31. Each team shall organize and schedule classes within the team.

21          Vacancies, which occur after initial assignment to teams, shall be subject to assignment procedures above.

22   5.     Non-Team Assignments

23          The following provision applies to all teaching assignments at non-team based schools and to non-team assignments in
24          team based schools.

25          Principals are expected to confer with departments regarding assignments for the following school year, including when
26          assignment changes become necessary or vacancies occur.

27          Principals shall direct each department in secondary schools and primary, intermediate, and special education departments
28          in elementary schools to separately meet for the purpose of recommending teaching assignments for the following school
29          year. A teacher who desires to change departments must submit his/her request, in writing, to the lead teacher or
30          department chair by February 25. Departments shall submit their recommendations to the principal prior to March 1,
31          taking into account special qualifications, which may be necessary for magnet program positions. Secondary departments
32          shall also take into account experience and qualifications that may be needed for particular courses. Department members
33          shall strive for consensus in making recommendations to the principal. However, any teacher may indicate, in writing to
34          the principal, his/her disagreement with the recommendations. Where a magnet program exists or is created within a
35          neighborhood school, the teachers in that program shall meet to recommend assignments following the procedures
36          outlined above.

37          The principal shall either:

38          a.     Approve the recommendations of the department, or

39          b.     Decline to approve the recommendations in whole or in part and inform the department members of his/her
40                 objections or concerns. The department shall then reconvene, consider the principal's objections and/or concerns
41                 and report their final recommendations to the principal by March 10.

42          The principal shall then determine the schedule and notify teachers of their tentative assignment before the last day of
43          school.



                                                                                                                                   24
                                                                                                      §220 Teaching Assignments
 1        However, the principal may decide after considering department recommendations (and disagreement of individual
 2        teachers, if any), to post a vacancy on a district-wide basis. In this event, the principal shall communicate to the teacher,
 3        in writing, why he/she believes the teacher does not possess training, experience, or individual qualifications appropriate
 4        for the assignment.

 5        If, among applicants for the vacancy, training, experience, and individual qualifications are substantially equal, seniority
 6        shall control the choice, provided that the placement is consistent with the racial balancing of the staff.

 7        The principal or designee shall determine the teaching assignments in consultation with the ILT.

 8   6.   Assignment Changes

 9        a.     Elementary Schools

10               Changes in assignments after the initial notification may be necessary due to changes in enrollment (school wide
11               or grade level) or program offerings. When such changes become necessary prior to the beginning of the school
12               year, the principal shall notify teachers in writing of the change at the teacher's summer address, including the
13               reasons therefore.

14        b.     Secondary Schools

15               Assignment changes after the initial notification may be necessary due to changes in enrollment, student
16               optioning, program offerings or problems, which arise in creating the master schedule. In such cases, the principal
17               or assistant principal shall consult with the department chairperson before making assignment changes. Principal
18               or assistant principal shall notify the affected teachers at their summer addresses of the change and the reasons
19               therefore.

20        c.     Timing for Changes in Assignment

21               Assignment changes after the beginning of the school year shall occur only for reasons of change in pupil
22               enrollment or program offerings. Such changes during the first academic term shall be completed within three
23               weeks of the beginning of the school year. All other changes shall take place at the beginning of the quarter and
24               the affected teachers shall be notified by the sixth week of the previous term.

25   7.   Teacher Day

26        a.     Length of Workday

27               The teacher workday shall be no more than four hundred twenty (420) consecutive minutes per day, including a
28               duty-free lunch period of thirty (30) minutes.

29        b.     School Organization Structure

30               As of the 2004-05 school year, teachers in K-8, 9-12 schools will follow schedules of predominate school
31               organization (i.e. same opening, closing time, lunch, minutes for instruction and planning bells). Because grades
32               seven and eight are no longer housed in separate facilities, language concerning that specific organizational
33               structure is obsolete.

34        c.     Preparation Time - Elementary Teachers

35               Elementary K-8 teachers shall be assigned preparation and/or conference time of 255 minutes per week.

36               The Federation and Board agree that all elementary students should have regular instruction by art, music, and
37               physical education specialists, except pursuant to §145.7. While such instruction is scheduled, the regular
38               classroom teacher shall have a preparation and/or conference period. Every elementary school shall have
39               certificated P.E., art, and music specialists who are non-load bearing. The Board shall assign sufficient specialists
40               so that each K-6 student shall receive instruction from each specialist. While such instruction is scheduled, the
41               regular classroom teacher shall have at least three preparation and/or conference periods. In addition, each
42               elementary teacher shall be assigned at least one additional 30 minute preparation/conference period weekly
43               during the students’ school day.

44               Elementary team and level leaders may be assigned additional preparation periods, but no more than twice the
45               number of preparation periods assigned to other teachers at their level.
     25
                                                                                               §220 Teaching Assignments
 1   d.   Elementary Library Session

 2        If an elementary class is taken to the library for the presentation of a regularly scheduled lesson by the teacher-
 3        librarian, the class teacher shall be authorized to use the time for a preparation and/or conference. However, if the
 4        teacher has otherwise been scheduled for the required minutes of preparation time, the principal may assign the
 5        teacher to participate with the class in the library.

 6   e.   Instructor Assistant Schedule

 7        IA’s who work directly for a team of teachers will be scheduled by the team. IA’s who serve the school as a
 8        whole, if any, shall be scheduled by the ILT (or by the principal if the school has no ILT). IA’s shall not be
 9        diverted from classroom assignments called for in the adopted schedule, except in emergencies or for supervisory
10        duties, determined as follows:

11        It is the intent of the district that non-teaching supervisory duties should be assigned to non-teaching personnel
12        and every effort shall be made to do so. Such duties shall include monitoring bus arrivals or departure or student
13        boarding, monitoring the cafeteria, playground, hallways or student restrooms.

14        The ILT shall assign supervisory duties utilizing non-teaching staff to the extent possible before any teachers are
15        assigned those duties. To the extent possible, the principal shall assign duties as recommended by staff.

16        If an insufficient number of non-teaching personnel impedes the assignment of supervisory duties to non-teaching
17        personnel, the school may request additional instructor assistant time from the Teacher Allocation Committee,
18        except to the extent that the Board has already allocated to team based schools a share of the overload funds
19        available to the committee.

20        These provisions do not relieve teachers of the responsibility to assist in the enforcement of school rules and in the
21        maintenance of decorum and discipline required for instruction

22   f.   Daily Schedule - High School Teachers

23        For high school, the daily schedule shall consist of not more than a homeroom and 280 minutes of classroom
24        instruction.

25        (1)    Where the school is organized on a seven (7) 50 minute class period schedule, each non-career technical
26               teacher will be assigned no more than five (5) regular classes and one period for preparation. During the
27               remaining period, a teacher may be assigned to study hall (for up to one period per week or the equivalent
28               amount of time during the school year) or to tutoring, including tutoring for proficiency tests, or may
29               volunteer for other student activities with the approval of the principal, for up to three (3) periods per week
30               or the equivalent amount of time during the year. The remaining two (2) periods per week shall be
31               reserved for preparation or conferences. However, at team based schools, the remaining periods may be
32               used to meet requirements for team planning periods, as provided in h., below

33        (2)    Where the school is organized on a six (6) class period schedule of 55-minute class periods, each non-
34               career technical classroom teacher will be assigned no more than five (5) regular classes and one (1)
35               period for preparation.

36        (3)    Where the school is organized on an eight (8) class period schedule, each non-career technical classroom
37               teacher will be assigned no more than six (6) regular classes and one (1) period for preparation. This form
38               of organization shall be used only for magnet schools or programs with unique requirements.

39        (4)    High schools may adopt schedules different from the three options above, provided the schedule is
40               recommended by the ILT (or TBC and principal agreement) and approved by a 2/3 vote of the entire
41               faculty, after presentation of the proposed schedule to the faculty at least five working days prior to the
42               vote.

43        (5)    All teachers in grades 9-12 shall be assigned no less than 225 minutes per week of preparation and/or
44               conference time or one class period daily, whichever is greater. This preparation and/or conference time
45               shall not be assigned outside the limits of the students' school day.




                                                                                                                             26
                                                                                                     §220 Teaching Assignments
 1        g.   Team Planning

 2             At team based schools, the ILT shall adopt a schedule in which teachers assigned to a team are scheduled for one
 3             class period daily or the equivalent amount of time during the week for team planning, if possible, but no less than
 4             3 class periods/week. The Board shall not be required to employ additional teachers solely to comply with this
 5             provision.

 6             Teachers shall not be required to remain at school beyond the contractual workday for team-based meetings unless
 7             compensated.

 8        h.   School Day

 9             The daily schedule shall be determined by the ILT.

10        i.   Leaving School or Work Center

11             Teachers may leave the school or work center with the approval of the principal or his/her designee. Approval
12             shall not be unreasonably withheld.

13        j.   Number of Preparations - Secondary Teachers

14             Teachers (7-12) shall not be assigned more than three preparations in each marking period, including one-quarter
15             course. In the event that the principal is unable to schedule classes in compliance with this provision, the principal
16             may, after consultation with the teacher and the department chair involved, schedule additional preparations by
17             distributing them in an equitable manner, including the academic level of the classes assigned, within a
18             department.

19             A preparation is defined as a grade level designation or a specific course within a subject area, requiring a separate
20             textbook and/or specific “curriculum bulletin”.

21        k.   Assignment of Specialists/Librarians

22             Elementary Teacher-Librarians

23             Each elementary school shall be staffed with a full-time certified teacher-librarian except as provided in §145.7.
24             Teacher-librarians shall work an additional five days beyond the standard teacher contract. In schools of 700
25             students or more, an instructor assistant shall be assigned to the library for one hour a day to assist the teacher-
26             librarian with shelving and other tasks so that the library can be fully utilized by students.
27

28             A single job description/category shall be developed to allow all K to 12 certified/licensed librarians to transfer
29             between elementary, middle, and secondary schools without the requirement of changing position categories.
30             The District and CFT will work together with the Library Curriculum Council toward the goal of restoring
31             services by 2007-08.
32             The Board of Education and CFT will work toward the goal of providing P.E., art, music, and library services to
33             all elementary students based on student population.
34             All students should have access to the following services of specialists (P.E., art, music, library, counselor and/or
35             SSW, lead social worker).
36             Physical Education, Art, and Music
37             By 2005-06 the District will commit to no more than 4 FTEs. They may be assigned to more than 2 schools.
38             Elementary Instrumental Music Services
39
40             In 2004-05 – The District will commit to up to five teachers
41             In 2005-06 – The District will commit to an additional five instrumental teachers (if grant money is available to
42             purchase instruments). These teachers are centrally assigned and may be assigned to more than 2 schools.
43

44             Art, Music, and physical education specialist teachers may be shared by more than 2 schools provided that
45             teachers have reasonable job requirements. Any teacher assigned to more than one school shall have non-
46             classroom duties at only one school. The time allowed for travel shall not be during the 30-minute duty-free lunch
47             period.

     27
                                                                                                     §220 Teaching Assignments
 1        l.     Pupil Breakfast Programs

 2               Teachers shall not be required to participate in any pupil breakfast program unless it is within the four hundred
 3               twenty (420) minutes.

 4        m.     Traveling Teachers

 5               At schools where, because of facility limitations, all teachers do not have a classroom of their own, the ILT shall
 6               jointly develop and implement guidelines to accommodate traveling teachers. The affected teachers shall be
 7               represented in the process. These arrangements shall include, at minimum, providing such teachers with desks and
 8               a secure place to store instructional materials and personal possessions.

 9   8.   Professional Responsibilities

10        a.     General Responsibilities

11               The instructional responsibility includes the daily preparation for effective teaching to district promotion, credit
12               granting standards, or graded courses of study, including defining teacher goals in terms of the learner, having a
13               wide knowledge of methods, including classroom management techniques from which selection may be made,
14               making effective use of instructor assistants for classroom instruction, and using evaluative techniques that are
15               consistent with those goals. Teachers are expected to adhere to professional standards in regards to attendance and
16               punctuality, grooming, professional growth and renewal, collaboration and cooperation with other personnel.
17               However, these responsibilities are only one (1) element of the total professional task. Responsibilities, some of
18               which require time beyond the school day, as defined in Paragraph (7.a.) of this section, that are considered part of
19               the contractual assignment are:

20               (1)    Parent and student conferences to report and evaluate pupil progress. The parties agree that involving
21                      parents in the school and with their children's education, including regular communication with parents, is
22                      very important to student success. Teachers are encouraged to develop and implement a plan for
23                      maintaining contact with parents regarding student progress. Parents are encouraged to contact teachers if
24                      they have concerns about student progress. However, neither parents nor other visitors shall be permitted
25                      to interrupt class or come to a teacher's room during class time unless they have made an appointment with
26                      the teacher. Parents and other visitors shall be required to check in at the school office.

27               (2)    Conferences with other teachers and administrators regarding students.

28               (3)    In non-team based schools, except in emergencies, inservice and staff meetings to improve the
29                      instructional program shall be held on Mondays, and there shall be no more than two (2) building wide
30                      staff meetings per month. Business faculty meetings shall last no longer than one (1) hour except in
31                      emergencies. However, meetings scheduled specifically for inservice training or on the first day of the
32                      teacher work year may exceed one hour. Inservice shall be planned in consultation with the faculty.

33                      In both team and non-team based schools, faculty meetings may be used for professional development.

34                      In team-based schools, business staff meetings shall be held on Mondays. Other staff meetings and
35                      professional development planned and approved by the school’s ILT shall be held on Mondays or other
36                      days, if approved by the ILT and a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the faculty.

37                      Teachers may also be required to attend four district-wide inservice or subject area meetings per year,
38                      which shall be scheduled on Mondays. Reasonable advance notice shall be given to teachers expected to
39                      attend.

40                      At secondary schools, the workday may be extended up to two additional Mondays per month for
41                      departmental, grade level, parent or student conferences, or other professional meetings at the school level,
42                      scheduled with the teacher.

43               (4)    During the school year, the annual open house and the annual school orientation meeting, if any.

44               (5)    Committee assignments and student activities which do not require an extensive amount of time beyond
45                      the school day shall be distributed equitably by the principal after consultation with the ILT. Committees
46                      shall be consistent with the provisions of §150.1.f. No teacher shall be required to accept more than two
47                      committee assignments functioning at any one time at the building level. No teacher shall be required to
48                      accept more than one (1) student activity sponsorship functioning at any one time.

                                                                                                                                                §220 Teaching Assignments
 1         b.         Activities Not Considered in Evaluation

 2                    While teachers may participate in other activities beyond the school day not referred to above and in additional
 3                    activities, such other or additional activities are voluntary, and shall not be a consideration in the evaluation
 4                    process.

 5         c.         Activities Receiving Additional Compensation

 6                    It is recognized that certain specified activities, which require an extensive amount of time beyond the school day,
 7                    receive additional compensation beyond the regular salary schedule. Those activities, which are recognized for
 8                    additional compensation, are indicated on Salary Schedule E, for Athletic Activities and Extra Curricular
 9                    Activities.

10   9.    School Calendar

11         If the calendar committee recommends a school calendar and the superintendent recommends a different calendar both
12         will be presented to the Board of Education for consideration and a decision.

13         The student testing/assessment schedule will be placed on the calendar before the school year begins to allow teachers
14         advance notice. The schedule may be changed if state requirements change during the year. Testing schedule changes not
15         required by the state will be made by mutual agreement of CPS and CFT.

16         The school calendar for the school year(s) shall reflect student session days, record reporting day(s), professional meeting
17         day(s) and paid/unpaid holidays.

18         Student Instructional/Attendance Days ........................................................................................................................... .178

19            These are days in which instruction of students takes place for no less than the minimum requirements of
20         state statutes.

21          Records/Conference Days……………………………………………………………………………………………………………….3

22              These days shall include three (3) one-half (1/2) days per year which shall be used for record reporting on the
23              last one-half (1/2) day of the first, second, and third terms. Three (3) school days per year in which classes
24              are dismissed one-half (1/2) day early or the equivalent amount of time during a different number of days for
25              the purpose of individualized parent-teacher conferences may be scheduled. Schools may elect to schedule
26              parent conferences in the evening and release teachers for an equivalent amount of time on a non-student
27              session day. Use of this option shall require approval by a two-thirds majority vote of the faculty, conducted
28              jointly by the principal and Federation building representative.

29         Professional Meeting Days …. ........................................................................................................................................ ….2

30                The opening day and the last day of school without students are for the purpose of preparing for the
31                opening and closing of school.

32         Paid Holidays ................................................................................................................................................................. ….8

33                Eight (8) days considered as a part of the work year that employees are not required to report.

                                                                         Total School Year ........................................................................................ 191

34   10.   Checkout Day

35         On the last day of school, the checkout procedure shall be expedited by the principal and teachers who opt to be paid on
36         the last day of school shall receive their checks upon completion of the checkout.

37   11.   Monthly Calendar

38         The adopted school calendar shall be printed at Board expense in the “monthly” form presently used. Each member of the
39         bargaining unit shall receive one (1) such copy of this printed calendar.




     29
                                                                                                        §220 Teaching Assignments
 1   12.    Evaluations of Instructor Assistants

 2          Classroom Instructor Assistants shall be evaluated by the teacher(s) they assist in the classroom. If an IA is assigned to a
