 3          teaching team, the team members shall complete the evaluation. If an IA is assigned to more than one teacher, but not to a
 4          team, the two teachers in whose classes the IA spends the most time shall jointly complete the evaluation. The Board shall
 5          provide an orientation to teachers who will conduct such evaluations.

 6          IA’s who serve the school as a whole, if any, shall be evaluated by the principal.

 7   13.    Preparation for Instruction

 8          Teachers shall be required to show evidence of daily preparation for instruction including lesson plans in a format
 9          determined by the ILT. Written lesson plans shall include objectives which reflect indicators/standards the activities to be
10          used to achieve the stated objective, and the means to be used in evaluating whether the objectives has been achieved.
11          Where objectives or activities for lessons are contained in the teacher edition of assigned textbooks or in adopted
12          curriculum bulletins, teachers will not be required to duplicate or copy such information, but may make reference to such
13          information in abbreviated form. Teachers shall not be required to complete any other form describing their daily lessons
14          other than the teacher's lesson plan. Career and lead teachers shall not be required to submit lesson plans to the principal
15          or designee except during a classroom visit or on an individual basis where the principal has concerns about the teacher's
16          instructional program.

17          Teachers shall be responsible for providing direction to Instructor Assistants assigned to their classrooms.

18          A common record of interdisciplinary team planning for middle school interdisciplinary academic teams shall be
19          maintained. The format of these records shall be recommended by the ILT.

20          Each teacher shall provide emergency lesson plans for inclusion in substitute folders. The format and contents of the
21          folder shall be recommended by the ILT including procedures for periodically updating the folder.

22   14.    Professional. Development

23          Up to two professional days may be added to the school calendar at the discretion of the CPS Board of Education. These
24          days will be paid separately from the school calendar at the per diem rate.

25          The school calendar will be extended at the beginning of the year to accommodate the optional days.

26          In addition, 6 hours of uncompensated professional development will occur outside of the school day, over the course of
27          the year, with content and schedule determined by ILTs.
28   §230                                                                                                      TEACHER ABSENCE

29   1.     Availability of Sick Leave Allowance

30          a.     Accrual of Sick Leave

31                 Pursuant to Section 3319.141 of the Ohio Revised Code, all full-time teachers shall accrue sick leave at the rate of
32                 one and one-fourth (1-1/4) day per month for each year under contract. “Full-time” shall be defined as one
33                 hundred ninety one (191) days or more of service for at least seven (7) hours per day. Teachers who render less
34                 than full time, per diem or hourly service shall accrue proportionate amounts of sick leave for the time actually
35                 worked. Unused sick leave shall be cumulative without limitation, with the exception of new hires after May 22nd,
36                 2004. New hires will be limited to a 200-day cap. Sick leave shall be credited fractionally and accrued in
37                 accordance with the Ohio Revised Code.

38          b.     Availability of Sick Leave

39                 The amount of sick leave available during any pay period shall not exceed the amount at the beginning of the pay
40                 period.

41          c.     Accumulation of Sick Leave

42                 No sick leave shall be accumulated for a teacher in pay status of less than one (1) day in any pay period or less
43                 than eight (8) hours in any pay period.


                                                                                                                                     30
                                                                                                             §230 Teacher Absence
 1        d.     Attendance Incentive

 2               Any teacher who has 96 percent overall attendance for a school year shall have 1 day of sick leave added to
 3               his/her accumulated sick leave at the end of the school year. For this purpose, only absence due to sick leave or
 4               leave without pay shall be included in calculating the teacher's attendance rate.

 5   2.   Sick Leave Advance

 6        Any teacher whose sick leave is exhausted shall receive an advance of five (5) days in the pay period in which loss of pay
 7        would otherwise occur. Said advance shall be charged against the sick leave he/she subsequently accumulates. Only one
 8        (1) such advance shall be granted until all sick leave advances have been repaid. Any balance of advanced sick leave
 9        remaining to an employee's credit at separation shall be deducted from the employee's final paycheck. In addition to the
10        advance of five (5) days referred to above, a teacher is eligible for an advance up to an additional fifteen (15) days of sick
11        leave in the pay period(s) in which loss of pay would otherwise occur subject to the following conditions:

12        a.     STRS Disability Applicants

13               If an employee seeking a sick leave advance is also an applicant for STRS disability retirement benefits, the Board
14               may require the employee to sign an agreement that s/he will repay the sick leave advance within six years if s/he
15               is not reinstated as a Board employee.

16        b.     Paying Back Advanced Sick Leave

17               Said additional advance shall be charged against sick leave the teacher subsequently accumulates. However, a
18               maximum of 10 of the 15 sick days a teacher accrues annually shall be applied to the repayment of the sick leave
19               advance.

20        c.     Yearly Limits

21               No more than one (1) such advance shall be granted in any year from July 1 through June 30.

22        d.     Repayment before Teacher Accrual

23               No more than one (1) such advance shall be granted unless the teacher has accrued sufficient sick leave to repay
24               any additional sick leave advanced.

25        e.     Balance at Separation

26               Any balance of advanced sick leave remaining to a teacher's credit at separation shall be deducted from the
27               teacher's final paycheck.

28               If an employee dies prior to returning from sick leave and repaying the advance, the Board may seek to recover
29               the amount owed from the estate or the Board may deduct the amount owed from any salary or benefits payable to
30               the employee.

31        f.     Approval of Advance

32               Such additional advance shall be made upon the written application of the teacher accompanied by a physician's
33               statement showing the necessity of such additional advance and the written approval of the Superintendent.
34               Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

35   3.   Termination of Employment and Sick Leave

36        a.     Retaining Sick Leave Upon Termination

37               A teacher who leaves the employ of the Board shall retain his/her accumulated sick leave for ten (10) years from
38               the date of termination of his/her last contract.

39        b.     Credit for Previous Employment upon Re-Employment

40               A teacher re-employed by the Board who, since leaving the employ of this Board, has been employed by other
41               boards of education or by state, county, or municipal governments of Ohio shall receive full credit for sick leave

     31
                                                                                                           §230 Teacher Absence
 1               accumulated both in the prior employ of the Board and in the employ of other agencies listed above as shown in
 2               the records of the last employing organization in accordance with the Ohio Revised Code.

 3        c.     Credit for Previous Employment upon Initial Employment

 4               Any teacher being employed by the Board who has been in the service of another board of education or state,
 5               county, or municipal government of Ohio shall receive full credit for the sick leave accumulated in this previous
 6               service as shown in the records of the last employing organization in accordance with the Ohio Revised Code.

 7               Employees hired January 1, 1997 or after, shall not be eligible for conversion upon retirement of sick leave earned
 8               with another Ohio public employer. When such employees use sick leave, pursuant to §230.2, they shall first use
 9               the sick days earned with the other Ohio public employer(s) until 50% of such sick leave is exhausted. Thereafter,
10               when sick leave is used, the Board shall alternately deduct 1 day of leave earned with the district and 1 day of
11               leave earned with other employers.

12   4.   Limitations and Requirements for Sick Leave Allowance

13        a.     Restrictions on Sick Leave Allowance

14               No salary payment for days of absence under sick leave provisions shall be made to any teacher except as
15               provided in subsequent paragraphs.

16        b.     Use of Sick Leave

17               A teacher may use sick leave for absence due to personal illness, injury, pregnancy, and exposure to contagious
18               diseases, which could be communicated to others, and for absence due to illness, injury, or death of the teacher's
19               immediate family. However, a teacher may use one day of sick leave per year for absence due to observance of a
20               religious holiday.

21               (Immediate family includes: parent, step-parent, child, spouse, sister, brother, grandparent, grandchild, parent-in-
22               law, sister-in-law, brother-in-law, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, aunt, uncle, nephew and niece.)

23        c.     Procedure for Using Sick Leave

24               For an absence resulting from the aforementioned causes chargeable to sick leave, the prescribed form of the
25               Board must be completed and is subject to administrative approval. This form shall accompany the advice of
26               change in payroll, which is signed and submitted, by the principal or the person in charge.

27        d.     Maternity/Paternity/Adoptive Leave

28               A teacher may use up to 30 days sick leave for absence due to the routine care and bonding with a newborn or
29               newly adopted child.

30   5.   Frequent Absence

31        When a principal is concerned about a teacher’s use of sick leave, the principal should confer with the teacher to
32        determine whether the district can assist the teacher with any problem that may be causing or contributing to the teacher’s
33        absence. The principal may inform the teacher of the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and/or other services.
34        Depending upon circumstances, this section should be invoked before §§ 7 or 8, below.

35   6.   Medical Explanation

36        A teacher who has used ten (10) or more sick leave days during a school year may be required to provide a medical
37        explanation or a physician's statement justifying the absence. Otherwise, s/he may be required to visit the EAP or a
38        similar service. Any consultation with or services provided by EAP shall be confidential, between the teacher and the
39        EAP counselor.

40   7.   Abuse of Sick Leave

41        At any time the principal has reasonable suspicion that a teacher is abusing any claimed sick leave, the principal may
42        require the teacher to present evidence that his/her use of sick leave is legitimate, or may give the teacher a written
43        warning which shall include reasons for the suspicion of abuse. The teacher may choose to present evidence that his/her
44        use of sick leave is legitimate to the EAP or similar service. In that event, the EAP shall verify to the Board if the
                                                                                                                                  32
                                                                                                              §230 Teacher Absence
 1         teacher's use of sick leave is legitimate but shall not reveal the specific conditions or reasons, without the employee’s
 2         consent, unless otherwise required by law.

 3         If the principal is not satisfied with the evidence presented, s/he may refer the matter to the Director of Human Resources.
 4         If the Director has reasonable suspicion that the teacher is abusing sick leave, the teacher may be required to visit the EAP
 5         or be examined by a Board designated physician.

 6         Abuse of sick leave may result in suspension of pay for up to three days as provided in §215.5 or in suspension or
 7         discharge pursuant to ORC §3319.141.

 8   8.    Return to Work

 9         If a teacher expects to be absent for an extended period, the teacher shall provide to the principal an estimated date of
10         return. After 10 consecutive days of absence, a teacher shall provide the principal with an estimated date of return, unless
11         the teacher is incapacitated.

12   9.    Extended Absence Due to Personal Illness

13         If a teacher has been absent due to personal illness continuously for more than fifty-nine (59) days or is expected to be
14         absent for such period due to personal illness and after consultation with the teacher, s/he shall be in unassigned sick leave
15         status until his/her sick leave days have been exhausted or until the end of his/her current employment year, whichever is
16         later, at which time s/he shall be placed on leave of absence or separated pursuant to applicable regulations and statutes.
17         For purposes of this section, “current employment year” is defined as the year beginning August 1 and ending July 31,
18         during some part of which the teacher has actually rendered service. A satisfactory teacher with more than one (1) year of
19         service shall have the right to return to the position the ensuing school year.

20         No advance of sick leave for the ensuing school year shall be granted to a teacher in unassigned sick leave status.

21         Nothing in this section shall be construed to preclude a teacher from returning to active employment from unassigned sick
22         leave status

23   10.   Death in Family

24         Teachers shall be allowed up to three (3) days of absence chargeable to sick leave for death in the immediate family or a
25         permanent member of the household. Additional days may be allowed, chargeable to sick leave, upon approval of the
26         Superintendent or his/her designee.

27   11.   Personal Leave

28         Teachers may take up to three personal leave days. Personal leave shall be granted upon notification to the principal two
29         days prior to leave on Tuesday through Thursday and ten days prior to leave on Monday or Friday, the day preceding or
30         following a recess or holiday, or any day in May or June; except in cases of emergency.

31         It shall be the responsibility of the principal and ILT to jointly develop a plan regarding the number of teachers who may
32         be out on personal leave (excluding emergency personal leave) on Monday, Friday, days preceding or following a recess
33         or holiday, or any day in May or June.

34         Any unused personal leave days shall be converted to sick leave on July 31. For any teacher who leaves the Board's
35         employ during the school year, unused personal leave days shall be converted to sick leave upon separation.

36         Three (3) personal leave days shall be available for teachers who are employed before January 1 in the school year from
37         August 1 through July 31.

38         Any teacher employed between January and March 31 shall be allocated one (1) day for personal leave purposes.

39         Any teacher employed after March 31 shall not be allocated any days for personal leave.

40   12.   Military Leave Not to Exceed Thirty-One (31) Days

41         Any teacher may, at any time upon application and approval thereof, be granted a leave of absence for military service not
42         exceeding thirty-one (31) days in one (1) calendar year as specified in Section 5923.05, Ohio Revised Code. If the
43         teacher's military pay during such a period of absence is less than his/her regular pay would have been for such period,
44         s/he shall be paid by the Board the difference between his/her regular pay and his/her military pay for such period. In
     33
                                                                                                             §230 Teacher Absence
 1         determining the teacher's military pay for the purpose of this section, allowances for travel, food, housing or uniforms
 2         shall not be considered, but any other pay or allowance of whatever nature, including longevity pay, shall be considered.

 3   13.   Extended Military Service

 4         A teacher who leaves his/her position to serve in the armed forces of the United States, as defined by law (Ohio Revised
 5         Code 3319.14) shall be considered to be on special leave of absence; and s/he shall be entitled to return to the service of
 6         the Cincinnati Public Schools under the terms of pertinent statutes, except that said teacher must return to service with the
 7         schools before one (1) year has elapsed from date of discharge. Upon such return, the teacher shall be returned to service
 8         in the school without loss of professional or financial status.

 9   14.   Non-Compensated Leaves of Absence

10         a.     Personal Illness or Illness in Immediate Family

11                Upon proper application and verification thereof, a teacher, except those employed in non-contract positions, shall
12                be granted a leave of absence without pay for personal illness or illness on the part of the teacher's immediate
13                family for the current school year.

14         b.     Study and Peace Corps

15                Upon proper application and approval thereof, a contract teacher with three (3) years of satisfactory service may
16                be granted a leave of absence for study, Peace Corps or exchange teaching in a school outside the Cincinnati
17                Public School system when such teaching is clearly in the interest of Cincinnati Public Schools. A contract teacher
18                may be granted additional leaves of absence, without pay, of like duration for such purposes upon completion of
19                additional periods of professional service of three (3) or more years.

20         c.     Travel and Special Consideration Leaves

21                A teacher who has completed five (5) or more continuous years of contract status service as a member of the
22                professional staff of the Cincinnati Public Schools, and who has attained continuing contract status, may upon
23                recommendation of the Superintendent be granted a leave of absence without pay for travel or special purposes
24                upon completion of additional periods of professional service of five (5) or more years.

25         d.     Maternity/Parental/Adoptive Leave

26                (1)     A teacher anticipating the birth or adoption of a child to the family may request a maternity/parental or
27                        adoptive leave of absence.

28                (2)     A teacher desiring such leave shall send, as soon as possible, to the Human Resources Office a request for
29                        such leave, which shall indicate the date, desired to begin such leave. The request shall be accompanied by
30                        a statement from the physician indicating the anticipated birth of the child. In the case of a request for
31                        adoptive leave, a statement from the adoption agency may be substituted for the physician statement.

32                (3)     The teacher shall, except in unusual circumstances, plan such leave to begin at a natural break in the
33                        instructional program, such as the end of a unit of study, the end of a marking period, the beginning of a
34                        vacation period, so that effectiveness of instruction may be maintained. If the conditions set forth in
35                        subparagraphs (1) and (2) above are met, the request for leave shall be granted.

36                (4)     The date of return from such leave shall be determined by the teacher after consultation with his/her
37                        physician, where applicable, and shall be planned to coincide with a natural break in the instructional
38                        program.

39                (5)     The Human Resources Office may require a statement from the teacher’s physician stating that the
40                        teacher’s health will not be jeopardized by her remaining at work prior to leave or her returning to work
41                        following leave.

42                (6)     A maternity/parental/adoptive leave shall be for a definite period, usually the current contract year (unless
43                        the leave commences in the second, third, or fourth term of the contract year in which case it may extend,
44                        at the teacher’s discretion, through the next ensuing contract year) subject to renewal for medical reasons
45                        substantiated by a physician’s statement.



                                                                                                                                     34
                                                                                                             §230 Teacher Absence
 1         e.     Public Service Leave

 2                A teacher has the right to become a candidate for public office and to serve in such elective office unless there is a
 3                specific legal prohibition. Upon application, leave of absence without pay in order to run for or serve in public
 4                office shall be granted. Upon return from public service leave, the teacher shall be restored to his/her former
 5                contract status.

 6         f.     Duration of and Return from Leave of Absence

 7                A leave of absence shall be for a definite period, usually the current contract year, subject to renewal at the
 8                discretion of the Superintendent, as provided elsewhere in this contract.

 9                Return from leave of absence prior to the stipulated expiration date shall be permitted. Assignment shall be made
10                to the first available vacancy for which the teacher is qualified.

11                A teacher returning from a leave of absence shall be placed along with surplus teachers and teachers requesting
12                voluntary transfers, with the following exception. A teacher requesting a leave of absence shall return to the same
13                school if the teacher so requests, and meets the following conditions:

14                (1)     The leave is effective at the beginning of the school year and the teacher agrees to return at the beginning
15                        of the ensuing school year.

16                (2)     The teacher requests the leave by August 1.

17                In such cases, the teacher shall be treated as a member of the staff of that school in making assignments and
18                surplussing decisions, if any, for the ensuing school year.

19         g.     Return from Disability Retirement

20                A teacher's return from disability retirement shall be governed by applicable statutes and will normally occur at
21                the beginning of the school year following a determination by STRS that the teacher is able to return to work.
22                However, the teacher may request to return to work during the school year. In that event, the teacher shall be
23                placed in the next available vacancy for which s/he has the necessary qualifications, experience, and training, and,
24                provided STRS has notified the Board that the teacher is no longer disabled. In addition, a teacher who returns to
25                CPS service from disability retirement within 5 years retains his/her seniority as of the effective date of the
26                disability retirement. If the returning teacher has been on disability retirement for more than three years, s/he may
27                be placed on evaluation, provided the teacher is notified no later than October 31.

28   15.   Civil Disturbance

29         In case of a civil disturbance, which occurs before the teacher leaves his/her residence for his/her assignment, the teacher
30         should make every effort to contact the proper school authorities who will determine whether the teacher will be required
31         to report to work. Teacher compensation shall not be affected nor shall the teacher lose any sick days or personal leave
32         days by school closing due to civil disturbances. If the teacher is re-assigned, s/he shall report to another school where no
33         such disturbance exists.

34   16.   Appearance in Court

35         a.     Compensation During Jury Duty

36                Employees summoned for Jury Duty shall incur no loss in pay, benefits or accrued leave. In case of absence in
37                response to a subpoena in (1) a court proceeding, or (2) an administrative hearing, in which neither the teacher nor
38                a labor organization recognized by the Board is a party, the Board shall deduct from the employee's salary only the
39                amount of any witness fee or other compensation in excess of $35 per day.

40         b.     Compensation When Teacher or Federation is a Party

41                In case of absence from duty for (1) a court proceeding or (2) an administrative hearing, in which the teacher or
42                the Federation is a party, no salary shall be paid to the teacher for the period of absence, except as allowed under
43                the appropriate section of Board policies, unless in the judgment of the Superintendent the teacher should receive
44                pay because the court proceeding or administrative hearing arises from a justifiable line of duty action on the part
45                of the teacher.


     35
                                                                                                              §230 Teacher Absence
 1          c.     Subpoenas

 2                 If a teacher is subpoenaed for a non-contract day, and the administration cannot provide a court substitute or
 3                 arrange a continuance, the employee shall be paid at his/her daily rate, on a pro rata basis.

 4   17.    Federation Conventions

 5          Teachers shall be given released time without loss of pay or benefits to attend Federation conventions and related
 6          conferences subject to the following limitations. The number of days annually available for conventions and conferences
 7          shall be 120. If a bargaining unit member identified by the Federation to be granted leave has attendance less than 95%
 8          due to sick leave and/or personal leave only, the Superintendent’s designee for Employee Relations may notify the
 9          Federation. The leave shall still be granted, but the Federation will be assessed one-half the cost of the substitute for the
10          leave.

11          Substitutes are included under the provisions of this section. Four additional days above those in the previous paragraph
12          are to be available for use of substitutes.

13          The Board is not required to release more than five (5) teachers from any particular school on a given day for Federation
14          conventions or conferences.

15          Conference leave shall not be granted during the first week of the school year unless the Federation’s national convention
16          is scheduled that week.

17   18.    Assault Leave

18          a.     Procedure

19                 Pursuant to Section 3319.143 of the Ohio Revised Code, the Board shall provide teachers with assault leave by
20                 which a teacher who is absent due to physical disability resulting from an assault, which occurs in the course of
21                 employment, shall be maintained on full pay status during the period of such absence. A teacher suffering such an
22                 assault may request assault leave by furnishing a signed statement on a form prescribed by the Board.

23                 Assault leave shall be granted upon approval of the request by the Superintendent. Approval by the Superintendent
24                 shall not be unreasonably withheld. The Superintendent may from time to time review the status of a teacher on
25                 assault leave so as to determine whether such leave shall continue. A teacher returning from assault leave shall be
26                 treated in the same manner as a teacher returning from sick leave. A teacher who has been on assault leave more
27                 than 45 days shall apply for disability retirement benefits from the State Teachers Retirement System or the
28                 teacher's assault leave will cease.

29                 For daily rate substitutes, salary paid during an assault leave shall be paid based upon the average number of days
30                 worked per pay period during all previous pay periods, not to exceed five pay periods. The amount of assault leave
31                 paid under this provision shall not exceed 180 days.

32          b.     Payment for Medical Treatment

33                 If medical attention is required, a certificate from a licensed physician stating the nature of the disability and its
34                 duration shall be required before assault leave can be approved for payment. Falsification of either a signed
35                 statement or a physician's certificate is grounds for suspension or termination of employment under Section
36                 3319.16 of the Ohio Revised Code.

37          c.     Exclusive of Sick Leave

38                 Assault leave granted under this section shall not be charged against sick leave earned or earnable under Section
39                 3319.141 of the Ohio Revised Code. All earnings paid under this section are in lieu of workers' compensation
40                 benefits.
41   §240                                                                                                TEACHING CONDITIONS

42   1.     Contributions/Donations

43          Solicitation of teachers for contributions and/or donations shall be limited to announcement of opportunities for such
44          contributions. The Federation and the Board recognize the special importance of the United Way and United Negro
45          College Fund and encourage every reasonable effort toward participation.

                                                                                                                                      36
                                                                                                          §240 Teaching Conditions
 1   2.   Faculty Facilities

 2        The Board shall continue its efforts to keep the schools reasonably and properly equipped and maintained. School
 3        building inadequacies develop because of changes in enrollment shifts in area population, changes in educational
 4        programs, and normal depreciation and obsolescence. It is recognized that at some buildings there are inadequacies,
 5        involving such facilities as: school-site parking, adequate lighting in school parking lots and at school entrances;
 6        classroom, including tack board, storage, and intercommunication system; teacher work areas; conference rooms;
 7        lounges, and restrooms. The Board's facilities improvement plan shall include providing or upgrading the above facilities
 8        to correct inadequacies and shall be implemented as financing is available. New construction or major renovation of any
 9        school shall include these facilities.

10   3.   Faculty Space

11        A facility shall be available to teachers during the school day where liquid refreshments may be purchased. ILT shall
12        determine the use of the proceeds pursuant to Board Policy #3257.3.

13   4.   Intercoms/PA Systems

14        All classrooms are to be equipped with a means of direct communication with the school office.

15        An oral signal shall be given to indicate the intercom is “on”. Announcements shall be made at times mutually agreed
16        upon by the ILT.

17        The administration shall be responsible for the efficient operation of the public address system.

18   5.   Telephone Calls

19        Each individual teacher receiving an emergency telephone call shall be notified of such call.

20   6.   Library Funds

21        Fines collected for lost or late library books shall be returned to the school library for use in expanding the collection, and
22        shall be in addition to their regular budget allocation.

23        The administration shall provide to each school a list showing the amount of library fines collected by each school and
24        returned to each school. The principal shall furnish this information to the librarian or teacher librarian, if any.

25   7.   Health and Safety

26        a.     Cooperation of Board and Federation

27               The Board and the Federation will cooperate in the continuing objective to eliminate accidents and health hazards.
28               The Board shall continue making reasonable provisions for the safety and health of its teachers.

29        b.     Grieving Hazardous Conditions

30               A teacher or group of teachers who believes that a teacher is being required to work under conditions which are
31               unsafe or unhealthy beyond the normal hazard inherent in the assignment in question shall have the right to file a
32               grievance at Level Two of the Grievance Procedure for preferred handling in such procedure.

33        c.     Safety Committee

34               The Board and the Federation agree to name a Safety Committee consisting of two (2) members designated by the
35               Federation, and two (2) members designated by the Board. The Safety Committee will advise the Superintendent
36               in writing in promoting safety and industrial hygiene. The Board shall determine the specific means by which an
37               alleged safety or industrial hygiene condition is corrected or eliminated, including taking equipment out of service.
38               The committee will hold regular monthly meetings and may decide to conduct inspections, where necessary.




     37
                                                                                                           §240 Teaching Conditions
 1          d.     Utility Failures

 2                Teachers shall not be required to work under conditions that are unhealthy due to utilities failure, such as power,
 3                heat, or water. The Federation shall be informed promptly when such utility failures occur and of the actions the
 4                administration plans to remedy the problem.

 5          e.     Snow Removal

 6                The Administration shall implement procedures for prompt removal of snow and ice from school drives,
 7                sidewalks, parking lots, and entranceways.

 8          f.     Safety Procedures for Dangerous Materials

 9                The Board shall establish and distribute to teachers safety procedures for the storage, handling, and disposal of
10                chemicals and dangerous materials, incorporating OSHA standards. Further, the Board shall identify teachers to
11                receive training regarding these standards. The science/health curriculum council shall participate in the planning
12                of such training.

13          g.     Moving

14                Teachers will be compensated through mover’s insurance for lost property during transitions; district will
15                supervise actual movement of property.
16   §250                                                                                   TEACHER TRANSFER PROCEDURES

17   1.     Voluntary Transfers

18          a.     Honoring Transfer Requests

19                Teacher requests for transfer will be honored if positions are available and the teacher is qualified for a particular
20                vacancy, provided that the transfer is consistent with the racial balance of the staff. However, a teacher who is in
21                the intervention program or continued for a second year of internship shall not be eligible for a voluntary transfer,
22                unless approved by the Peer Review Panel.

23                Teachers shall be considered for vacancies by school interview panels a according to procedures described in e.
24                below. At the time a teacher is offered a position, s/he shall either accept or refuse the position. If a teacher accepts
25                a position, s/he may be required to report to that assignment. However, a teacher who was surplussed from a
26                building may return to that site until the first day of the new school year. However, a surplus teacher who has
27                accepted a transfer may elect to waive his/her right to return to his/her original school and to serve instead at the
28                newly assigned school for the coming school year. In this case, his/her right to return to their original school shall
29                be for extended an additional year.

30                A teacher may refuse a voluntary transfer after accepting a position only for extenuating circumstances and if it is
31                feasible to move the replacement. Said refusal shall not prevent subsequent re-application for transfer.

32          b.     Vacancy Announcements, Applications and Timeline

33                Teachers may apply for positions by category (by level at a specific school, for example). Schools will continue
34                to identify specific open positions.

35                There shall be two distinct transfer periods, Round 1 and Round 2. During these transfer periods, teachers may
36                apply only for positions included in the vacancy announcement for that transfer period and only positions listed in
37                these vacancy announcements may be filled.

38                Round 1

39                In round one, the Board shall announce throughout the school district vacancies known for the following school
40                year. Teachers who submit a request for transfer shall be considered for the announced vacancies.

41                There shall be one priority level. Teachers may list up to five positions as Priority choices.

42                Priority requests are for positions to which the teacher prefers to transfer. The teacher’s application for each
43                Priority position must be considered.
                                                                                                                                        38
                                                                                            §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1             A teacher who accepts a position listed on the round one announcement is not eligible to seek another position
 2             listed on the round two announcements.

 3             Vacancies listed in the round one announcement shall be filled, to the extent possible, prior to the Round one
 4             deadline.

 5             Round 2

 6             During Round two, the Board shall announce throughout the district all vacancies for the following school year,
 7             which were not included in the Round 2 announcement, and those vacancies remaining open from the Round 1
 8             announcement. Any teacher who does not receive a transfer in Round 1 may submit a request for transfer within
 9             seven (7) calendar days following that announcement.

10             Vacancies listed on this announcement must be filled, to the extent possible, and teachers notified by the mutually
11             agreed date on the timeline. However, if vacancies remain unfilled at the end of either transfer period, requests
12             from qualified teachers for positions posted during that period must be honored before new candidates are
13             considered.

14             All teachers who applied for a transfer in Round 2 by the end of the staffing timeline shall be notified whether or
15             not they received a transfer by the end of the school year.

16             The Board will send an updated list of all vacancies to the Federation and to all schools for posting. Teachers will
17             be informed that the update will be available at all schools, the Human Resources Office, and the Federation
18             Office.

19             Vacancies which remain or occur after July 1 shall be filled first by surplus teachers and teachers returning from
20             leave of absence who have not yet been placed in them by new employees. The exception to this is the district may
21             hire properly trained Montessori teachers to be assigned to Montessori schools to positions for which they are
22             properly certificated/licensed, even when a pool of surplus teachers without Montessori training exists. Selection
23             of these new hires shall be consistent with Section 250.1.e.

24             Vacancies, which occur after the school year begins, may be filled by hiring. However, teachers hired after the
25             school year begins are subject to displacement at the end of the year.

26        c.   Teachers Returning From Leave of Absence

27             The Human Resources Office shall mail vacancy announcements to teachers scheduled to return from leaves of
28             absence. Such teachers shall have the opportunity to apply for vacancies and shall be considered along with
29             teachers requesting transfer. Teachers scheduled to return from leave of absence who are not placed by July 1 shall
30             have priority for placement along with surplus teachers.

31        d.   Modification of Dates

32             The Federation President and the Human Resources Director will establish a committee annually to set budget and
33             staffing time line dates. They may agree to modify specific dates used in these transfer procedures to
34             accommodate the school calendar. Modifications must be announced before the annual process begins. The dates
35             for budget and staffing activities will be established and announced annually using the following time line:




     39
                                                                                        §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1        Timeline:
           7 weeks            Student Information Systems would have seven (7) weeks from the October ADM to
                              send student projections to schools.
           2 weeks            Schools would have two (2) weeks to review student projections and respond
           1 week             Schools and Student Information Systems would have one (1) week to come to
                              consensus on student projections
           1 week             The Budget Office would have one (1) week to load budgets and distribute to
                              schools. Early retirement date notification.
           4 weeks            Schools would have four (4) weeks to review budget, staff, submit to ILT, LSDMC
           1 week             The Budget Office would have one (1) week to do a budget/surplus review
           2 weeks            Human Resources would have two (2) weeks to work the position process
           1 week              Round 1 Posting would have a one (1) week process
           1 week             Human Resources would have one (1) week to distribute applicant information
           3 weeks            Schools would have three (3) weeks for the round one interview process
           2 weeks            Human Resources would have two (2) weeks to work on the staffing process
           1 week             Round 2 Posting would have a one (1) week process
           1 week             Human Resources would have one (1) week to work on the staffing process
           3 weeks            Schools would have three (3) weeks for the round two interview process
           1 week             Human Resources would have one (1) week to work on the staffing process
           31 weeks           Total

 2        *Job share deadline: April 15th

 3   e.   Selection Process

 4        The Board and Federation agree that teachers and principals should have a greater role in selecting teachers to fill
 5        vacancies. Therefore, the parties agree that such decisions shall be made jointly by the principal and teachers in
 6        that department, team, or level at the school. These provisions apply only to positions, which serve at a single
 7        school and report to the principal.

 8        When vacancies occur, teachers in the department, team, primary or intermediate unit shall elect no more than four
 9        teachers in the unit, one of whom shall be the lead teacher in the unit, if any, to serve with the principal or
10        designee as an interview panel. In team-based schools, the team and the principal or designee shall constitute the
11        interview panel, with the addition of a teacher in the same subject area as the vacancy who shall be appointed by
12        the ILT. When vacancies occur in school wide positions, including elementary and middle school art, music and
13        physical education specialists, educational service personnel, librarians and teacher-librarians, the ILT shall select
14        four teachers to serve with the principal or designee as an interview panel. If fewer than three teachers remain in a
15        team, department or unit, the ILT shall select additional teachers to serve on the interview panel to reach a
16        minimum of three. The panel shall review any relevant written information provided by the applicant or by the
17        principal, and interview preferred applicants. Following such review and the interviews, the panel shall select a
18        teacher for the vacancy. In making its decision, the panel shall apply criteria stipulated in f. below. Selection of a
19        candidate requires the agreement between the principal and a majority of the teachers of the selection panel.

20        A team of teachers or the majority of the team with appropriate certification for the posted positions may apply for
21        vacant positions at any school, which has a sufficient number of vacancies.

22        For vacancies occurring during summer recess, the principal shall be responsible to make good faith efforts to
23        contact all screening panel members. At least two members of the screening panel must be present for the
24        selection to be considered a product of this process. Otherwise, the decision is subject to a grievance under the
25        provisions of §300.3.g. The school staff shall consider teacher’s summer availability when selecting a screening
26        panel.

27        These selection provisions shall apply to vacancies beginning with the 1995-96 school year at all schools. This
28        process applies to new hires as well as transfer applicants.

29        Appeals of decisions made by local school interview panels shall be submitted directly to the Alternate Grievance
30        Panel. Appeals may be filed by a current CPS teacher who applied for a vacancy but was not selected, by the
31        Federation or by any teacher who alleges that the provisions of this section were not honored in the interview and
32        selection process. Decisions of the Alternate Grievance Panel are final and binding. If the Panel’s vote is tied, the
33        decision of the interview panel shall be upheld.

34        The Board and Federation shall provide a training opportunity annually to members of the selection panels
35        established in this section, which shall be offered prior to the beginning of the transfer process.

                                                                                                                             40
                                                                                                §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1        f.     Determining Factors in Granting Transfer Requests

 2               If more than one (1) teacher who is properly certified requests a transfer to a specific building or unit, and training,
 3               experience, and individual qualifications are substantially equal, and the transfer is consistent with the racial
 4               balancing of staff, seniority shall control the choice.

 5        g.     Withdrawal of Transfer Request

 6               A teacher may withdraw his/her name from the transfer list at any time prior to written notification of transfer
 7               from the Human Resources Office.

 8        h.     Vacancy Announcements to Non-Public School Sites

 9               Vacancy announcements shall be distributed to each non–public school site where any bargaining unit member
10               delivers services.

11        i.     Newly Created Positions

12               The Board shall include newly created positions in district-wide vacancy announcements. Such positions include
13               full time teaching assignments and non-classroom student service positions not previously available at a school.

14               If such a position is created after the June 1 vacancy announcement, a notice shall be mailed to all teachers
15               assigned to the school where the position will be created who possess appropriate certification. The Board shall
16               allow 10 days from the date the notice is mailed for teachers to apply before filling the position. Such vacancies
17               are subject to the provisions in §220 Assignment and §250 Transfer.

18        j.     Notice of Transfer Granted

19               All notices of transfer shall be in writing from the Human Resources Office.

20        k.     Refusal of Transfer Request

21               Teachers shall be given, in writing, specific reasons for refusal of transfer requests within thirty (30) days after it
22               is determined that a transfer will not be granted.

23               In the event of a successful grievance, the remedy shall be to place the grievant in the vacancy requested at the
24               beginning of the next reporting period or quarter in the instructional program. The person who has been displaced
25               as a result of a successful grievance shall be given preference in assignment to a similar vacancy elsewhere when
26               available.

27        l.     Denial Based on Racial Balance

28               Effective for transfers that occur for the 1992–93 school year, no teacher shall be denied a transfer for more than
29               two consecutive years based on the racial balance at his/her current school.

30        m.     Commitment to Remain with Team

31               A teacher who applies for, is selected for, and accepts a position as part of a teaching team may be expected, at the
32               team’s discretion, to make a commitment to remain with the team for two school years (or three years if necessary
33               to complete one cycle of students). If that teacher so requests, the other team members may subsequently release
34               the teacher from this commitment by at least a 2/3 vote.

35        n.     Monitoring Personnel Actions

36               At the end of transfer Rounds One and Two, and by September 15, the Board shall publish a cumulative list of the
37               teachers selected for each position to be sent to all CPS sites receiving vacancy announcements.

38   2.   Administrative Transfers

39        A teacher receiving an administrative transfer shall be informed in writing with the reasons delineated by the
40        Superintendent or designee.


     41
                                                                                                    §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1        In addition to other grounds for administrative transfer, a teacher may be administratively transferred for refusing to take
 2        training necessary to implement the school’s magnet program, neighborhood school program focus or School Wide Title I
 3        Project, provided such training is available during the regular workday or the teacher is paid for the additional time
 4        required. For purposes of this section, if the ILT releases teachers during the school day in order to take training outside
 5        of the school day on regular workdays such training shall be considered paid time. Such training requirements shall be
 6        recommended by the ILT and approved by 2/3 vote of the faculty and shall include reasonable timelines for completing
 7        the training.

 8   3.   Surplussing

 9        a.       Reasons for Surplussing

10                 Teachers may be surplussed due to decreased enrollment or a change in program offerings or school organization.
11                 Surplussing shall be treated by the following procedures in the order of priority:

12                 (1)       Before a teacher is treated as “surplus”, voluntary transfer requests from that teacher's building shall be
13                           granted if the position is available.

14                 (2)       Before a surplus teacher is transferred from his/her school, that teacher who is properly certificated may
15                           displace a junior teacher within the building, provided training, experience, and individual qualifications
16                           are substantially equal, and the transfer is consistent with the racial balancing of staff. However, at team
17                           based schools, the Board shall not disrupt teaching teams by surplussing or reassigning team members
18                           after the last day of the school year unless significant changes in enrollment cause a reduction in the
19                           school’s budget allocation and the ILT agrees there is no sound alternative.

20                 (3)       When a surplus teacher is to be transferred from his/her building, that teacher shall have the opportunity to
21                           express preference for existing vacancies and be placed along with those teachers requesting a transfer,
22                           teachers returning from leave of absence and unassigned teachers. If a choice needs to be made between
23                           two (2) or more teachers who are properly certificated and their training, experience, and individual
24                           qualifications are substantially equal and the transfer is consistent with the racial balancing of staff,
25                           seniority shall control the choice.

26        b.       Relocating/Consolidation/Mergers/Surplussing in All Schools
27
28             Relocating

29                 (1)       When an entire school is relocated to a new site, all teachers assigned to such school who desire to remain
30                           with the school by transferring to the new school site may do so provided that positions are available and
31                           the transfer is consistent with the racial balancing of the staff.

32        Merger

33                 (1)       If an entire program or school is merged with an existing program or school of the same type, all teachers
34                           in both sites shall be considered as one staff and any necessary reductions in staff shall be done in
35                           accordance with this section.

36                 (2)       When new positions are added in a program within a building or school, such positions shall be treated as
37                           vacancies, which shall be filled in accordance with this section.

38                 (3)       Any teacher who is declared surplus shall be entitled to exercise the right to displace a junior teacher
39                           within the building in accordance with provisions of Section §220 and Paragraph 3.a above.

40        Consolidation
41
42                 (1)      When two or more existing schools are consolidated, all teachers from the sites shall be considered as one
43                          staff and any reductions in staff shall be done in accordance with this section. Prior to staffing reductions,
44                          teachers from all affected sites shall be given the opportunity to indicate whether or not they want to be
45                          considered for a position in the consolidated school. Teachers indicating they do not wish to be considered
46                          shall be surplussed without rights to return under §250.3c.
47
48                 (2)      Teachers indicating they wish to be considered but are surplussed shall have return rights under §250.3c.
49                          Additionally, any teacher indicating a preference to remain that is surplussed, shall have rights set forth in
50                          §250(3)(a)(2).

                                                                                                                                         42
                                                                                                 §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1

 2               (3)    When two or more existing schools are consolidated, the administration must consult with the federation
 3                      prior to making a determination regarding the strategy for delivering instruction. However, the
 4                      administration retains the right to make the final determination.
 5
 6               (4)    Training shall be made available to all teachers not trained in the strategy for delivering instruction after the
 7                      consolidation in accordance with the district’s overall professional development process. The training shall
 8                      be held within the teacher workday or the administration shall provide compensation in accordance with the
 9                      CBA. Sec. 250.
10
11               (5)    Surplussing and staffing for consolidated schools will occur in conformity with district-wide staffing
12                      schedule, to be accomplished by the principal or the administration's designee in the absence of a principal.

13        c.     Returning to Original School

14               Surplus teachers shall have the right to return to their original school in the reverse order of their transfer out,
15               provided a request for such transfer is made and the return can be accomplished within two (2) years of the
16               original transfer, the teacher’s last performance evaluation was satisfactory or better, and the transfer is consistent
17               with the racial balancing of staff. However, if a surplus teacher joins a team at another school, his/her right to
18               return shall be postponed until the teacher fulfills or is released from his/her team commitment, pursuant to
19               §250.1.m and shall apply only for the ensuing school year.

20        d.     Notification of Surplussing

21               Any teacher who is surplussed shall be sent written notification. If verbal notice is given, written notice must be
22               sent within 10 days.

23        e.     School Intervention and Redesign

24               Pursuant to the School Assistance and Redesign Plan (hereafter, the plan) developed by the parties, when a school
25               falls in the Redesign category, based on the criteria set forth in the plan, and is closed, all teachers serving at the
26               school shall be displaced and treated as surplus. All teaching positions at any new school, which replaces the
27               closed school, shall be considered vacancies. Teachers shall be selected, according to the provisions of the plan,
28               based on their training, experience and individual qualifications for the program to be offered at the redesigned
29               school and for specific teaching positions. Teachers displaced by school redesign shall have the opportunity to
30               apply for vacancies at the newly designed school, if they possess the appropriate certificate or license, and shall
31               have the rights afforded to surplus teachers under §250.3.a (3) above. However, §250.3.c shall not apply.

32   4.   Job Sharing

33        Two properly certificated teachers may, upon written joint request to the Director of Human Resources by April 15, share
34        one position at a single school for the ensuing school year with each teacher assigned and paid 50%, upon approval by the
35        principal. Both teachers shall comply with the provisions of the contract and may designate certain responsibilities and
36        working conditions such as lunch and preparation time subject to the approval of the principal. The Board shall pay the
37        cost of all benefits.

38        Both teachers shall return to full-time status if previously employed full-time effective the ensuing school year, unless
39        another written joint request for the ensuing school year is approved by the principal. Teachers returning to full-time
40        status from job sharing shall be considered for vacancies within the building and district along with surplus teachers,
41        teachers returning from leave and teachers requesting transfers.

42        If either of the teachers who are sharing a position cannot or will not perform his/her share of the duties of the shared
43        position, the remaining teacher shall remain in the position, full time.

44        Teachers sharing a position shall receive credit for a full year of service for purposes of certificate renewal or upgrade and
45        one-half year of service credit for placement on Salary Schedule C.

46   5.   Selection of Educational Service Personnel

47        The following provisions shall govern selection of teachers for vacancies in educational service personnel positions,
48        including counselor, visiting teacher, psychologist, librarian, teacher librarian, home-school teacher or home-school
49        coordinator. Teachers who are properly certificated for one or more of the above positions, or who expect to be
50        certificated by August 1, may apply by April 15 for assignment to a position for the following school year. Each year the

     43
                                                                                                 §250 Teacher Transfer Procedures
 1          Board shall announce this opportunity to teachers by March 15. The announcement shall include the certification and any
 2          other qualifications required for each position.

 3          One screening panel shall be established for all such positions, convened by the Human Resources Director or his/her
 4          designee. Alternately, the Human Resources Director or his/her designee may convene separate panels for one or more
 5          ESP categories. Each panel shall consist of an equal number of administrators and of practitioners currently serving in
 6          such positions who shall be appointed by the Federation.

 7          The purpose of the screening panel(s) shall be to recommend candidates for placement on eligibility lists for ESP
 8          vacancies. The panel(s) shall consider all applicants who meet minimum qualifications, including candidates who are not
 9          current CPS employees, and shall review references, personnel files, and other data necessary in arriving at its
10          recommendations. All deliberations shall be confidential. The panel shall submit to the Human Resources Office a list of
11          candidates recommended for ESP positions in each of the above categories. This list shall constitute the eligibility list for
12          ESP vacancies for the following school year, unless the position is filled pursuant to 10.b.1, 2, 3, or 4. However, long-
13          term substitutes may be used to fill an ESP vacancy only if there is no qualified candidate on the eligibility list.

14          Applicants may remain on the eligibility list for no more than two years without applying again to be considered by the
15          screening panel.

16          However, the Human Resources Director or his/her designee may reconvene the screening panel(s) during the summer or
17          during the school year if less than 3 applicants remain on the eligibility list for an ESP category or if there are more
18          vacancies in an ESP category than applicants on the eligibility list. or if the percentage of African-American applicants on
19          an eligibility list is more than 5% below the district-wide percentage of African American teachers.

20          If it is necessary to convene the panel to screen candidates for the eligibility lists during the summer months, the Human
21          Resources Director shall notify the members of the panel at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting at their summer
22          addresses. The inability of a panel member to meet during the summer recess shall not prevent the remaining members
23          from making recommendations regarding placement of candidates on the eligibility lists.

24          When a vacancy occurs and the training, experience, and individual qualifications of the applicants are substantially
25          equal, seniority shall control the choice.

26   6.     Stabilizing Faculties at Schools with High Turnover Rates

27          The Administration and Federation will jointly identify schools at which retaining or recruiting experienced staff shall be
28          a priority. At these schools, targets for the percentage of resident, career, and lead teachers shall be established and
29          Human Resources shall be directed to post vacancies at these schools in an effort to reach these ratios within three years.
30          Teachers electing to fill these identified positions shall receive 10 professional development days (or equivalent) to be
31          used during the following 2 years. Current career and lead level staff remaining at the school an additional year shall also
32          be provided 10 professional development days. Up to three teachers may transfer together to these schools.

33   7.     Unassigned Teachers Notice of Vacancies

34          Contract teachers who are unassigned shall be notified of any vacancy for which they are properly certified which occurs
35          during the school year and must be considered for the position.
36   §260                                                                                                                 SENIORITY

37   1.     Definition

38          Seniority shall be defined in priority as follows:

39          a.     Years of Continuous Contractual Service

40                 Total number of continuous contractual years in the Cincinnati Public Schools, including any period of approved
41                 leave. Teachers whose contracts were not renewed in April 1974, but who were rehired during the 1974-75 school
42                 year, shall be considered as having continual contractual service.

43          b.     Years in Current Building

44                 Total number of years in the school building of current placement.



                                                                                                                                      44
                                                                                                                          §260 Seniority
 1          c.      Years in Subject/Level

 2                 Total number of years in the assigned subject area and/or level.

 3          d.      Years Employed as Certificated Teacher

 4                 Total number of years employed as a certificated teacher in a state-approved institution(s).
 5   §270                                                                                REDUCTION-IN-FORCE PROCEDURES

 6   1.     Introduction

 7          When conditions such as declining student enrollment, limited financial resources, reduction in or discontinuance of
 8          selected services occur, it may be necessary to implement a “Reduction-in-Force” (RIF) procedure. For the purpose of
 9          this RIF procedure, the following definitions are used:

10          a.      Reduction-in-Force: to discontinue the services of employees serving in a given classification because of a
11                  reduction in the number of positions available.

12          b.      Position Classification: a position title, which is listed on the employee salary schedules by the Cincinnati Board
13                  of Education

14          c.      Displacement: the exercising of the right of an employee with greater entitlement to a position causing another
15                  employee with lesser entitlement to be removed from a position within the position classification.

16          d.      Entitlement: rights of employees determined by the application of the specified criteria listed in Paragraph (2),
17                  below.

18   2.     Criteria

19          The following criteria are to be applied in order of priority as listed:

20          a.      Certification: Appropriate certification for the grade level, subject matter to be taught and/or for the position
21                  classification.

22          b.      Contractual Status: For the purpose of reductions in a position classification, teachers with limited contracts shall
23                  be considered before those with continuing contracts.

24          c.      Part-Time Employment: Part-time employees serving under limited contracts shall be considered for reduction-in-
25                  force before consideration of full-time employees.

26          d.      Training, Experience and Individual Qualifications

27          e.      Seniority:

28                  (1)    Total number of continuous contractual years of service in the Cincinnati Public Schools in position
29                         classification, including any period of approved leave. Employees whose contracts were not renewed in
30                         April 1974, but who were rehired during the 1974-75 school year, shall be considered as having
31                         continuous contractual service.

32                  (2)    Total number of continuous contractual years of service in the Cincinnati Public Schools, including any
33                         period of approved leave. Employees whose contracts were not renewed in April 1974, but who were
34                         rehired during the 1974-75 school year, shall be considered as having continuous contractual service. Any
35                         employee whose contract is non-renewed or suspended due to reduction-in-force who is subsequently
36                         rehired as a contract teacher during the term of his/her re-call right under Section 5 below shall be
37                         considered as having continual contractual service.

38                  (3)    Total number of years employed as a certificated teacher in a state-approved institution(s).




     45
                                                                                             §270 Reduction-in-Force Procedures
 1   3.   Applying Criteria

 2        If a choice needs to be made between two or more teachers who are similarly situated with respect to criteria (a), (b), and
 3        (c), and training, experience and individual qualifications are substantially equal, the teacher with the greater seniority as
 4        defined in the order of priority in criteria (e) above shall be retained.

 5   4.   Reduction in Non-Teaching Positions

 6        When the number of employees in any of the following classifications is reduced, such employees shall be identified for
 7        change of status on a system-wide basis. If a choice needs to be made between two (2) or more such employees who are
 8        properly certificated and their training, experience, and individual qualifications are substantially equal, seniority in the
 9        position classification shall control the choice. Such classifications are counselors, teacher-librarians, librarians,
10        psychologists, school social workers, and school nurses.

11        An employee who suffers a reduction-in-force who is serving in a position classification other than teacher, and who
12        served as a teacher in the Cincinnati Public Schools prior to assignment in the current position classification, shall have
13        the right to exercise entitlement to a teaching position.

14        Before a surplus employee, who has been changed in status from a non-teaching-position classification to a classroom
15        teacher, is transferred from his/her school, that employee shall have the opportunity to exercise the rights set forth in
16        §250.3.

17   5.   Re-Employment

18        An employee whose position classification has been changed as a result of these RIF procedures shall be offered re-
19        employment to that position classification before such vacancy is filled by an employee who has not served in the position
20        classification previously or a candidate not currently employed by the Cincinnati Board of Education. However, an
21        exception to this is the district may hire teachers who have completed proper Montessori training to teach in a Montessori
22        school, assigned to positions for which they are certificated/licensed. Selection of these new hires shall be consistent with
23        Section 250.1.e.

24        If CFT and CPS mutually agree that a need exists for Paideia trained teachers to be hired during a time when RIF re-
25        employment terms apply, CPS and CFT agree to re-open this section of the contract.

26        Employees shall be re-employed based upon the criteria specified in Paragraph (2) above, except for Montessori and
27        Paideia trained teachers. If a choice needs to be made between two or more teachers who are similarly situated with
28        respect to criteria (a), (b), and (c), and training, experience and individual qualifications are substantially equal, the
29        teacher with the greater seniority as defined in order of priority in criteria (e) above shall be re-employed. Entitlement re-
30        employment shall remain in effect for eighteen (18) months. When a satisfactory part-time employee is non-renewed
31        under this article, s/he shall be offered full-time employment, if available, before new employees, but after full-time
32        employees have been re-called.

33        A teacher reinstated within 18 months (of the start of the first school year following the RIF notification) shall be
34        considered as having continuous contractual service. For evaluation purposes and credit on Salary Schedule C, such
35        teacher shall be credited with the years of service s/he had when laid off.

36   6.   Effect of State Law

37        These procedures shall apply to reductions-in-force only when implemented under the provisions of Sections 3319.11 of
38        the Ohio Revised Code.

39   7.   Re-Training

40        For those teachers laid off due to reduction-in-force the Board agrees to reimburse such teachers for tuition expenses up to
41        a maximum of 12 semester or 18 quarter hours, provided the teacher completes the required coursework for a temporary
42        teaching certificate in comprehensive science, secondary math, or other areas of certification which may be designated by
43        the Director of Human Resources or his/her designee. If these re-training certification requirements are completed by
44        September 1, 2000, 2001, 2002, the Board shall re-employ the teacher effective at the opening of the new school year.

45        The following provisions shall apply to such re-training opportunities:




                                                                                                                                     46
                                                                                              §270 Reduction-in-Force Procedures
 1          a.     Must be Willing to Accept Full-Time Position

 2                 Part-time teachers who are employed 50% of the time or more shall be eligible only if they are willing to accept, if
 3                 offered, a full-time position.

 4          b.     No Interruption of Benefits

 5                 Teachers who are re-employed for the following school year shall suffer no interruption of health or term life
 6                 coverage provided they complete the re-training by September 1, 2000, 2001, 2002.

 7          c.     Re-Training Agreement

 8                 Are-training agreement shall be signed by the teacher and the Human Resources Director or his/her designee.

 9          d.     Notice

10                 The Board shall make every effort to notify teachers who will be subject to RIF procedures as soon as possible
11                 during the school year.

12   8.     Priority as Long-term Substitutes

13          Teachers who have been RIFed shall be given priority for long-term substitute positions for which they are qualified.
14   §300                                                                                              GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE

15   1.     Definitions

16          a.     Grievance

17                 A “grievance” shall mean a complaint in writing that there has been an alleged violation, misinterpretation or
