18                 misapplication of any provision(s) of this contract, which arose during the term of this contract or the predecessor
19                 contract. Such grievance shall be submitted on the prescribed form, which shall be available in the school office
20                 and from a Federation Representative.

21          b.     Grievant

22                 The “grievant” shall mean the teacher, teachers, or the Federation filing the grievance.

23          c.     Days

24                 The term “days,” when used in this section, shall mean contract working days unless otherwise indicated. Thus,
25                 weekends, holidays, and vacation/recess days are excluded. Summer break is excluded except as indicated in
26                 Paragraph (2.h.), below.

27   2.     General Provisions

28          a.     Purpose

29                 Good morale is maintained by sincere efforts of all persons concerned to work toward constructive solutions to
30                 problems in an atmosphere of courtesy and cooperation. The purpose of this procedure is to secure equitable
31                 solutions to problems at the lowest possible administrative level. The grievance proceedings shall be kept as
32                 informal and confidential as may be appropriate at any level of the procedure.

33          b.     Conference

34                 Prior to the formalizing of any grievance into writing, the employee may request a conference with the supervisor
35                 for the purpose of presenting a complaint, as well as the possible resolution of the complaint. It shall be the
36                 employee's prerogative to have a Federation representative present at such conference or at any other step in the
37                 grievance procedure.




     47
                                                                                                 §300 Grievance Procedure
 1   c.   Federation Right

 2        The Federation shall have the right to appear at any level of the grievance procedure and shall receive copies of all
 3        written decisions and records pertaining to the grievance.

 4   d.   Rights of Grievant/Representative

 5        Every teacher shall be represented by the Federation in the grievance procedure. The teacher shall have the right to
 6        be present at any grievance discussion and shall be present at any grievance discussion when the Board and/or the
 7        Federation deem it necessary. When the presence of a teacher at a grievance hearing is requested by either party,
 8        illness or other incapacity of the teacher shall be grounds for any necessary extension of grievance procedure time
 9        limits.

10        The failure of the grievant to act on any grievance within the prescribed time limits will act as a bar to any further
11        appeal and any administrator's failure to give a decision within the time limits permits the grievant to proceed to
12        the next step. The time limits, however, may be extended by mutual agreement.

13   e.   Protection of Grievant

14        An employee who participates or intends to participate in any grievance as defined herein shall not be subjected to
15        discipline, reprimand, warning or reprisal because of such participation or intention. All documents,
16        communications, and records dealing with the processing of the grievance shall be filed separately from the
17        personnel files of the participant.

18   f.   Hearings, Conference, and Processing

19        Hearings and conferences under this procedure shall be conducted at a time and place which will afford a fair and
20        reasonable opportunity for all persons, including witnesses entitled to be present, to attend and will be held,
21        insofar as possible, after regular school hours or during non-teaching time of personnel involved. When such
22        hearings and conferences are held at the option of the administration during school hours, all employees whose
23        presence is required shall be excused, without loss of pay or benefits, for that purpose.

24        It is agreed that any investigation or other handling or processing of any grievance by the grievant or
25        administration shall be conducted so as to result in no interference with or interruption whatsoever of the
26        instructional program and related work activities of school personnel.

27   g.   Expediting Grievance

28        Grievances shall be expedited. Every effort shall be made to resolve grievances prior to the end of the school year
29        in which the grievance was filed. The time limits specified may be extended by mutual agreement.

30   h.   Reducing Time Limits

31        (1)    If a grievance is filed which might not be finally resolved under the time limits set forth herein prior to the
32               end of the school year, and which if left unresolved until the beginning of the following school year, could
33               result in irreparable harm to those involved in the grievance, the time limit set forth herein shall be reduced
34               so that the grievance procedure may be concluded prior to the end of the school year.

35        (2)    If a grievance is filed prior to the end of the school year and cannot be resolved by the closing of that
36               school year, the grievance procedure shall continue into the summer break with all time limits doubled.

37        (3)    There shall be no arbitration during the summer unless both the CFT and the Board agree.

38        (4)    Any complaint arising over the summer break which is not resolved before the beginning of the school
39               year, may be filed as a grievance two weeks before the first day of school. All time limits shall be enforced
40               at that time.

41   i.   Labor Relations Administrator/CFT Field Representative Meetings

42        The Superintendent’s designee for Labor Relations and the Federation Field Representatives shall meet bi-weekly
43        to discuss outstanding grievances and/or other contractual issues. Attempts to resolve any outstanding issues
44        should, as a professional courtesy, be discussed with the principal before a grievance is filed.


                                                                                                                             48
                                                                                                        §300 Grievance Procedure
 1   3.   Procedure

 2        a.    Level One

 3              A grievance must be filed in writing with the principal or the appropriate administrator within fifteen (15) days
 4              after said event, upon which it is based, or within fifteen (15) days after said event could reasonably be assumed to
 5              have been known by either a teacher or the Federation. The grievance conference shall occur within five (5) days
 6              after the grievance is filed. The grievant shall be accompanied by the Federation Building Representative or any
 7              other Federation representative of the grievant's choosing. The principal or appropriate administrator shall render a
 8              written decision within five (5) days of the grievance conference.

 9        b.    Level Two

10              In the event a grievance has not been satisfactorily resolved at Level One, the Federation shall file, within ten days
11              of the principal's or the appropriate administrator's written decision at Level One, a completed copy of the
12              grievance with the Superintendent or his/her designee. Within seven (7) days after such written grievance is filed,
13              the grievant, the Federation, and the Superintendent or his/her designee should meet to resolve the grievance. The
14              Superintendent or his/her designee shall file his/her decision within five (5) days of the Level Two meeting and
15              communicate it to the grievant and the Federation.

16              At the request of either the Board or the Federation, grievance mediation shall occur prior to the Level Two
17              grievance conference. The Board and Federation shall agree, by October 1, 1994, on an agency, individual, or
18              panel to provide such mediation services. The parties shall develop specific procedures for grievance mediation,
19              with the assistance of the mediator.

20              If grievance mediation is requested, time limits are suspended until the mediation occurs. A formal Level Two
21              conference shall be conducted within 5 days of the final mediation session, unless the grievance is resolved
22              through mediation. Thereafter, the normal time limits shall be observed.

23        c.    Level Three

24              If the grievance has not been satisfactorily resolved at Level Two, the Federation may demand arbitration within
25              90 days of receiving the Level Two decision. The arbitrator's decision shall be final and binding.

26              (1)    The Board and the Federation shall agree on a panel of five (5) arbitrators to hear and decide cases for one
27                     (1) year on a rotating basis.

28              (2)    The arbitrator selected to consider a particular grievance shall be that arbitrator next in order of rotation
29                     who can schedule the hearing with the parties within thirty (30) days.

30              (3)    The parties shall accept a date(s) offered within the 30 days or as soon thereafter as dates are available,
31                     unless the time limit is extended by mutual agreement. Unavailability of the parties’ representatives shall
32                     not be a valid reason for refusing all such dates offered by arbitrators on the panel.

33              (4)    If more than one arbitration hearing is pending at any time, the date of the initial filing of the grievance
34                     shall determine the order of rotation of the arbitrators.

35              (5)    After any arbitrator on the panel has rendered an award, either party, within fourteen (14) days, may
36                     remove such arbitrator from the panel. In addition, if either party so requests by August 1 of any school
37                     year, one or more arbitrators shall be removed from the panel. In either event, the parties shall attempt to
38                     agree on additional arbitrator(s) to complete the panel. If the parties are unable to agree on additional
39                     arbitrator(s) within fourteen (14) days of the removal of an arbitrator from the panel, the parties shall
40                     request a list or lists, as the case may be, of seven (7) arbitrators each from the Federal Mediation and
41                     Conciliation Service. The parties shall then alternately strike names from the list(s) until the number of
42                     arbitrators remaining equals the number needed to complete the panel of five (5) arbitrators.

43              (6)    The arbitrator shall not have the authority to alter, modify, add to or subtract from any of the terms of this
44                     contract.

45              (7)    The costs for the services of the arbitrator shall be shared equally by both parties.

46              (8)    Post-hearing briefs, if any, shall be filed within twenty (20) days of the receipt of transcript, or within
47                     twenty (20) days of the close of the hearing if no transcript is ordered. The arbitrator shall render a

     49
                                                                                                §300 Grievance Procedure
 1               decision in writing within thirty (30) days after post-hearing briefs have been submitted or within thirty
 2               (30) days after the hearing, if no briefs are to be filed.

 3        (9)    The Arbitrator’s decision shall be final and binding upon the Board, Federation, and grievant(s). Within 30
 4               days after receiving an arbitrator's written opinion, the Board of Education shall ratify and initiate
 5               implementation of the decision of the arbitrator.

 6   d.   Teacher Termination

 7        Binding arbitration is provided at Level Two upon waiver of statutory proceedings by the affected teacher on all
 8        teacher dismissal cases. Dismissal of an apprentice teacher is covered under the provisions of TES guidelines, not
 9        by this provision.

10   e.   Teacher Non-Renewal (5 years satisfactory service)

11        A non-tenured teacher who has completed five consecutive years of satisfactory or better service has the right to
12        file a grievance challenging the Board's decision not to renew his/her contract and to pursue that grievance to final
13        and binding arbitration.

14   f.   Teacher Non-Renewal (less than 5 years service)

15        In lieu of statutory proceedings, a non-tenured teacher with less than 5 consecutive years of satisfactory or better
16        service shall have the right to a hearing before a Board appointed referee, selected by agreement between the
17        Board and the Federation to hear such appeals, provided the teacher submits a written request to the
18        Superintendent for such a hearing within 10 days of receiving written notice of the Superintendent's
19        recommendation not to re-employ the teacher. The appointed referee may serve no longer than one year, unless
20        the parties agree to extend his/her appointment.

21        Such hearings shall be held before the Board acts on the Superintendent's recommendation not to re-employ the
22        teacher. However, the teacher's request for a hearing shall automatically extend the deadline for notification of
23        non-renewal through May 31.

24        At the hearing, the Superintendent, or his/her designee, shall summarize the teacher's evaluation and the reasons
25        for the non-renewal recommendation and shall present any supporting documentation or witnesses within two
26        hours and the teacher shall have the opportunity to present his/her appeal along with any supporting
27        documentation or witnesses within a two-hour period. The teacher shall have the right to representation by the
28        Federation.

29        The decision of the referee shall be in the form of a recommendation to the Board of Education.

30   g.   Alternate Procedure

31        Certain grievances filed by teachers regarding personnel decisions shall be assigned to an alternate internal dispute
32        resolution procedure for a prompt, final, and binding decision if the grievance is not resolved at Level I. Such
33        grievances are those that involve applying contract language to a specific incident or administrative decision and
34        in which the meaning or intent of contract provisions is not in dispute. Grievances eligible for this procedure shall
35        include those which contest an assignment, surplussing, or placement decision, layoff or recall decision, selection
36        of a teacher for ESP positions or for eligibility lists, provided the above stipulations apply. This procedure shall
37        not apply to cases, which involve discipline or dismissal.

38        Grievances assigned to this procedure shall be considered by an internal appeals panel, consisting of 2 teachers
39        appointed by the Federation and 2 administrators appointed by the Superintendent. In the event of a tie vote of the
40        panel, the grievant shall have immediate access to Level Three of the grievance procedure.

41        On the Thursday and Friday two weeks before the end of each quarter, the Alternate Grievance Panel shall meet to
42        resolve outstanding grievances. In addition, the Thursday and Friday two weeks before the opening of school, the
43        Alternate Grievance Panel shall meet to resolve outstanding grievances filed during the summer. Other dates may
44        be agreed to by the CFT and the Board. The grievant, the Federation, and the administration shall be responsible
45        for providing pertinent information and documents to the panel members at least 5 days prior to the hearing. Such
46        information shall include any data relevant to the case.

47        The panel shall consider the documentary evidence, hear testimony from any witnesses offered by the parties, and
48        render a final and binding decision, including an appropriate remedy, consistent with the terms of this contract, at

                                                                                                                            50
                                                                                                         §300 Grievance Procedure
 1                 the close of the hearing. Neither party shall be represented by attorneys, except by mutual consent, but the grievant
 2                 shall be entitled to representation by the Federation and the administration shall be appropriately represented. If
 3                 any panel member has a conflict of interest in any grievance, they shall be temporarily replaced by the appropriate
 4                 party.

 5                 The parties shall arrange appropriate training for members of the panel. The panel shall determine any other
 6                 procedures it may require, subject to approval of the parties. Either party may terminate the entire alternate
 7                 procedure described above by giving 30 days notice to the other party of its intention to terminate the procedure.
 8                 In the event the procedure is terminated, all pending cases shall be assigned to Level Two of the grievance
 9                 procedure.

10   4.     Mediation for Lawsuits

11          In the event of a lawsuit between the parties, mediation shall occur at the request of either party, using the same service
12          and procedure as in grievance mediation or using another dispute resolution procedure agreed to by the parties.

13   5.     Common Grievance/Arbitration Record

14          The parties shall compile a common record of grievance activity. The record shall include all grievances filed, dates, a
15          general statement of the issue, dates of grievance conferences, and dates of decisions at each step, and a statement of the
16          final outcome. The data shall be reported annually to the Superintendent, Federation President, and Board of Education.
17          The parties shall each designate a representative to be responsible for monitoring the compilation and reporting of this
18          data. Decisions of the Alternate Grievance Panel and arbitration decisions shall be jointly reported by the Federation and
19          the Board.
20   §400                                                                                                                     PUPILS

21   1.     Student Discipline

22          a.     Compliance with District Code of Conduct and State Law

23                 The suspension, expulsion, or removal of students shall be made in strict compliance with ORC 3313.661 and
24                 3313.66 and Board Policies 5144 and 5113.2. The principal shall immediately notify the police when a criminal
25                 offense is committed which endangers the safety of students, staff, or others.

26          b.     Administrative Support of Teacher

27                 The Board and Federation agree that consistent enforcement of clear and specific rules are vital to maintaining a
28                 safe and orderly learning environment. The classroom teacher shall have the full support of the Board in
29                 maintaining classroom discipline. Professional support services shall be provided to insure that every student's
30                 opportunity for an education is protected.

31          c.     Self-Defense

32                 A teacher may use such force as shall be reasonable and necessary to protect himself/herself from attack, to
33                 prevent school property from damage and/or destruction, and/or to prevent possible injury to another person.

34          d      Local School Behavior Plan

35                 The Superintendent shall require that each school adopt and follow a local school discipline policy to supplement
36                 Board policies. It shall include rules for student conduct, consequences of violating such rules, responsibilities of
37                 parents, teachers, administrators, and other staff. It shall address class cutting and truancy, including a plan for
38                 prompt communication with parents when students have cut class or are absent without a valid explanation. It
39                 shall include pre-suspension options and make use of alternate placement options provided by the Board.

40                 The local school behavior plan shall be developed by the ILT and aligned with the current district strategies.
41                 Student representatives, where appropriate, shall be added. The plan shall be reviewed and approved annually,
42                 with or without revisions, by the ILT.

43                 This shall be reduced to writing for the school and distributed to faculty on the first teacher workday of the school
44                 year and to students and parents by the first day of the second week of the school year.



     51
                                                                                                                         §400 Pupils
 1        e.     Removal of Disruptive Students

 2              A teacher shall have the right to remove from class pupils exhibiting disruptive behavior with reasons submitted in
 3              writing as soon as possible. Disruptive behavior includes the use of violence, force, coercion, threat, harassment,
 4              serious insubordination, or repeated acts of misbehavior, any of which cause disruption or obstruction to the
 5              educational process. The right to remove students for cause extends to all curricular and extracurricular activities
 6              affecting teachers while acting in the course of their employment.

 7              Once removed, a student will not be returned to class until disciplinary action has been determined, specified in
 8              writing.

 9        f.     Chronically Disruptive Students

10              The lead psychologist and/or the Student Services managers assigned to the Instructional Support Teams will
11              work with the school psychologist and teacher(s) to develop a transition plan for students returning from A2E,
12              A2S, and other non-school assignments that will include additional support services as determined to be
13              appropriate. The same personnel will also work with teachers to develop appropriate strategies for tier 3 students
14              who have exhibited persistent and disruptive behaviors.

15              CFT and the Board agree to work collaboratively to strengthen professional development and to expand
16              alternative placement centers for chronically disruptive students within the law.

17        g.     Student Discipline Reports

18              The Board shall provide quarterly to the Federation school-by-school reports of suspensions and expulsions
19              including the offenses committed.

20        h.     Assistance for Classroom Management

21              Individual staff members who are experiencing serious difficulty in classroom management, impacting upon
22              student discipline and learning, shall receive assistance from both the local school and district resources, including
23              lead teachers at the school. Visitations should be arranged in order for the teacher to observe well-managed
24              classes. Such assistance may be mandated by the principal or voluntarily requested by the teacher. In either case
25              the assistance should be provided promptly.

26   2.   Teacher Assault by Student

27        a.     Recommendation, Report, and Hearing

28              A student who physically assaults a teacher, who is performing a duty in the line of employment, including
29              extracurricular activities, shall be immediately suspended, and a recommendation for expulsion shall be made to
30              the Superintendent by the building/unit administrator. The teacher suffering from assault shall submit written facts
31              of the incident to the building/unit administrator and Federation building representative.

32              The principal shall immediately report any alleged physical assault by a student on a teacher to the
33              Superintendent’s designated hearing officer and the SRO. The principal shall also submit to the Superintendent’s
34              designated hearing officer and to the school resource officer the results of his/her investigation and the disciplinary
35              action taken or recommended. The principal or assistant superintendent shall provide copies of all such reports to
36              the teacher and to the Federation.

37              In the case of an assault on a teacher by a student, the Superintendent’s designated hearing officer shall conduct
38              the expulsion hearing and shall make a recommendation to the Superintendent. The teacher shall be notified of the
39              date, time, and place of the hearing and shall have the right to be present. The teacher shall be entitled to
40              representation by the Federation at such hearing. To the extent permitted by law, a student who the principal has
41              recommended for expulsion may not return to school prior to the hearing. The hearing shall be conducted within
42              10 days of the student’s suspension.

43              After considering the results of the teacher’s report of the incident, the results of the investigation, and the
44              Superintendent’s designated hearing officer’s recommendations, the Superintendent shall expel any student who
45              has physically assaulted a teacher to the extent allowed by law. If a student appeals the Superintendent's expulsion
46              order arising from an assault on a teacher to the Board of Education or to a Board appointed referee, the Board
47              shall notify the teacher and the Federation of such appeal and of the date, time, and place of the hearing. The
48              teacher shall be entitled to representation by the Federation at such hearing.

                                                                                                                                    52
                                                                                                                       §400 Pupils
 1        b.    Assistance in Student Assault Cases

 2              The Administration shall:

 3              1.     Obtain information from the building/unit administrator and investigating police officer concerning the
 4                     case and designate a liaison between the teacher and all parties operating in the case.

 5              2.     Immediately notify the teacher of his/her right to file charges against the student, and to inform him/her of
 6                     the procedure to be followed. If the teacher files charges against the student, a representative of the
 7                     administration, upon request, shall be present for any court hearing or proceeding arising from the charge.

 8              3.     Provide the teacher with released time for court appearances stemming from his/her professional activities.

 9              4.     Ensure that the teacher does not lose compensation or accumulated leave.

10              5.     Assist a teacher who is required to appear in court for an action taken in the exercise of duty to the extent
11                     of legal limits. In civil matters, the Board's insurance carrier shall represent the teacher through legal
12                     counsel and shall coordinate legal representation with attorneys appointed by the Federation or its
13                     insurance carrier. The teacher shall receive compensation for absence from duty for a court proceeding or
14                     administrative hearing when such an absence arises from a justifiable line of duty action on the part of a
15                     teacher.

16   3.   Pupil Adjustment

17        a.    Intervention Based Services and Supports

18              Each school should have a fully functioning intervention assistance team (IAT) that includes a general educator,
19              intervention specialist, parent of the child in question, building administrator, and the appropriate related service
20              provider, as needed. All activities related to the functioning of this team must be in compliance with the Ohio
21              Operating Standards. All referrals for multi-factored evaluations will be consistent with the Ohio Model
22              Procedures and the Operating Standards for Ohio’s Schools Serving Children with Disabilities.

23        b.    Multifactored Evaluation Referral

24              When a teacher submits a referral for multifactored evaluation and the Intervention Assistance Team deems it
25              appropriate, a request for parent approval shall be sought immediately. If parental approval is obtained, the
26              principal shall ensure that the forms are forwarded to the Department of Student Services.

27        c.    Make-Up Work

28              The opportunity to make up class work as a result of an unexcused absence is at the discretion of the teacher and
29              the principal. However, the Local School Discipline plan may require teachers to provide assignments to students
30              assigned to in-school suspension, under procedures included in the local school discipline plan. Further, teachers
31              are expected to provide assignments for students who are suspended or expelled for more than 3 but less than 16
32              days, if requested by the parent, guardian, or the parent or guardian’s designee, or an adult student. Teachers will
33              also provide make-up work to students suspended for 1 to 3 days, upon their return, if requested by the student, a
34              parent or guardian.

35              Suspensions and expulsions may be scheduled so that students are permitted to attend school for the purpose of
36              taking exams or demonstrating proficiency required for promotion, provided the student does not pose a physical
37              threat to other students, teachers, or staff.

38              Administrative procedures for implementing these provisions shall be reviewed by the EIP.

39        d.    Informing Teacher of Student Needs

40              All staff members who have a legitimate educational interest should be provided with information regarding a
41              child’s unique educational and behavioral needs. All staff members will respect the confidentiality rights of all
42              students.




     53
                                                                                                                    §400 Pupils
 1   e.   Informing Teacher of Problem

 2        A teacher who is assigned a pupil known to have a physical, social or emotional problem shall be informed by the
 3        administrator or counselor of the nature of the problem. The teacher shall also take reasonable steps to understand
 4        the nature of the problem and work with the student in a professional manner.

 5   f.   Administrator Present in Building

 6        For the protection of both pupils and teachers, there shall be an administrator or his/her designee present when the
 7        building is open. If the building administrator is absent longer than five days and if his/her designee is a teacher,
 8        that teacher shall be relieved of teaching responsibility.

 9   g.   Student Absence

10        Progress reports shall include a mark or symbol to indicate that a student was denied credit or is failing due to
11        excessive absence.

12   h.   Grading and Promotion

13        Teachers are responsible for the assignment of quarterly grades, the assignment of rubric scores and portfolio
14        scores on promotional grids and promotion or retention decisions as well as placement decisions at non-
15        promotional grades. Teachers and district administration shall communicate to students and their parents the
16        performance standards students must meet, the meaning of district assessment scores and how grades and rubric
17        scores are determined. Teachers are expected to have documentation for grades and rubric scores assigned.

18        The teacher's promotion/retention decision (K-8) or report card grade may not be changed by the principal. If a
19        dispute arises, the teacher and principal shall attempt to resolve it through a collaborative effort between all parties
20        involved. However, if the dispute is not resolved and the principal believes that the teacher's grade or decision is in
21        violation of district policy or is not justified, the principal may request that the Department of Quality
22        Improvement appoint a district audit team composed of teachers. The team shall examine the teacher's
23        documentation and may, if additional evidence is needed, evaluate the student's proficiency using teacher
24        certifiable and/or product rubrics by examining the student’s portfolio as well as other student work the teacher
25        may have. Audit teams shall be trained by the Department of Quality Improvement and shall apply defined
26        procedures and criteria, including district curriculum and promotion standards. Such procedures and criteria shall
27        be made available to the parent(s), principal and teacher involved in any grading or promotion/retention dispute
28        upon request. The audit team may uphold or modify the grade or promotion/retention decision. Decisions of the
29        audit team are final.

30        The administration shall ensure that every teacher assigned to a teaching position that requires completion of
31        promotion grids shall complete appropriate training in regard to district promotion standards and the use of such
32        grids. Such training shall also be made available to any other teacher who requests it.

33   i.   Due Dates for Grades

34        Quarter and semester grades and attendance reports shall not be due in the school office before noon on the second
35        teacher workday following the last workday of each quarter, except that fourth quarter grades and reports may be
36        due at the end of fourth quarter Records Day.

37   j.   Pupils in Building

38        All pupils who are not under the direction of a staff member or Board designee shall be out of the building within
39        fifteen (15) minutes of the close of school.

40   k.   Student Transportation/Excess Liability Insurance

41        The Board shall continue to provide the excess liability insurance coverage for a teacher in his/her automobile
42        whenever that teacher transports a student(s) in his/her automobile in the course of any school related activity.

43   l.   Student Cumulative Records

44        Student cumulative records for students changing from one Cincinnati Public School to another shall be available
45        in the receiving school not later than 10 working days after the student has been enrolled. Upon receipt of the
46        cumulative record for the student, the teachers of the student shall be notified.

                                                                                                                               54
                                                                                                                           §500 Staffing

 1   §500                                                                                                                    STAFFING

 2   1.     Teacher/Pupil Ratio

 3          The Board will establish a system-wide teacher/pupil ratio of 51 or 51.5 teachers, subject to final review and agreement
 4          by the parties, including educational service personnel, per 1000 regular program pupils based on an average daily
 5          membership (1/2 kindergarten membership and membership in grades 1 through 12 in regular programs, all as defined in
 6          Section 3317.02, et seq. of the Ohio Revised Code) as of the first full school week on October of each school year.

 7   2.     Class Size Reduction

 8          The Cincinnati Public Schools respect the research that suggests that small classes in early grades have lasting benefits on
 9          student achievement. The class size in the primary (K-3) grades would be 18 to 1 (ratio not implied) with an IA added in
10          each class that reaches 19 students and a cap of 25 students in individual teachers’ classrooms. Overload pay will be given
11          to these teachers for classes with 26, 27, and 28 students beginning the third quarter, and no primary classroom will
12          exceed 28 students during the second semester. Every effort will be made to minimize multi-age/combination classes with
13          the exception of Montessori Schools or any other planned and properly approved multi-age/combination program focus.

14   3.     Class Size Limits
15

31          In grades 7-12 no more than 150 students per day shall be assigned to any academic teacher. Specialists who teach 5
32          periods shall be assigned no more than 180 secondary students per day. Specialists who teach 6 classes shall be assigned
33          no more than 200 secondary students per day.

34          Academic classes shall be defined as: reading; English; math; science; social studies; and foreign language.

35          For reasons of health and safety of students, Industrial Arts classes shall be treated as an academic class for the purpose of
36          class size.

37          No teacher in grades 4 through 12 shall be assigned more than 4 students above the limit. Teachers in grades 4-12 who are
38          assigned 3 to 4 students above the limit shall be assigned an instructor assistant and the right to receive any overload
39          payment shall cease.
40
41          Teachers in grades 4-12 who are assigned 1 to 2 students over the limit shall receive an overload payment of $135.00 per
42          student per instructional hour per year at the conclusion of the school year.

13          Class size limits shall not apply to band and choir.

14          Summer school teachers assigned students above the class size limits shall be eligible for overload pay under guidelines
15          determined by the Teacher Allocation Committee.

16   4.     Enforcement Procedures

17          Enforcement procedures for class size limits shall be as follows:

18          The Teacher Allocation Committee shall continue to monitor class size at all district schools and shall advise the schools
19          on steps they can take to correct violations of class size limits. The committee may authorize re-assignment of teachers
20          through the third Monday after Labor Day. In exceptional cases where a school is unable to organize classes within the
21          limits, the committee shall have the authority to allocate additional funds above per pupil allocations up to a district wide
22          limit of $700,000.

23          The Board shall not be obligated to provide more than $115,560 in overload payments annually.

24          The committee may adopt guidelines governing the payment of overload pay and the allocation of instructor assistants to
25          overload classes specified above.

26          A grievance may be filed on adherence to the process, on hiring at the ratio in §500.1 above and on establishing a reserve
27          pool, but not on the educational soundness of a decision to allocate or not to allocate any teachers to any school. A
28          grievance cannot be filed on an issue as to which the committee was unable to reach a decision.
29   §605                                                                         EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT PERSONNEL (ESP)

30   1.     General Coordination of Support Staff

31          a.     Caseload

32                 Speech pathologists, school social workers, and psychologists shall each form an assignment committee consisting
33                 of no more than three administrators for that discipline and three members appointed by the practitioners in that
34                 discipline. Each committee shall develop and recommend to the responsible administrator designated by the
35                 Superintendent assignment of schools and caseloads within that discipline. Such assignments shall, to the extent
36                 possible, provide for equitable distribution. Each committee shall review caseloads periodically.

37                 In any school, which has more than one counselor, counselors shall meet, at least annually, with the principal or
38                 designee, for the purpose of assigning caseloads. To the extent possible, caseloads shall be assigned on an
39                 equitable basis.

40          b.     Facilities

41                 All counselors, psychologists, and school social workers shall be provided in each school with a telephone and
42                 adequate office space in a private setting, within existing facilities, for the purpose of conducting conferences and
43                 evaluations.



                                                                                                                                          56
                                                                                         §605 Educational Support Personnel (ESP)
 1   2.     Speech Pathologists

 2          Speech pathologists shall receive 7 hours released time for every increment of 30 students for the purpose of preparing
 3          IEP's, rounded to the nearest one half day. Speech pathologists shall have the same preparation time as load bearing
 4          teachers.

 5   3.     School Psychologists

 6          a.     Vacancies, Transfers, and Assignments

 7                 There are presently three general categories of School Psychologists.

 8                 (1)     School Psychologists
 9                 (2)     Auxiliary Services School Psychologists
10                 (3)     Special Program Positions

11                 When a vacancy occurs in any of these three categories, the vacancy may be filled by present psychologists
12                 according to the transfer procedures of the contract.

13                 Assignment of psychologists in the general category shall be made according to provisions of Paragraph 1.a.
14                 above.

15   4.     School Social Workers

16          Any extension to the 191-day contract of educational support personnel is at the discretion of the school hiring the person
17          and/or the district for specific assignment.

18          At a minimum each school shall have access to social worker, counselor services or lead SSW at .2 (2/10)

19   5.     Other Staff

20          Occupational therapists, physical therapists, audiologists and orientation mobility instructors shall provide service and
21          supports to students in accordance with the Operating Standards for Ohio’s Schools Serving Children with Disabilities.
22          Occupational therapists, physical therapists and orientation mobility instructors shall have the same preparation time as
23          load bearing teachers.
24   §610                                                                                                       SPECIAL TEACHERS

25   1.     Special Education

26          All Intervention Specialists shall provide a wide array of supports and services within a comprehensive service delivery
27          model as outlined in the Operating Standards for Ohio’s Schools Serving Children with Disabilities. A wide array of
28          supports and services (direct and indirect) includes but is not limited to the following: consultation, individual instruction,
29          large group instruction, small group instruction, whole class instruction, team-teaching, inclusive practices, etc.
30          Intervention Specialists shall be afforded the same rights and responsibilities as all other bargaining members.

12                       One instructional assistant is to be assigned to the instructional classroom of the intervention specialist, where
13                       there is a combination of one or more Emotionally Disturbed students with one or more Orthopedic, Other Health
