15                       No more than six students with disabilities shall be assigned to a general education class for inclusion unless some
16                       staff assistance is provided to assist the general education teacher.

17             c.        Placing Students in Classes

18                       All students with disabilities should have an active and up-to-date IEP that outlines all provisions regarding their
19                       special education and related services. Students with disabilities shall not be placed in a special education class
20                       unless there is written documentation of the student's disability and the student has, at minimum, a temporary IEP.
21                       The placement team shall then write an IEP within the time specified in applicable state regulations.

22                       Primary and intermediate students with disabilities shall not be assigned to the same special education
23                       instructional period.

24                       The Department of Student Services compliance administrator shall employ teachers as needed, at the extended
25                       employment rate, to assist with placement of units and students and with other compliance activities. Intervention
26                       Specialist lead teachers shall have preference for these assignments.

27             d.        IEP’s

28                       Intervention Specialists are responsible for facilitating the annual completion (throughout the school year) of all
29                       Individual Education Programs (IEPs) for every student on their caseload. All IEPs are to be submitted by the
30                       annual due date to the Department of Student Services immediately upon completion. Each intervention specialist
31                       who is responsible for preparing more than six IEP’s shall be assigned two “IEP workdays” annually, during
32                       which a substitute teacher will be provided. These workdays are to provide time for the intervention specialist to
33                       prepare for and/or participate in IEP conferences and shall be scheduled prior to the deadline for submission of
34                       IEP’s.

35                       Further, any teacher responsible for writing IEP's in excess of the enrollment limit as of February 1 shall be
36                       entitled to an IEP workday in addition to the two (2) days provided by e. above.

37
38        e.        Alternate Assessments
39
40                  The district will offer a half-day of training on the alignment of IEPs, academic standards, and alternate assessments at
41                  the beginning of the school year. In addition, a full day will be offered by the district for professional development or
42                  completion of alternate assessments, centrally or at the school, as deemed appropriate by the teacher. Class coverage
43                  will be provided by the school for both sessions, prior to the due date for submitting alternate assessments.

44             f. Case Coordinators

45                       A Case Coordinator shall be appointed at each school which has a caseload, defined as follows. Caseloads include
46                       students identified as disabled and students with suspected disabilities, including students in the school’s
47                       attendance zone who attend non-public schools or pre-school classes, but excluding cases managed by district
48                       teachers or educational support assigned to non-public schools.

49                       A credentialed lead teacher (intervention specialist) or a lead counselor, school social worker, or school
50                       psychologist shall receive priority consideration for the position. If none are available, an intervention specialist, a

     59
                                                                                                             §610 Special Teachers
 1              counselor, school social worker, speech-language pathologist, or school psychologist shall be appointed. If none
 2              are available, a general education teacher may be appointed.

 3              Case coordinators shall be appointed from applicants by a selection panel appointed by the ILT, which includes
 4              the principal, intervention specialist and general education teacher(s).

 5              Case Coordinators shall receive supplemental pay at an annual rate according to a schedule, caseload, and
 6              compensation guidelines agreed upon by the parties by June 1, 1997 for the term of the contract, based upon the
 7              caseload.

 8              A Case Coordinator who is also appointed as a Intervention Specialist Lead Teacher at the school shall be eligible
 9              for additional compensation as Case Coordinator only if the school has more than the number of students
10              designated by the parties on his/her caseload in addition to identified disabled students in attendance at the school.
11              Such compensation shall not exceed an amount agreed to by the parties as provided in the schedule described
12              above.

13              Case Coordinators shall be paid from a pool of money in an amount to be negotiated by the parties by June 30,
14              1997.

15              The administration shall collaborate with members of CFT for the purpose of reviewing the case coordinator
16              position and recommending improvements. In the absence of an agreed upon resolution, the existing contract will
17              remain in effect.

18        g.     Special Education Reopener

19              If the State of Ohio adopts legislation that mandates substantial changes in the design of the Special Education
20              Program, the parties shall reopen regarding the impact on terms and conditions of employment.

21   2.   Career Technical Education

22        All career technical teachers who are required by state standards to have extended employment and are not on an
23        extended contract shall be paid their daily rate of pay for such employment.

24   3.   Pre-School Teachers

25        a.     Teacher Workday

26              The workday for pre-school teachers shall be seven hours, including a 30-minute duty-free lunch and 30 minutes
27              daily for preparation and/or conference time. The standard work year for pre-school teachers shall be the same as
28              for other teachers.

29        b.     Benefits and Leave

30              Pre-school teachers shall enjoy the same fringe benefits, holidays, personal leave, and sick leave as other teachers.

31        c.     Salaries

32              Pre-school instructors shall be placed on Salary Schedule C under the same provisions as other teachers.

33        d.     Budget

34              Pre-school teachers shall be informed of the supply equipment and materials budget for their program and may
35              submit requests for such funds.

36        e.     Seniority

37              For pre-school teachers, seniority shall be defined as follows:

38              i.        total number of years of continual service in the CPS as a pre-school instructor or contract teacher
39              ii.       total number of years in the building of current placement
40              iii.      total number of years in a pre school program (e.g. ESEA Chapter I, Headstart, or others)


                                                                                                                                   60
                                                                                                            §610 Special Teachers
 1          f.     Grant Opportunities
 2
 3                 The Board and Federation agree to develop a district-wide Preschool Advisory Committee to review grant
 4                 opportunities and funding implementation on an annual basis.

 5          g.     Pre-School Re-opener
 6                 Due to the many changes in state and federal requirements for preschool under consideration, the board and CFT
 7                 agreed to include a re-opener in the contract if needed to enable CPS to apply and compete successfully for grants
 8                 to preschool programs.

 9   4.     Work-Study Coordinators

10          Work-study coordinators shall work 5 days following the close of school. The schedule for such days shall be approved
11          by her/his supervisor. By September 20, each work-study coordinator shall identify 5 days during the school year s/he
12          will not report to school subject to approval of their supervisor. Otherwise, the supervisor of the work-study coordinator
13          shall identify the 5 days. No two days may fall in the same month nor be consecutive. Other than for reasons of
14          separation, the work-study coordinator shall receive paychecks and accrue sick leave as if those days had been served.

15   5.     Summer School Teachers

16          a.     In schools that operate a summer school program for their own students, principals shall select teachers for
17                 summer school positions from among applicants within the school. Positions not filled by teachers at the school
18                 shall be announced throughout the district. Preference shall be given to lead and career teachers with the
19                 appropriate certification, teaching within the level.

20                 For any summer school program operated by the district, positions will be announced throughout the district and
21                 teachers shall be selected on a district-wide basis. Preference shall be given to lead and career teachers with the
22                 appropriate certification, teaching within the level.

23          b.     Summer school teachers assigned to teach 3 or more hours per day shall be assigned one 45-minute preparation
24                 and/or conference period daily.

25          c.     Evaluation procedures, if any, for summer school teachers shall be negotiated by the Board and the Federation.

26          d.     Summer school salaries are governed by Appendix A, Schedule G.

27          e.     Summer school teachers shall be entitled to use accrued sick leave or personal leave on the same basis as contract
28                 teachers during the regular school year. However, any absence of more than 3 days during the first week of
29                 summer school may result in loss of the position.

30          f.     If a reduction in the number of summer school teachers in a summer school operated by the district becomes
31                 necessary after the beginning of summer school, summer school teachers shall be released within the level based
32                 on certification and seniority, beginning with the least senior, except that career and lead teachers shall receive
33                 priority for retention of positions.

34                 If a reduction in the number of summer school teachers at a school becomes necessary after the beginning of
35                 summer school, the teachers shall be released from the school on the same basis as above.

36          g.     Upon request, the Board shall mail paychecks of summer school teachers to their home or summer address.

37          h.     In addition to the above, the following contract provisions apply to summer school teachers: §§100, 110, 120, 130,
38                 140, 160, 180, 200.1, 215 (1, 2, 3, 5), 240, 260, 300, 400, 500, 800, 810, 820, 900.
39   §620                                                                                                           SUBSTITUTES

40   1.     Definition

41          a.     Class I        Daily Rate Substitute

42                 Refers to a substitute who has indicated restrictions on his/her service or who has not qualified as a Class III
43                 substitute.



     61
                                                                                                                       §620 Substitutes
 1        b.      Class II       Daily Rate Substitute

 2                Refers to a substitute teacher who has been in an assignment for more than 10 but less than 21 days.

 3        c.      Class III      Daily Rate Substitute

 4                Refers to a substitute teacher who has indicated no restrictions on assignments and who agrees not to limit his/her
 5                service to any particular school(s), grade level(s), assignment(s), subject(s), day(s) of the week, or to a certain
 6                number of days.

 7                For purposes of this section, a refusal means declining any assignment prior to 30 minutes after the start of school
 8                or being unavailable for assignment between 6 am and 8 am two days in a ten-day period.

 9                If a Class III substitute teacher refuses any assignment more than two times in any quarter, they will be
10                reclassified as a Class I substitute teacher for 5 pay periods. At that time, one may reapply for Class III status. If
11                Class III status is lost a second time, one must wait until the following school year to reapply.

12                Personal illness and other absences outside the employee’s control will not be considered a refusal but will be
13                deducted from the substitute teacher’s accumulated sick leave and no compensation will be paid provided the
14                substitute teacher has leave. If no leave is available, such absence will be considered a refusal.

15        d.      Class IV       Daily Rate Building Substitute

16                A building substitute is a substitute teacher who is assigned to the same building daily and is available for
17                reassignment if necessary.

18        e.      Class V        Long-term Substitute

19                §620.10.a defines long-term substitutes and sets forward terms and conditions of employment. Long-term
20                substitutes are automatically terminated at the end of the school year.

21        f.      Hourly Rate

22                When an hourly rate is used, it shall be one-seventh of the substitute’s current daily rate, including sick leave
23                incentive, extended assignment rate and Class III status.

24        Building substitutes shall not replace another substitute who has been in an assignment 11 days or more unless the
25        building substitute is certified for the assignment and the original substitute is not. If a building substitute is assigned to a
26        long-term (21 days or more) assignment, a Class III substitute shall be assigned to the building each day the building
27        substitute is reassigned. However, if the building substitute fills a vacancy by March 1, which is expected to last until the
28        end of the school year, another building substitute shall be assigned to the school.

29   2.   Workday

30        a.     A substitute teacher day shall consist of 420 minutes, which includes a 30-minute duty-free lunch and no more
31               than 345 minutes subject to assignment in school.

32               However, in grades 7-12, a substitute shall not be assigned to teach more than 6 class periods per day and shall
33               enjoy a preparation period of 45 uninterrupted minutes or a class period daily, whichever is greater.

34               This provision will not apply in cases where a substitute teacher arrives late and the regular teacher’s preparation
35               time has passed nor will it apply to a substitute teacher who is only assigned for a half day.

36               Class II and Class V substitute teachers shall follow the normal daily schedule for that assignment.

37        b.     If a substitute agrees to be assigned duties for more than 345 minutes or teach one more class beyond the
38               requirement of paragraph 2a above (for grades 7-12), the substitute will be compensated at his/her current hourly
39               rate. Each additional class period taught will be considered an hour of time.

40        c.     If a substitute teacher’s required workday extends beyond 7 hours, the substitute will be compensated at his/her
41               current hourly rate to the nearest 15 minutes. Working day includes lunch, preparation, and travel time, if more
42               than one building is assigned.

                                                                                                                                        62
                                                                                                                     §620 Substitutes
 1        d.     When the principal assigns a substitute teacher additional time to confer with the absent teacher prior to or
 2               following a period of absence, such time will be paid at the substitute teacher’s current daily rate.

 3        e.     Records Day

 4               If a substitute teacher is assigned to grade exams, compute quarterly grades, or attendance records for an absent
 5               teacher, s/he will receive one half-day’s pay.

 6        f.     At a school, Class I Substitutes shall be placed in the assignments for which they were called, unless:

 7               (1)    reassigned in the same area as the original assignment. Areas are defined as academic, non-academic, or
 8                      special education.

 9               (2)    assignment for which called is no longer available.

10               (3)    called for one-half day but full day assignment is now available.

11               (4)    an insufficient number of substitute teachers are available in the building

12               (5)    reassigned in the substitute teacher’s area of certification

13               (6)    no specific assignment was designated

14               If the above conditions are not met, the substitute teacher may accept reassignment or “call in pay” as described
15                       above.

16        g.     §220.8.a (1), (2), (3), (4), Par 1 shall apply to building substitutes (Class IV) and Class II substitutes. §220.8.a (5)
17               shall apply to building substitutes only on a voluntary basis.

18        h.     Call in Pay

19               If a substitute teacher is assigned and subsequently not needed, an attempt will be made to reassign the substitute
20               teacher. If a reassignment is not available, the substitute teacher will be compensated for one-half day. The
21               principal may provide one-half day of appropriate work for the substitute teacher to perform with pay.

22               Class I and Class A substitutes may refuse reassignment without affecting their call in pay.

23   3.   Evaluation and Career Plan

24        a.     Evaluation

25               The substitute performance evaluation form used shall be that developed by a joint committee of Federation
26               representatives and administrators. Any revision in the form shall require the mutual consent of the parties.

27               If a performance evaluation summary is completed regarding a substitute, it must be accompanied by
28               documentation of the substitute teacher’s performance, including such items as classroom observation reports,
29               written reports, if any, from teacher(s) who the substitute has replaced, and other documentation relating to the
30               sub’s responsibilities at the school. If a substitute is rated less than satisfactory on classroom performance, the
31               evaluator(s) shall conduct at least one classroom observation sufficient in length to justify all conclusions reached.
32               The substitute shall receive a copy of all performance evaluations and may attach a rebuttal to any evaluation.

33               The Department of Human resources shall provide any substitute with an opportunity to discuss more than two
34               less-than-satisfactory performance evaluations.

35               Before a long-term substitute (Class V) who has served in an assignment 30 days or a building substitute (Class
36               IV) who has served as the building substitute in the building for more than 30 days is removed or dismissed due to
37               performance, a performance evaluation must be completed including documentation as described above. However,
38               such documentation shall include two classroom observations instead of the one referred to above.




     63
                                                                                                              §620 Substitutes
 1   b.   Voluntary Evaluation

 2        A Class III substitute may request that a substitute performance evaluation be completed provided that the
 3        substitute serves at least 30 days at the school during the school year or serves in a LTS assignment 30 days or
 4        more. The evaluation may be requested from up to two principals per school year and must be requested no later
 5        than ten days after completion of the 30 days provided the substitute is assigned in the building at least five days
 6        after the request. Such evaluations may be completed at various times during the school year but may not be
 7        requested after May 1. A building substitute may request an evaluation from his/her principal for the school year
 8        no later than November 30.

 9        At least two classroom observations, substantial enough in length to justify the conclusions reached, must be
10        completed as part of such evaluations. These observations may be conducted by the principal, assistant principal,
11        supervisor, or by a teacher designated by the principal who is certified in the same area as the substitute. (Note:
12        The Career in Teaching Program Agreement shall govern which teachers may perform this role.) However,
13        substitute performance evaluation shall be completed by the principal or assistant principal.

14   c.   Daily Reports

15        By September 1994, the Board and Federation will develop a two-part report whereby teachers and substitutes can
16        share information regarding workday(s).

17   d.   Appointment/Discipline/Dismissal

18        All substitute teacher appointments shall be for a school year or a portion thereof remaining after the date of
19        appointment with no expectation of continuing employment. Discipline and dismissal of substitute teachers during
20        the course of a school year shall be in accordance with §215 Par (1, 2, 3, 5). Adherence to the procedures
21        described in this section is subject to the Grievance procedure. However, a substitute teacher may not file a
22        grievance challenging the Board’s decision to dismiss said teacher.

23        Principals shall provide documentation to support any request that a particular substitute not return to their school
24        to be a substitute teacher.

25   e.   Training and Advancement

26        An inservice training program committee shall be developed for substitute teachers. The district-wide substitute
27        representatives shall provide recommendations regarding the content and other arrangements. If offered beyond
28        the workday, inservice sessions shall be voluntary, or, if attendance is required, paid at the substitute’s hourly rate.

29   f.   Continuing Education

30        Upon request, substitutes will be referred to local universities for information regarding certification and re-
31        certification. Career counseling will be available to all substitutes.

32   g.   Advancement

33        A list of proposed building substitute positions for the following school year shall be announced by May 1.
34        Substitutes shall be invited to submit an application indicating their interest in building substitutes (Class IV),
35        long-term substitute (Class V) positions, or Class III status for the following year.

36   h.   Career Plan

37        A request will be made by the Department of Human Resources of all substitutes with a standard teaching
38        certificate, by May 15, to ascertain if the substitute is interested in full-time employment. All substitutes having
39        answered yes will be required to submit a resume to be distributed to all appropriate principals. The resume will
40        include, but not be limited to, the following:

41        1)     Certification
42        2)     Experience
43        3)     Voluntary evaluations or observations
44        4)     Recommendation




                                                                                                                               64
                                                                                                                     §620 Substitutes
 1   4.   Sick Leave

 2        a.     Building Substitutes

 3               Building substitutes (Class IV) shall be eligible for sick leave on the same basis as regular teachers.

 4        b.     Other Daily Rate Substitutes

 5               All substitutes will accrue sick leave at the same rate as regular teachers.

 6               Classes I, II, and III substitutes may use accrued sick leave if s/he has been working at the same school or
 7               assignment for three consecutive workdays. However, a Class I, II, and III substitute may use no more than 3 days
 8               of sick leave in any 10-day period.

 9        c.     Sick Leave Conversion

10               Substitute teachers will have sick leave conversion upon retirement, pursuant to §700.4.s at the substitute’s final
11               daily rate of pay, but may not convert accumulated sick leave transferred from another employer.

12               For a substitute teacher who retires from the Cincinnati Public Schools but has previous service as a Cincinnati
13               Public School contract teacher, sick leave conversion shall be paid so that sick leave accumulated as a contract
14               teacher shall be paid at the teacher’s last contract salary; sick leave accumulated as a substitute shall be paid at the
15               final substitute rate.

16   5.   Attendance Incentives

17        An additional $2.00 a day daily rate substitute teachers who have an accumulated sick leave balance of 30 days earned as
18        a Cincinnati Public Schools daily rate substitute teacher will be paid for each day worked the following school year. This
19        determination will be made as of January 1, 1990 and each August 1 thereafter.

20        Effective beginning the 1989-90 school year, a lump sum payment of $2.00 per day worked will be paid to any retired
21        teacher who works 85 days. Such payment will be made by July 1.

22   6.   Appearance in Court

23        Class III, IV, and V substitute teachers who are absent in response to a subpoena in a (1) a court proceeding, or (2) an
24        administrative hearing, in which neither the substitute teacher nor a labor organization recognized by the Board is a party,
25        shall incur no loss in pay, benefits, or accrued leave subject only to a deduction of the amount of any witness fee or other
26        compensation in excess of $35 per day. §230.16.b shall also apply to daily rate substitute teachers. If the absence is longer
27        than one day, pay shall be based upon the average percentage of days worked during the previous two pay periods.

28        However, any substitute whose appearance arises from a justifiable line of duty action on the part of the substitute and
29        any substitute who is subpoenaed as a witness to an incident arising in the line of duty, shall be paid for those day(s) and
30        shall suffer no loss of pay, benefits, or accrued leave.

31   7.   Fringe Benefits

32        a.     Building substitutes are eligible the same health benefits and Term Life Insurance as other full-time teachers, by
33               making the same contribution.

34        b.     All substitutes who work 85 days during the school year shall receive a benefit bank deposit of $300 on
35               September 1, if they are currently employed by the Board in any capacity.

36        c.     There shall be a separate property damage fund for daily rate substitutes of $1,000 per year. This fund shall be
37               administered pursuant to §700.4.s If a surplus remains in the regular teacher fund, substitute teachers may apply
38               for such surplus.

39        d.     If a long-term substitute (Class V) has been in an assignment for at least 30 days of the last quarter and has served
40               to within 5 days of the end of the school year, s/he will not lose benefits during the summer recess.




     65
                                                                                                                     §620 Substitutes
 1   8.    Daily Rate Substitute Teacher List

 2         The Department of Human Resources shall maintain a list of substitute teachers by areas of certification noting grades,
 3         subjects and/or areas of greatest experience and shall make that list available to each school, updating it on a quarterly
 4         basis.

 5   9.    General Provisions

 6         In addition to paragraphs 1 through 8 of this section above, the following provisions of this contract apply to daily rate
 7         substitutes: §100 Term of Contract; §110 Recognition; §120 Fair Practices; §130 Federation Rights; §140 Personnel
 8         Files; §150 School Leadership; §160 General Provisions; §180 School Budgets; §220 Teaching Assignments, Par 6, 8,
 9         and 11; §230 Teacher Absence, Par 18; §240 Teaching Conditions; §300 Grievance Procedure; §400 Pupils; §700
10         Salaries/Fringe Benefits, Par 2,p and r, §800 Board Authority; §810 Amendment; §820 Legality; §900 Term of Contract;
11         and other provisions which are expressly applicable to daily rate substitutes or a particular class of daily rate substitute.
12         No other provisions apply.

13   10.   Long-Term Substitute Teachers

14         a.     Definition

15                Long-term Substitutes are defined as substitute teachers who serve on a temporary basis in a position for more
16                than 20 consecutive working days. The effective date of appointment shall be the 21st consecutive day of service
17                in a given position. If a substitute is filling a vacancy or if serving for a teacher who is absent and serves in the
18                position for more than 20 days, the pay shall be retroactive to the first day of the assignment. However, a
19                substitute may be appointed as a long-term substitute prior to the 21st day, whether serving in a vacancy or
20                replacing an absent teacher. If so, the substitute shall be paid as a long-term substitute beginning with the effective
21                date of the appointment and shall be paid, as stipulated above, for days served in the assignment prior to the date
22                of appointment. Consecutive workdays shall not be interrupted by the use of sick leave, assault leave, Federation
23                leave, or any other approved absence.

24         b.     Conditions for Employment

25                Long-term substitute teachers may be appointed only when one or more of the following conditions occur:

26                (1)     temporary positions created by absence of regular employees occur for periods of more than twenty
27                        consecutive working days;

28                (2)     the long-term substitute teacher does not meet minimum employment standards by training, references or
29                        interview performance or did not qualify for a standard Ohio certificate;

30                (3)     the long-term substitute is a retired Ohio teacher;

31                (4)     the long-term substitute teacher does not wish to make a commitment for the completion of the current
32                        school year;

33                (5)     a regular vacancy occurs subsequent to November 30.

34         c.     Dismissal

35                Long-term substitute teachers serve temporarily and are subject to dismissal:

36                (1)     when the performance is less than satisfactory in the judgment of the principal and supervisor;

37                (2)     upon return of the regular employee;

38                (3)     when a long-term substitute teacher was employed under Paragraph 10.b (2), above, and a fully qualified
39                        candidate is available;

40                (4)     at the conclusion of the school year if employed at that time.




                                                                                                                                      66
                                                                                                                     §620 Substitutes
 1          d.     Qualifications for Contract

 2                 Long-term substitute teachers who serve 120 or more days during a given school year and who are employed for a
 3                 regular vacancy for the ensuing school year for which they are fully qualified shall be given contracts. Long-term
 4                 substitute teachers who are employed as of the end of the school year and who served 120 consecutive working
 5                 days during the school year as a long-term substitute teacher and who are employed under contract at the
 6                 beginning of the ensuing school year shall receive seniority credit effective the date of last appointment as a long-
 7                 term substitute teacher.

 8          e.     Evaluation

 9                 Long-term substitute teachers shall be appraised using the substitute teacher evaluation process. However, long-
10                 term substitute teachers employed prior to December 1 shall be appraised using the standard evaluation process.

11          f.     Priority for Re-Employment

12                 Long-term substitute teachers shall be considered for re-employment after contract teachers who have been laid
13                 off, but before applicants who have not been employed as long-term substitute teachers during the previous school
14                 year.

15          g.     Salaries and Fringe Benefits

16                 Long-term substitute teachers' salaries and fringe benefits are governed by the provisions of the Collective
17                 Bargaining Contract applicable to contract teachers.

18   11.    Building Substitutes

19          An elementary school’s ILT may requisition a building substitute or arrange to share a building substitute with another
20          school, using its budget allocation.

21   12.    Availability of Substitutes

22          The parties recognize that maintaining an adequate pool of qualified substitute teachers requires continuous effort. The
23          Board shall actively recruit substitute teachers, including advertising in newspapers of general circulation.
24   §700                                                                                    SALARIES AND FRINGE BENEFITS

25   1.     Salary Increases

26          All salary schedules shall be increased by 1.0% effective January 1, 2007, except Schedule E.

27          All salary schedules shall be increased by 2.0% effective January 1, 2008, except Schedule E.

28          There will be an economic re-opener on January 1, 2009.

29          a.     Career Teacher Increment

30                 The annual salaries of teachers who qualified for the career teacher increment under the Career in Teaching
31                 Program Agreement between the parties, as amended by the parties June 14, 1999 Budget Reduction Agreement,
32                 shall be increased by $1000, in addition to any lead teacher increment. However, no additional teachers may
33                 qualify for the increment after September 1, 2000.

34          b.     Teacher Pay for NTBC/Professional Certification

35                 Any teacher attaining National Teacher Board Certification shall have $1000 added to his/her base salary, in
36                 addition to any salary supplement provided by the state, the next full school year the certification is in effect.

37                      •      Speech-language pathologists with national certification from the American Speech, Language, and
38                             Hearing Association are eligible for a $1,000 stipend.

39                 Pending the availability of new, additional operating funds, a $1000 stipend will be available for the following:


     67
                                                                                                    §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1                        •     Occupational Therapists with certification from American Occupational Therapy Association, Inc.;

 2                        •     Physical Therapists with certification from American Board of Physical Therapy Specialists;

 3                        •     School Psychologists with certification from National Association of School Psychologists; and

 4                        •     School Nurses with certification by the National Board for Certification of School Nurses.

 5        c.        Training Increments

 6                  The annual salaries of teachers who complete 100 hours of required or inservice instruction shall be increased by
 7                  $750. The annual salaries of teachers shall be increased by an additional $250 for each 100 completed additional
 8                  hours of such instruction. The increments shall be effective at the beginning of the school year following
 9                  completion of the coursework. However, no additional teachers may qualify for the increment after September 1,
10                  2000.

11             d.   Physical Therapist
12                  Beginning with the ratification of the 2004 contract, Physical Therapists will be hired at step four. Physical
13                  Therapists who have not reached step four prior to the ratification of the 2004 contract will be moved to step four.

14             e.   Recruitment and Retention
15
16                  The Superintendent or his designee may declare areas of shortage. Upon declaration, incentives to hire and retain
17                  teachers or related services staff in areas may be implemented by the Department of Human Resources. These
18                  may include:
19
20                  •     The November 2001 reimbursement program for teachers whose certificates are in a shortage area, when
21                        these teachers agree to be employed in the shortage area for at least three years in the district.
22                  •     Placement of new hires on the salary schedule for their level of experience up to 17 years of service when
23                        there is a 3-year agreement to be employed in the district.
24                  •     The Department of Human Resources may place speech-language pathologists and occupational therapists at
25                        step four if shortages exist.
26
27                  In addition, the 2001 reimbursement program detailed below remains an option to be decided by Human
28                  Resources:
29
30                  For new hires in the areas of identified teacher shortages, the district shall provide up to $2,000 per year, for up to
31                  three years for a maximum of $6,000, in areas of mathematics, science, and special education or other declared
32                  areas. This includes Professional Practice School interns. Current employees who completed re-certification in the
33                  areas of identified teacher shortages during the 2000-01 school years, and began teaching classes are also teaching
34                  classes in the areas of need. New hires returning to CPS after a hiatus of one or more years would be eligible to
35                  receive the incentive. These incentives will be contingent upon using the funds for the purposes listed below and
36                  subject to submission of receipts:
37
38                        •     Professional development for courses that improve one’s knowledge of subject taught
39                        •     Tuition reimbursement for courses that improve one’s knowledge in the subjects taught
40                        •     To repay student loans
41                        •     To reimburse new hires for expenses associated with relocation

42   2.   Salary Schedule

43        a.        Initial Position on Salary Schedule

44                  The initial salary of a teacher shall be the minimum on the schedule for which the teacher is qualified, plus any
45                  allowance due the teacher for prior teaching experience and/or military service. Allowance for prior teaching
46                  experience shall be made on the basis of:

47                  (1)       One (1) year of credit for each year of teaching experience up to a maximum of ten (10) years of which no
48                            more than three (3) years may be substitute teaching experience.

49                  (2)       Allowance for military service shall be made on the basis of one (1) year of credit for each year of military
50                            service up to a maximum of six (6) years.


                                                                                                                                        68
                                                                                              §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1             (3)    Allowance for a combination of prior teaching and military service shall be made on the basis of one (1)
 2                    year of credit for each year of military service up to a maximum of six (6) years, and prior teaching
 3                    experience up to a maximum of ten (10) years.

 4             (4)    School nurses shall receive credit for each year of school nursing experience up to a maximum of ten (10)
 5                    years.

 6             (5)    In determining the initial salary of a teacher of trade and industrial career technical subjects, a year of work
 7                    experience, either at the apprenticeship level or beyond, shall be accepted as a substitute for a year of
 8                    college or university work, and a total of four (4) years of such work experience, or of four (4) years of
 9                    college or university training and work experience combined, shall be accepted in lieu of college
10                    graduation. Any year of work experience above the apprenticeship level, which is not used for satisfying
11                    the college graduation requirement, shall be accepted in lieu of teaching experience provided such work
12                    experience shall have been directly related to the specific career technical field in which the person is
13                    assigned.

14             (6)    Part-time experience shall be credited for initial placement on the salary schedule and for annual service
15                    increments as follows:
16                    (a)     One full year of credit for regular full-time service of 120 days within a given school year;
17                    (b)     One-half year credit for regular full-time service between 60 and 119 days within a given school
18                            year;
19                    (c)     No credit shall be given for less than 60 regular full-time days of service;
20                    (d)     Annual service increments shall be given only at the beginning of a school year;
21                    (e)     Credit for one-half year of service shall carry forward until a full year of credit is earned and given
22                            on the schedule;
23                    (f)     Part-time teachers (those appointed for a fraction of the workday) shall receive experience credit on
24                            a pro rata basis.

25        b.   Increments

26             Salary increments become effective at the beginning of each contract year. Future increments are based upon the
27             completion of the appropriate number of days of prior service.

28             Annual advancements in salary shall be granted in accordance with the rates of increments specified in the salary
29             schedule until the proper maximum salary has been attained.

30             A teacher who has been employed full time and has received pay for at least one hundred twenty (120) days is
31             eligible for an annual increment at the beginning of the next school year.

32             For non-classroom teachers for whom there is not yet an evaluation instrument, those qualifying for the first time
33             for the following experience or longevity steps shall be required to obtain a satisfactory or better rating on a
34             performance evaluation completed during the first, third, and fifth year of employment and the year prior to the
35             effective date of the increments at steps 17, 22, and 27. A teacher shall be denied an increment due to a less than
36             satisfactory evaluation and has the right to challenge the evaluation through the grievance procedure. Further, such
37             teacher shall be re-evaluated during the next school year or the next evaluation cycle, whichever comes first. Upon
38             a satisfactory or better evaluation, the teacher shall be advanced on the salary schedule based on full credit for
39             his/her experience. A teacher who is placed in the Intervention process by the Peer Review Panel shall not receive
40             a longevity increment unless and until s/he completes the process with a satisfactory or better rating. No teacher
41             shall be denied a salary increment due to the administration’s failure to conduct a scheduled evaluation.

42        c.   Initial Position on New Salary Schedule

43             The initial salary of a teacher shall be the minimum on the schedule for which the teacher is qualified, plus any
44             allowance due the teacher for prior teaching experience and/or military service. Allowance for prior teaching
45             experience shall be made on the basis of:

46             (1)    All teachers in their first year of employment with the District and their first year of teaching beginning
47                    2000-01 will participate in the Teacher Evaluation System. The results of that evaluation will determine
48                    the teacher’s placement on the new salary schedule for the 2002-03 school year. All teachers in the first
49                    year of their teaching career will be placed at the apprentice level.



     69
                                                                                                §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1               (2)    Effective 2002-03 teachers new to the district, but with 2-5 years of successful experience will be placed at
 2                      the novice level on the new salary schedule. Teachers new to the district with more than five years of
 3                      successful experience will be placed at the career level on the new salary schedule. Teachers with six to
 4                      seven years of experience will be placed at career level, step 1 on the new salary schedule. Teachers with
 5                      more than seven years will be place at career level, step 2 on the new salary schedule.

 6               (3)    School nurses shall receive credit for each year of school nursing. That experience is credited the same as
 7                      prior teaching experience as defined in (2) above.

 8               (4)    In determining the initial salary of a teacher of trade and industrial vocational subjects, a year of work
 9                      experience, either at the apprenticeship level or beyond, shall be accepted as a substitute for a year of
10                      college or university work, and a total of four (4) years of such work experience, or of four (4) years of
11                      college or university training and work experience combined, shall be accepted in lieu of college
12                      graduation. Any year of work experience above the apprenticeship level, which is not used for satisfying
13                      the college graduation requirement, shall be accepted in lieu of teaching experience provided such work
14                      experience shall have been directly related to the specific vocational field in which the person is assigned.
15                      That experience is credited the same as prior teaching experience as defined in (2) above.

16               (5)    Part-time experience shall be credited for initial placement on the salary schedule and for annual service
17                      increments as follows:
18                      (a)     One full year of credit for regular full-time service of 120 days within a given school year;
19                      (b)     One-half year credit for regular full-time service between 60 and 119 days within a given school
20                              year;
21                      (c)     No credit shall be given for less than 60 regular full-time days of service;
22                      (d)     Annual service increments shall be given only at the beginning of a school year;
23                      (e)     Credit for one-half year of service shall carry forward until a full year of credit is earned and given
24                              on the schedule;
25                      (f)     Part-time teachers (those appointed for a fraction of the workday) shall receive experience credit
26                              on a pro rata basis.

27        d.     Movement through the Schedule

28               Salary increments become effective at the beginning of each contract year.

29               A teacher who has been employed full time and has received pay for at least one hundred twenty (120) days is
30               eligible for an annual increment at the beginning of the next school year.

31   3.   Provisions Applying to the Salary Schedules

32        a.     Appendix A

33               The salaries of teachers covered by this contract are set forth in Appendix A, which is attached hereto and made a
34               part of this contract. Teachers shall be placed at the appropriate step.

35               Personnel on yearlong Schedule E contracts will be paid quarterly. All others will be paid when contracts are
36               completed.

37        b.     Term of Service

38               All personnel included under this salary schedule have an annual term of service as per the teacher's individual
39               contract.

40        c.     Pay Plans

41               Twenty-six (26) checks delivered every other Friday year-round, beginning with the fourth Friday of the school
42               year, each for a uniform amount, except for the first pay of the year to be paid on the second Friday of the school
43               year which will be of non uniform amount; or

44               Twenty-one (21) checks delivered every other Friday from the opening of school through the end of school,
45               beginning with the fourth Friday of the school year, each for a uniform amount, except for the first pay of the year
46               to be paid on the second Friday of the school year which will be of non uniform amount.

                                                                                                                                    70
                                                                                                §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1               Deductions from paychecks shall be made, whenever possible, in uniform amounts. At the employee’s option,
 2               final paychecks of the 21-check plan shall be delivered to the teachers on the Friday that is at least one week
 3               following the last working day of the school year.

 4               The above pay plans shall not be construed so as to limit or restrict the board’s authority to establish and amend
 5               the school calendar or to open and close schools in accordance with state law.

 6        d.     Effect of State Mandates on Salary

 7               Any state mandated salary increase shall be part of, and shall not be in addition to, any salary increase resulting
 8               from the application of this Article.

 9        e.     Pay for Workshops

10               The Board shall develop a process in consultation with the CFT to expedite the payment for workshops and other
11               inservice activities so that participants are paid within 45 working days of the activity. The process shall include a
12               mechanism for partial payment for continuing programs that go beyond 45 working days.

13        f.     Emergency School Closings

14               In explanation of Board policy, where the Superintendent has authorized the closing of school due to an
15               emergency condition, an employee shall receive pay for such day where the employee would otherwise have been
16               in pay status, whether or not the employee has been reassigned to another location. Such pay shall not be charged
17               to any accrued leave. All bargaining unit members shall be treated the same on declared snow days.

18        g.     Montessori Teacher Training

19               As an exception to our present practice, teachers who have completed a Montessori training program at an
20               institution accredited by one or more of the recognized Montessori associations shall receive credit on the salary
21               schedule as if they had earned college credit for the training provided that the Board has accepted or would accept
22               such training as meeting the Board's training requirements for teaching in a Montessori magnet school.

23   4.   Medical, Prescription and Dental Coverage

24        a.     Medical and Prescription Plans

25               Employees electing medical coverage shall choose a Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) or a Point of
26               Service (POS) medical plan. Coverage shall be equivalent to or better than Humana of Ohio’s New Health HMO
27               and Co-Choice POS plans, respectively, as described in the attached plan designs, including prescription drug
28               coverage.

29        b.     Board Contributions

30               Upon application by the employee, the Board will purchase or provide single, two person or family coverage for
31               any employee appointed for six tenths (.6) time or more, less the dollar amount shown on the monthly employee
32               contribution schedule below, which shall be periodically deducted from the employee's paychecks.

33               For employees appointed for less than six-tenths (.6) time, the Board shall pay one-half (1/2) the cost of single,
34               two person or family coverage.

35        c.     Right to Opt-Out

36               An employee may decline medical coverage through the Board’s Plan. The Board my request proof of alternative
37               coverage. The Board shall pay an employee declining coverage under the Board’s Plan$50/month if eligible for
38               two-person coverage and $100/month if eligible for family coverage.

39        d.     Dental Plans

40               Employees shall also be eligible for dental coverage on the same basis as described above. Coverage shall be
41               equivalent to or better than Dental Care Plus DMO, as described in the attached plan design

                                                                                              §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1        g.   Right of Board to Change Carriers

 2             The Board may change the health (medical and/or dental) insurance carrier(s), or provide coverage through self-
 3             insurance, provided that:

 4             (1)    the resultant coverage(s) is at least equivalent to the coverage(s) as of July 1, 2007;

 5             (2)    the Board has given the Federation 60 days' notice of the proposed change and an opportunity to be
 6                    consulted about the proposed change;

 7             (3)    the Board has selected the new carrier(s) through solicitation of proposals, unless the change is to self-
 8                    insurance; and

 9             (4)    the joint Employee Benefits Committee has been given the opportunity to evaluate and make
10                    recommendations about the change.

11        h.   Eligibility for Coverage while on leave

12             Teachers shall not be eligible for coverage under the Board group plan unless part or all of the fee is payable by
13             the Board. However, the Board shall pay the full cost for one year of either a single or family health contract (if
14             eligible) less the employee contribution for any teacher placed on unpaid leave of absence due to personal illness
15             or maternity. Employees on such leave of absence for personal illness or maternity for an additional year(s), and
16             employees on other unpaid leaves of absence, shall have the option to continue coverage under the Board Group
17             Plan by paying the full monthly premium. Long-term substitutes shall become eligible for coverage effective the
18             first day of the month following 30 workdays of employment.

19        i.   COBRA Coverage

20             In accordance with the provisions of the various sections of 3923 O.R.C., as amended, and Public Law 99-272,
21             Title X (COBRA), as amended, the Board shall offer current and former employees continuation of Health,
22             Dental, and Prescription coverage in the event of change(s) in marital status, birth or adoption of a child, loss of
23             dependent status, death of the primary insured, or loss/reduction of job/hours.

24        j.   Medical Reimbursement Bank

25             The Board has established a plan under which a bookkeeping account (called herein a “reimbursement bank”) has
26             been established for each regular full-time employee and regular employee working one-half time or more. As of
27             January 1, 1990 the Board, subject to Appendix E (available separately), will credit $275 annually to the
28             reimbursement bank of each such employee who is both employed by the Board on such date and is only eligible
29             for single coverage under the Board's regular medical expense plan and $325 annually to the reimbursement bank
30             of each employee who both is employed by the Board on such date and is eligible for family coverage under the
31             Board's regular medical expense plan. Effective January 1, 2005, the Benefit Bank contribution will increase to
32             $325 (single) and $400 (family). Effective January 1, 2006, the reimbursement bank contribution will increase to
33             $350 (single) and $425 (family). All amounts credited to an employee's reimbursement bank may only be used
34             for reimbursement of the employee's medical, dental, vision, and hearing care expenses, including meeting
35             deductibles or co-pay amounts under the Board's other medical plans. Starting on January 1, 2008, over the
36             counter drugs will be eligible for reimbursement. However, employees may not be reimbursed from the medical
37             reimbursement bank for the monthly employee contribution to medical, prescription and dental coverage, which
38             are periodically deducted from their paychecks. Operation of such reimbursement banks will be in accordance
39             with and subject to Appendix E. Until actually paid, all reimbursement amounts will constitute general assets of
40             the Board and will not be held in trust or in any way segregated from the general assets of the Board. In order to
41             access these monies, starting on January 1, 2008, the employee must complete the Health Risk Assessment (HRA)
42             administered through the healthcare provider.

43        k.   Employee Assistance Program

44             The Board will continue to offer/provide an employee assistance program. The Employee Benefits Committee
45             shall adopt guidelines concerning the operation of the program.

46        l.   Employee Benefits Committee

47             (1)    Composition


     75
                                                                                       §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1               The Board and the Federation agree to continue the Employee Benefits Committee with representation
 2               from all unions, representing Board of Education employees. The committee shall include a minimum of
 3               two members from each bargaining unit with proportional representation among the bargaining units. The
 4               committee shall not be less than 15 or more than 19 in number. The Board shall also be represented on the
 5               Committee. Representatives on the committee may call for smaller caucuses of their choosing at any time
 6               during the meeting.

 7        (2)    The role of the Employee Benefits Committee is to:

 8               (a)    recommend needed benefit changes;

 9               (b)    research, analyze, and recommend benefit providers and changes;

10               (c)    communicate to and educate employees about utilization of benefits to promote cost containment
11                      and effective implementation of benefits; and

12               (d)    provide on-going monitoring of providers' performance and employee concerns.

13        (3)    The Employee Benefits Committee shall meet at least once monthly to review health care utilization and
14               plan for future design of the plan. No later than twelve months prior to the expiration of the Board’s
15               contract with the health care provider or administrator, the Committee shall meet and reveal the plan’s
16               utilization and cost. No less than six months prior to the expiration of the health care contract, said
17               Committee shall make recommendations to the bargaining units and the Board. Request for a proposal
18               shall be accepted no later than five months prior to the contract expiration with the Committee making a
19               recommendation to the parties as to the carrier, cost and design. Agreement on the carrier, plan design and
20               cost shall be reached no later than three months prior to expiration of the health care contract. Employees
21               on the Committee shall not suffer any loss of pay for reasonable hours of committee duty, which conflict
22               with the employee’s scheduled duty hours.

23        (4)    Adjustments to Benefits Bank

24               In April of each year a review shall be conducted to determine the Board’s total health care expenses for
25               the previous year. If the Board’s costs were less than $35,096,000, the difference between actual cost and
26               $35,096,000 shall be applied to increase the Benefit Bank. Increased amounts to the reimbursement bank
27               shall be implemented effective September 30 of that year. Any such adjustments shall be recommended
28               by the Benefits Committee and approved by the Superintendent’ and the Unions’ Leadership.

29   m.   Additional Voluntary Insurance Programs

30        No later than April 1, 2004, the Board will arrange to offer as voluntary programs group plans for home, auto,
31        long-term care and prepaid legal services payable 100% by employees.

32   n.   Term Life Insurance

33        Eligibility for the $30,000 term life insurance effective March 1. 1988 shall be extended to include teachers on an
34        annual salary basis appointed for one-half (1/2) time or more.

35   o.   Termination of Health Insurance

36        The Cincinnati Board of Education shall terminate health coverage immediately for each teacher who is absent
37        without authorized leave, but such coverage shall be reinstated immediately upon the teacher's return to work.
38        During the interim period of time between the start of a teacher's absence without authorized leave and the time
39        when the health care provider is able to terminate the health coverage for said teacher, the Cincinnati Board of
40        Education shall have the right to deduct from the teacher’s paycheck, the amount equal to the teacher's pro rata
41        share for health coverage for each day of unauthorized absence up to the time the termination becomes effective.
42        It is expressly understood that such termination of coverage shall continue for any period of time that the
43        Cincinnati Public Schools are closed due to a strike or work stoppage for each teacher who was absent without
44        authorized leave on the last working day immediately before the shutdown.

 1        p.   Tax Sheltered Annuity

 2             Embodying the benefits of Section 403(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 as amended, the Board may,
 3             upon authorization of the teacher, make annual salary deductions to be applied to the purchase of an annuity
 4             contract.

 5        q.   Pay Deductions Authorized By The Teacher

 6             (1)    Greater Cincinnati Public School Employee Credit Union
 7             (2)    Effective the conversion of Payroll to the ADP system, employees may elect direct deposit of payroll
 8                    checks to any financial institution meeting the requirements for electronic transfers standard to the banking
 9                    industry.
10             (3)    United States Savings Bonds

21        r.   Purchasing STRS or SERS Service Credit

22             District employees shall have the option of purchasing STRS and SERS credit on a pre-tax basis, as provided by
23             law.

24        s.   Conversion of Sick Leave at Retirement

25             Subject to the provisions of Section 124.39 of the Ohio Revised Code, a retiring employee hired before May 27th,
26             2004, shall be eligible to be paid for one-half (1/2) of his/her accrued but unused sick leave at the daily rate of pay
27             which is the teacher's salary divided by the number of days in the work year minus one day. A retiring employee
28             hired after May 26th, 2004 shall be paid for one-quarter (1/4) of his/her accrued but unused sick leave at the daily
29             rate of pay which is the teacher's salary divided by the number of days in the work year minus one day. Said
30             payment shall eliminate all sick leave accrued by the employee.

31             The daily rate of pay will be calculated by factoring in the teacher’s contract salary and any applicable career level
32             stipend, training increment, and lead teacher stipend and dividing by 190.

33             CFT and the Board recognize the obligation of sick leave payout to comply with applicable provisions of the
34             Internal Revenue Code and Regulations.

35             Payments of accrued sick leave to retiring employees shall be made to an employer sponsored 403(b) and 401(a)
36             plan, the terms of which shall be submitted to CFT for approval.

37             Accrued sick leave payments shall be made with respect to retiring employees, as follows:

38             First Payment: The maximum amount payable under the Internal Revenue Code and Regulations in the first year
39             of distribution of such benefits shall be paid in the first of the month following the cashing/receipt of the first
40             retirement payment by the employee, providing the Board is notified by the 20th of the month of the
41             cashing/receipt of such payment.

42             Subsequent Payments: The second payment, which shall be in an amount equal to the maximum amount allowed
43             under the Internal Revenue Code and Regulations, shall be made on the first Friday of January in the year
44             following the first payment. If any subsequent payments remain due, such payments shall be made the first Friday
45             of the following January.

46             The parties understand that the Internal Revenue Code and Regulations allow a maximum payment of no more
47             than $82,000 of accrued sick leave in year one and no more than $41,000 in year two or subsequent years. To the
48             extent that applicable Internal Revenue Code and Regulations change, then the Board shall make payments to
49             retiring employees consistent with such changes, distributing the maximum allowed by the Internal Revenue Code

     77
                                                                                          §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1         and Regulations in the year of retirement and in subsequent years in accordance with the schedule for payments in
 2         this section.

 3         An employee who notifies the Board officially by the early retirement date notification published annually that
 4         he/she plans to retire effective at the end of the school year shall receive an additional 5 days pay at the daily rate
 5         added to sick leave conversion in addition to their normal entitlement.

 6         Sick leave conversion shall be paid to survivors upon the death of an employee who has 10 years of service with
 7         the Board on the basis of one (1) day's pay for each two (2) days accumulated, unused sick leave. For those hired
 8         after May 22, 2004, sick leave conversion shall be paid to survivors upon the death of an employee who has 10
 9         years of service with the Board on the basis of one (1) day’s pay for each four (4) days accumulated, unused sick
10         leave.
11
12         If teachers do not qualify as part of the eligible or defined group in the Accumulated Leave Plan, the following
13         provision applies:

14        The Board shall make these payments to retiring staff as follows: One-half of the sick leave conversion the first of
15        the month following the cashing/receipt of the first retirement payment, providing the Board is notified by the 20th
16        of the month of the cashing/receipt. If the first half is paid between January 1 and June 30, then the second half
17        shall be paid the first Friday of the following January. If the first half is paid between July 1 and December 31, then
18        the second half shall be paid the first Friday of the following July.

19   t.    Mileage Reimbursement

20         Eligible teachers shall receive reimbursement at the rate permitted by the Internal Revenue Service for employee
21         business expenses when their automobiles are used for Board business.

22         Teachers eligible to receive mileage reimbursement shall be those who report to more than one (1) location on any
23         school day to perform assigned duties. Reimbursement shall be made by the Treasurer's Office after receiving the
24         Mileage Report Form signed by the teacher and approved by the school administrator to whom the teacher reports.

25   u.    Damage to Personal Property

26         The Board shall provide reimbursement for damage to a teacher's personal property excluding cash resulting from
27         an assault, which occurred in the course of employment or, from vandalism or theft on the school site or at another
28         location while on school business. The Board shall establish an annual fund of $10,000 to pay claims under this
29         provision. The fund will provide reimbursement to teachers only to the extent that the teacher does not have
30         insurance coverage protecting against such damage. When the fund is exhausted, the Board shall have no further
31         obligation to pay such claims. The Board and CFT will agree on guidelines concerning the payment of expenses
32         from this fund. The plan shall have a $100 deductible after private insurance coverage has been exhausted. The
33         employee pays the first hundred dollars of loss, except in cases of loss due to an assault by a student.

34   v.    Holidays and Holiday Pay

35         In explanation of Board policy, any employee absent without pay on either his/her next scheduled workday
36         preceding a holiday or his/her next scheduled workday following a holiday shall be allowed no pay for the
37         holiday; however, if an employee was sick and had exhausted earned sick leave, and had worked up to 5 working
38         days of a holiday, and reported to work within 5 days after the holiday, the employee, upon approval by the
39         Board, shall be allowed pay for the holiday.

40   w.    Retirement “Pick-up”

41         The Board shall designate each employee's mandatory contribution to the STRS of Ohio as “picked-up” by the
42         Board as contemplated by IRS Revenue Rulings 77-462 and 81-36 (although they shall continue to be designated
43         as employee contribution as permitted by OAG Opinion 82-097) in order that the amount of the employee's
44         income reported by the Board as subject to Federal and Ohio income taxes shall be the employee's total gross
45         income reduced by the then current percentage amount of the employee's mandatory STRS contribution which has
46         been designated as “picked-up” by the Board. The amount designated as “picked-up” by the Board shall be
47         included in computing the final average salary for retirement purposes, provided that no employee's total gross
48         income is increased by such “pick-up” nor is the Board's total contribution to the STRS of Ohio increased thereby.
49         The amount designated as “picked-up” by the Board shall be included in computing the employee's daily rate for
50         the purpose of sick leave conversion upon retirement.



                                                                                                                               78
                                                                                                   §700 Salaries and Fringe Benefits
 1          x.     Adoption Assistance Program

 2                 Upon application by the teacher, the Board will reimburse up to $2,000 of required expenses incurred by the
 3                 employee in the placement and adoption of a dependent minor child. Such expenses may include:

 4                 Payments will be made as follows:

 5                 (i)     Payments will be made within 30 days after the child is placed in the adoptive family's home, (the date the
 6                         child becomes a member of the household, not the date of final adoption which usually comes later) and
 7                         evidence of eligible expenses paid has been submitted to the Board.

 8                 (ii)    In cases of multiple adoptions, the adoption of each child would be considered separate. A maximum of
 9                         $3,000 will be payable to any one family within a twelve month period.

10          y.     Tuition Waivers for CPS

11                 For teachers who live outside the school district who wish to enroll their children in CPS, tuition waivers shall be
12                 granted, provided the current Ohio State Statutes permit State aid to be received for the student. The same
13                 enrollment and application procedures, including deadlines, as those applied to other non–resident pupils shall be
14                 in effect.
15   §800                                                                                                       BOARD AUTHORITY

16   1.     Board Authority Granted by State Law

17          It is recognized by the parties that the Board is invested by the laws of the State of Ohio with the government and control
18          of all of the Cincinnati Public Schools. This authority of the Board shall include, but shall not be limited to, the authority
19          to make such rules, regulations and policies as are necessary for the government of the public schools, the employees of
20          the Board, and the pupils of the schools. Nothing in this contract shall constitute transfer of the authority of the Board as
21          established by the laws of the State of Ohio.

22   2.     Implementation of Board Authority

23          The administrative authority of the Board shall be implemented by the Superintendent and his/her designees whose
24          authority shall include, but not be limited to, the authority to direct and assign teachers and to carry out such other duties
25          as the Board determines as provided by the Ohio Revised Code.

26   3.     Exclusion of Board Policies and Practices from Contract

27          Policies and practices of the Board and the administration are not a part of this contract, except as stated herein, and may
28          be adopted, revised, amended, suspended or rescinded at the discretion of the Board or the administration.
29   §810                                                                                                               AMENDMENT

30   1.     Necessity to Renegotiate

31          This contract may be amended by mutual written agreement of the Board and the Federation. Nevertheless, the parties
32          acknowledge that during the negotiations, which resulted in this contract, each had the unlimited right and opportunity to
33          make demands and proposals, and that the understandings and agreements arrived at by the parties after the exercise of
34          that right and opportunity are set forth in this contract.

35          Therefore, for the life of this contract, each party agrees that the other shall not be obligated to negotiate with respect to
36          any subject matter not specifically referred to or covered in this contract.
     §820                                                                                                                   LEGALITY

     1.     Conflict with Law

            If any provision of this contract or any application of this contract to any teacher or group of teachers is contrary to law,
            then such provision or application shall not be deemed valid except to the extent permitted by law, but all other provisions
            or applications shall continue in full force and effect.
